Lake St. Louis is a private-lake community in western St. Charles County, and its food scene clusters at The Meadows — an open-air shopping district that mixes national anchors like Von Maur with a genuinely strong bench of homegrown spots. Add a craft distillery-meadery and a from-scratch Italian bistro on Highway N, and you can build a whole day here without touching a chain.
From a chef-driven New American kitchen to a distillery that makes beer, bourbon, and mead, here's where to eat in Lake St. Louis.
Most of the independents cluster in The Meadows at Lake St. Louis (Meadows Circle Drive, off Lake St. Louis Blvd / Hwy 40-64), with a couple on Highway N (63367). Watch the town line — Lake St. Louis blends into Wentzville, O'Fallon, and Dardenne Prairie (63368), so a lot of "Lake St. Louis" lists pull in spots that aren't. We've kept to verified 63367.

### BC's Kitchen
The standout. BC's Kitchen is the chef-driven New American room most consistently named the area's best sit-down independent — seasonal, local-ingredient cooking like an andouille-chicken-shrimp gumbo with cornbread, in a wine-list-and-craft-cocktail setting rather than a sports bar.
📍 11 Meadows Circle Dr, Suite 400, Lake St. Louis, MO 63367

### Cugino's Craft Kitchen
Cugino's is the family's craft kitchen (the original is in Florissant; this is the Meadows location) — award-winning blackened chicken nachos, house meatballs, in-house-cured pastrami, and tagliatelle Bolognese. Family-owned since 2004.
📍 10 Meadow Cir Dr, Suite 116, Lake St. Louis, MO 63367

### Donatelli's Bistro
Donatelli's is the from-scratch Italian bistro on Highway N where dinner comes with a singer, not a TV — live music Wednesday through Saturday, a full martini and wine program, and monthly high-end wine dinners.
📍 8653 Hwy N, Lake St. Louis, MO 63367

### Burnt Barrel Brewery, Distillery & Meadery
Burnt Barrel is a Missouri craft spot making beer, honey-wine (mead), and spirits under one roof — taste a mead flight next to a bourbon they distilled themselves, with crispy fried mushrooms, a signature soft pretzel, and toasted ravioli. Order food at the bar. Thu–Sun.
📍 730 Lakeside Plaza, Lake St. Louis, MO 63367

### Fuego Tex-Mex Bar & Grill
Fuego ("fire") is the 2026 newcomer that took over the former Prados suite — fire-grilled Tex-Mex with chicken mole enchiladas, quesabirria tacos, and house-made salsas from an independent operator. Fresh and new; hours may still be settling.
📍 21 Meadow Cir Dr, Suite 326, Lake St. Louis, MO 63367

### Southern Grace Coffee
Southern Grace is the genuinely local independent coffee shop that's become The Meadows' community living room — artisanal espresso and Southern-inspired café fare and hospitality, surrounded by national logos.
📍 20 Meadows Circle Dr, Suite 216, Lake St. Louis, MO 63367

### Hygge
Hygge — named for the Danish idea of cozy contentment — is the healthy café and juice bar sourcing from local farmers: açaí bowls, pressed juices and immunity boosters, smoothies, and coffee. The "cozy, healthy, happy place" of the district.
📍 21 Meadow Cir Dr, Suite 325, Lake St. Louis, MO 63367

What's the best restaurant in Lake St. Louis, MO?
BC's Kitchen — a chef-driven, seasonal New American room (its gumbo is a local signature) that's the most consistently named best sit-down independent in the area. Cugino's and Donatelli's round out the top.
What is The Meadows at Lake St. Louis?
An open-air shopping district off Lake St. Louis Blvd that mixes national anchors (Von Maur) with homegrown food — Cugino's, BC's Kitchen, Fuego, Southern Grace Coffee, and Hygge are all there, walkable in one trip.
Are some "Lake St. Louis" restaurants actually in other towns?

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
Here's a thing most St. Louisans don't know, even ones who've lived here their whole lives: about twenty-five minutes east, in a little Illinois college town called Lebanon, there's a red-brick main street so well-preserved that Charles Dickens stayed the night there in 1842 and wrote it up afterward, praising the local inn for cleanliness and comfort that would shame any village alehouse back in England.
That inn — the Mermaid House, built in 1830 by a retired sea captain who swore he'd seen mermaids — still stands on St. Louis Street. And the brick street around it, anchored by McKendree University (the oldest college in Illinois), has quietly become one of the more charming places to eat in the whole Metro East. It's a small scene, and an honest guide has to admit a few good spots have closed recently — but the survivors are worth the drive. Here's where to eat in Lebanon.

### The Gasthaus
Lebanon's German bones show at The Gasthaus , a German-American bar and grill on the brick street where schnitzel, bratwurst, and proper potato salad share a menu with burgers, steaks, and seafood. Locals point to the seafood chowder and the shrimp and grits with Andouille — and there's a roomy, dog-friendly patio for when the weather cooperates.
📍 115 W St. Louis St, Lebanon, IL 62254

### The Lantern BLE
For breakfast and lunch, The Lantern is the home-cooked heart of downtown — biscuits and gravy, peaches-and-cream French toast, and "famous" meatball subs, with a rotating seasonal menu that keeps regulars checking back. It's the kind of place that fills up with students and locals both.
📍 222 W St. Louis St, Lebanon, IL 62254

### St. Louis Coffee World
One of Lebanon's best surprises: St. Louis Coffee World moved to the brick street in late 2024 and brought something you won't find at any chain — espresso and signature lattes plus a full Filipino menu. Think ube cheese pandesal, crispy lumpia, and leche flan alongside a Peanut Butter Tiramisu latte, all inside a historic exposed-brick storefront.
📍 125 W St. Louis St, Lebanon, IL 62254

### Smitty's Pizzeria
Newer to the downtown strip, Smitty's hand-tosses its pizzas and earns its reviews on the crust and the fresh parmesan. Heads up on the hours — it runs Thursday through Sunday only — so plan your pizza night accordingly.
📍 122 E St. Louis St, Suite B, Lebanon, IL 62254

### Mexico Tipico
Just off the brick street on the Madison corridor, Mexico Tipico is the full-service Mexican spot — burritos, enchiladas, Caldo del Mar, Pollo Jalisco, Steak Ranchero — with dine-in, takeout, curbside, and delivery all on the table. The dependable, sit-down south-of-the-border option in town.
📍 501 S Madison St, Lebanon, IL 62254

### Creekside Bar and Grill
Over on the west side, Creekside Bar and Grill is the neighborhood sports-bar play — burgers, wings, pizzas, and a full bar with craft beer and cocktails. When you want a game on and a basket of wings, this is the room.
📍 800 W McAllister St, Lebanon, IL 62254

### A town that earns the trip
Lebanon is small, and it's honest to say its food scene runs tight — a few longtime spots have closed in the last year, which is exactly why supporting the survivors matters. But few towns this size offer this much atmosphere : the preserved brick of St. Louis Street , the 1830 Mermaid House with its Dickens connection, and McKendree University keeping the place young. Come the first Saturday in October, the Lebanon Fall Festival fills the brick street with 100-plus vendors and food stands — kettle corn, caramel apples, funnel cakes, homemade bread — for a 50-year-running tradition.
That kind of place is precisely what gets lost on the big national apps, and precisely what a hyper-local directory is built to surface. Search St Louis Near Me Directory for Lebanon and the Metro East before you head over. Exploring more of the Illinois side? The Riverbend county seat of Jerseyville up in Jersey County is another genuine find.
And if you run a spot on the brick street — or want to — getting listed is how the next carful of visitors (or the next hungry McKendree student) finds you.

### FAQ
Is Lebanon, IL worth visiting for food?
For the combination, yes — a handful of genuinely good independents (German fare, Filipino-fusion coffee, hand-tossed pizza, real Mexican) set against one of the best-preserved historic brick main streets in the Metro East.
What's the story with Charles Dickens and Lebanon?
Dickens stayed at the Mermaid House Hotel on St. Louis Street in 1842 and praised it in his travel book American Notes . The 1830 building still stands and is on the National Register of Historic Places.
Are Lebanon's restaurants open every day?
Not all — Smitty's Pizzeria runs Thursday through Sunday only, and a few spots close one weekday. The town has seen some turnover recently, so it's worth a quick call before driving over.
When is the Lebanon Fall Festival?
The first Saturday in October, on the downtown brick street — a 50-plus-year tradition with 100+ vendors and plenty of festival food.

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
Livingston is a village of about 800 in northeastern Madison County, tucked off I-55 Exit 37 with old Route 66 running right through it — and home to one of the most photographed roadside attractions on the Illinois Mother Road, the giant Pink Elephant. Its in-town dining is exactly two spots: a Route 66 diner in a giant ice-cream-cone building and a local tavern. People in Livingston get hungry too — here are the real ones, plus the closest favorites a few minutes up the road.
From never-frozen charbroiled burgers under a pink elephant to Friday catfish nearby, here's where to eat in Livingston.
Livingston's two spots are on Veterans Memorial Dr and Livingston Ave (62058), right by I-55 Exit 37. Hours vary by season (the diner) and the tavern keeps late bar hours — call ahead. For more, Worden is ~6 minutes south and Staunton ~7 minutes north on old Route 66.

### Twistee Treat Diner at the Pink Elephant
The Route 66 landmark — a 1950s-themed diner inside an actual giant ice-cream-cone building with a hot-pink tile floor, attached to the Pink Elephant Antique Mall (a 30,000-sq-ft former 1929 high school guarded by a giant pink elephant). Charbroiled burgers made with fresh local beef that's never frozen, plus a big hand-scooped and soft-serve ice-cream menu. Family-run since 2015.
📍 908 Veterans Memorial Dr, Livingston, IL 62058

### Bonnie & Klides Bar & Grill
The town's after-dark gathering spot — a true small-town tavern right off I-55 where reviewers single out the steaks, with bar food and a full bar, friendly bartenders, and hands-on owners. Open very late (1 a.m. weeknights, 2 a.m. weekends); confirm kitchen hours separately.
📍 595 Livingston Ave, Livingston, IL 62058

### Closest favorites a few minutes away
Livingston is small, so locals drift up and down I-55 / Route 66 — these are fresh picks worth the short drive:
- Worden (~6 mi south): The Rustic Tavern & Grill (Philly cheesesteaks, live music) and Yellow Dog Cafe & Bar (Friday catfish big enough to split; cash or check only).
- Staunton (~7 mi north): Cavataio's Restaurant & Pizzeria (family Italian since 1988) and DeCamp Station (a historic Route 66 roadhouse — weekends only, and listed for sale, so call first).

### Why this town matters
Livingston is a tiny Route 66 town whose whole dining identity is roadside-traveler culture — a diner in a giant cone building next to a pink elephant, and a tavern off the interstate. That's exactly the forgotten-Mother-Road charm nobody else writes up. We map it, then point you to Worden and Staunton for more.

### FAQ
Is there anywhere to eat in Livingston, IL?
Yes — two spots: the Twistee Treat Diner at the Pink Elephant (Route 66 landmark, charbroiled burgers and ice cream) and Bonnie & Klides Bar & Grill (a local tavern known for steaks). For more, it's a 5–7 minute drive to Worden or Staunton.
What's the Pink Elephant in Livingston?
The Pink Elephant Antique Mall — a 30,000-sq-ft former 1929 high school marked by a giant pink elephant statue, one of the most photographed roadside attractions on Illinois Route 66. The Twistee Treat Diner (in a giant cone-shaped building) sits right there.
Where do locals go nearby for dinner?
Worden (Rustic Tavern, Yellow Dog Cafe's Friday catfish) for casual, and Staunton (Cavataio's for Italian, DeCamp Station for a Route 66 experience) for a destination meal — all a few minutes away.

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
Madison is a small (~2,400-person) industrial river town between Granite City and Venice, anchored by the McKinley Bridge into St. Louis and World Wide Technology Raceway. Its in-town dining is thin and honest about it — but it has one nearly-century-old fish-house landmark worth crossing the river for, plus a couple of neighborhood bar and grills. People in Madison get hungry too — here's the real local food, plus where to go next door.
From a cash-only fried cod sandwich on cream bread to soul food a mile away, here's where to eat in Madison.
Madison's in-limits independents are on Madison Ave and State St (62060). The standout is cash-only and runs limited days; the bars keep tavern hours — call ahead. ZIP/wrong-town traps abound: "Mack's Irish Pub" results are Madison, Wisconsin ; Jerry's Cafeteria and Ernie & Annie's are Granite City. For a fuller meal, Venice (next door), Granite City, and Pontoon Beach are minutes away.

### Marko's Fish House
The gem. A nearly century-old, multi-generational family fish house — and the reason to come. The fried cod sandwich is golden and generous on soft bakery-style Italian cream bread with homemade tartar, banana peppers, onions, and pickles. Cash only, a Lenten-Friday institution: open Tue–Fri, closed weekends and Monday. A 4.8-star, taste-of-childhood spot.
📍 820 Madison Ave, Madison, IL 62060

### McGee's Bar & Grill
A long-standing neighborhood tavern (around 19 years) listed for bar-and-grill and barbecue fare, open late into the bar-close hours. A genuine local watering hole — call ahead to confirm the kitchen.
📍 1112 State St, Madison, IL 62060

### Angelo's Bar and Grill
A newer, laid-back late-night spot with pool, darts, and front-and-back bars — more tavern than kitchen, but a real neighborhood hang on Madison Ave. Confirm food hours before you go.
📍 1348 Madison Ave, Madison, IL 62060

### Closest spots a short drive away
Madison is small, so the neighbors fill it out:
- Niddy's Kitchen — next door in Venice — a Black-owned soul-food kitchen where the catfish is the order (see our Venice guide).
- For Mexican and fuller sit-down meals, Granite City and Pontoon Beach are minutes away with their own guides.

Madison is industrial and small, and we say so — but a nearly-century-old family fish house making one of the area's great cod sandwiches is exactly the kind of landmark worth the McKinley Bridge crossing. World Wide Technology Raceway sits in Madison, but has little on-site sit-down dining — Marko's Fish House (about half a mile) is the closest genuine local independent. Most other "near the track" spots are actually in Granite City.

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
Part of West County — explore the whole region in our West County restaurant guide .
Manchester runs right along its namesake road, and that corridor hides a deeper food bench than a West County drive-through would suggest — a 1982 steakhouse, a pancake house that opens at 6 a.m., a fish-and-game grill with walleye, and a tucked-away row of Thai, sushi, and Indian. The catch is the city line: Manchester Road is a boundary, so Google and Yelp constantly mislabel genuine Manchester spots as "Ballwin." We went by the city's own directory.
From a 40-year steakhouse to a walleye-and-frog-legs grill, here's where to eat in Manchester.
Most of Manchester's independents sit along Manchester Road and Big Bend (63011/63021), several tucked into plazas like Lafayette Center and Nationalway. Because the road is a city line, don't be thrown when an app says "Ballwin" — the spots below are confirmed Manchester. A couple are local family groups, labeled honestly.

### Tucker's Place
Tucker's Place has been grilling hand-cut steaks here since 1982 — a dim-lit, no-frills neighborhood steakhouse (part of a small local St. Louis group) where the porterhouse, not the decor, is the point. Closed Sundays, which tells you it's run like a neighborhood place.
📍 14282 Manchester Rd, Manchester, MO 63011

### Uncle Bill's Pancake & Dinner House
Uncle Bill's is the West County outpost of the longtime St. Louis pancake original — open at 6 a.m. seven days a week, Belgian waffles and omelets and corned beef hash, coffee that keeps coming, breakfast served all day. The old-school morning anchor.
📍 14196 Manchester Rd, Manchester, MO 63011

### Lazy River Grill
Lazy River Grill is the independent American grill where the walls are a working outdoor museum of fishing, hunting, and camping gear — and the dish regulars drive in for is the in-house-breaded walleye, with frog legs on the side. A genuine West County original.
📍 631 Big Bend Rd, Manchester, MO 63021

### Manee Thai
Manee Thai has been family-owned in West County since 2009 — from-scratch curries (Panang, Masaman, pineapple), sauces made daily, and a patio when the weather turns. An award-winning neighborhood Thai kitchen, not a franchise.
📍 481 Lafayette Center, Manchester, MO 63011

### Sushi Ai
Sushi Ai is the small, locally owned sushi and hibachi bar tucked into the Lafayette Center plaza — one location, recently renovated, no chain behind it. Rolls, hibachi entrees, and udon done right.
📍 471 Lafayette Center, Manchester, MO 63011

### Joey B's Food & Drink
Joey B's (part of the St. Louis Gianino family group) has one of the biggest outdoor bars and patios in West County — award-nominated wings, Fried Chicken Tuesday, burgers, and a bottomless weekend brunch. The warm-weather corridor gathering spot.
📍 14445 Manchester Rd, Manchester, MO 63011

### Cheers Bar & Grill
Cheers Bar & Grill is the genuine neighborhood watering hole — breakfast plates and biscuits-and-gravy in the morning, bar-and-grill fare until 1 a.m., pool and a regulars' crowd. Recently reopened in a new Manchester location.
📍 61 Nationalway Shopping Center, Manchester, MO 63011

Why do Manchester restaurants show up as "Ballwin"?
Manchester Road is a municipal boundary, so Google and Yelp routinely tag genuine Manchester spots (Tucker's, Uncle Bill's, Sushi Ai, Joey B's) as "Ballwin." The city's own business directory confirms they're inside Manchester.
Where's the best breakfast in Manchester?

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
Part of St. Louis County — explore the whole region in our St. Louis County restaurant guide .
Maplewood is the little inner-ring town that turned two streets into one of the best independent food-and-drink strips in St. Louis. Park once on Manchester or Sutton and you can walk from a whole-animal butcher's lunch counter to a nationally famous brewery to a 30-seat chef's tasting room. Almost none of it is a chain — which is exactly why people drive in from across the region.
From a barrel-aged beer legend to a duck-fat-fries butcher shop, here's where to eat in Maplewood.
Nearly everything clusters along Manchester Road and Sutton Boulevard (63143), so it's a true park-once-and-walk strip — and a designated Green Dining District, with a lot of local sourcing. A couple of spots are daytime-only or closed Mondays/Tuesdays. One honest note: the old Boardwalk ice cream shop has closed, so don't come chasing it.

### Side Project Brewing
Side Project is one of the most award-decorated breweries in the entire country, sitting on a quiet Maplewood corner — barrel-aged and farmhouse ales that beer fans drive in from across the Midwest to chase, with food from their on-site mobile kitchen. (Sister spots nearby: Side Project Cellar and Side Project Pizza.)
📍 7458 Manchester Rd, Maplewood, MO 63143

### Schlafly Bottleworks
Schlafly Bottleworks is the brewpub arm of St. Louis's original craft brewery — house beers on tap plus a full kitchen of beer-cheese soup, wings, and tacos, served at long communal tables. Maplewood's de facto town square for a pint. Open daily.
📍 7260 Southwest Ave, Maplewood, MO 63143

### Bolyard's Meat & Provisions
Bolyard's is billed as St. Louis's only whole-animal butcher — and you can eat a sandwich and a cone of beef-tallow fries on the patio while they break down pasture-raised hogs in the open cutting room. House sausages, broths, weekend breakfast sandwiches.
📍 2733 Sutton Blvd, Maplewood, MO 63143

### Robin Restaurant
Robin is the tiny 30-seat room where chef Alec Schingel plates a seasonal “fine comfort” tasting menu — elevated Midwestern dinner-party food (think hot dish and pork schnitzel) that reads indulgent but eats like home. Reservations recommended.
📍 7268 Manchester Rd, Maplewood, MO 63143

### The Blue Duck
The Blue Duck is the New American smokehouse where they cure, smoke, and pickle in-house — BBQ burnt ends with pickled red onion, bacon-fat hand-cut fries, and a smoked-meat brunch. They even wash a rye whiskey in duck fat for a house cocktail.
📍 2661 Sutton Blvd, Maplewood, MO 63143

### Sabroso Cocina Mexicana
Sabroso is chef Miguel Pintor's traditional Mexican kitchen — the move is the cochinita pibil, Yucatán pork slow-roasted four to five hours until it falls apart, with pickled habanero onions that bite back. The real-deal Mexican on Sutton.
📍 2726 Sutton Blvd, Maplewood, MO 63143

### The Crow's Nest
The Crow's Nest is the dim, horror-movie-decorated gastropub with a metal soundtrack — pork poutine, cheese curds, a heavy-metal “Metal Brunch,” and a kitchen that runs late into the night. The fun, loud one.
📍 7336 Manchester Rd, Maplewood, MO 63143

### Living Room Coffee & Kitchen
Living Room is the family-owned café and in-house coffee roaster — fresh-roasted coffee, scratch breakfast and lunch, a bakery case, wooden tables, and a patio. The neighborhood morning anchor.
📍 2810 Sutton Blvd, Maplewood, MO 63143

### Why this town matters
Maplewood proves what an independent strip can be — a butcher, a tasting-menu room, a national-name brewery, and a Mexican kitchen, all walkable on two streets, all locally owned. It's regularly named one of St. Louis's best indie food neighborhoods, and the chain apps barely register it. We map the whole strip.

### FAQ
What's the best restaurant in Maplewood, MO?
Depends on the night: Robin for a chef's tasting menu, The Blue Duck for smokehouse New American, Sabroso for traditional Mexican. For the marquee name, Side Project Brewing is a nationally awarded destination.
Is Maplewood walkable for food and drink?
Very — almost everything sits along Manchester Road and Sutton Boulevard, so you can park once and walk between a butcher-shop lunch, a brewery, and a scratch-kitchen dinner.
Does Maplewood have a distillery?
No — that's a common mix-up. Maplewood's craft-spirits identity is its breweries (Side Project, Schlafly); StilL 630 is a downtown St. Louis distillery, and a similarly named “Maplewood” distillery is actually in Chicago.
Where's the best coffee in Maplewood?
Living Room Coffee & Kitchen on Sutton roasts its own beans and does a scratch breakfast and lunch — the neighborhood morning spot.

### Plan your Maplewood visit
Coffee at Living Room, a butcher-counter lunch at Bolyard's, a pint at Side Project, and a smokehouse dinner at The Blue Duck — all on foot. For more local spots across the metro, explore St Louis Near Me Directory .

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
Marine is a tiny Madison County village of about 900 people, and its food scene is exactly that size — and that's part of the small-town charm. There's no pretending it's a dining destination, but people in Marine get hungry too, and when you want a bite right here, there are three genuinely local spots, all within a couple of blocks of each other in the village center: a flat-top diner with an ice cream window, a 60-year family tavern, and a scratch-cooking restaurant in the old café building.
From fresh-griddled Frisco burgers to a 60-year biker tavern, here's where to eat in Marine.
All three sit within two blocks in the village center on/near Duncan St and Division St (62061). Hours are small-town tight — call ahead, and know the diner is closed Sun/Mon and the catering-focused spot keeps limited dine-in hours. For more variety, Highland is about 7 miles east and Edwardsville about 12 west.

### The Marine Diner
The Marine Diner is the locally owned flat-top diner and burger joint that took over the old Millie's Diner building — fresh-griddled cheeseburgers (including the Frisco Burger), corn dogs, rotating daily specials (Wednesday taco salads, Thursday pork steaks, Friday fish), and an ice cream window for after. Closed Sun/Mon.
📍 302 W Division St, Marine, IL 62061

### Phyl's Chet & Rose's Tavern
Phyl's is a 60-plus-year family tavern — grilled cheeseburgers, wings, wraps, a Friday fried-fish special, and tacos on the last Sunday of the month. A known stop for bikers and Harley riders, with karaoke nights. The small-town bar where everyone seems to know each other.
📍 204 N Duncan St, Marine, IL 62061

### The Food Dude Restaurant & Catering
The Food Dude moved into the old Parkview Café building and turned the village's longtime breakfast corner into a scratch-cooking comfort-food spot — chicken Parmesan with skin-on mashed potatoes, house chicken salad, creamy pastas, made-from-scratch desserts. Primarily catering and food-truck, with limited evening dine-in (Wed–Sun) — confirm before you go.
📍 330 N Duncan St, Marine, IL 62061

### Why this town matters
Marine is a 900-person village, and three genuinely local spots — a flat-top diner, a 60-year tavern, a scratch kitchen — is exactly right for a town this size. That's not a shortfall; it's the small-town Madison County charm. We map what's really here, and point you to Highland and Edwardsville when you want more.

What's the must-try local spot in Marine, IL?
The two anchors are The Marine Diner (fresh cheeseburgers, daily specials, ice cream window) and Phyl's Chet & Rose's Tavern, a 60-plus-year family tavern famous for its Friday fish and biker-friendly vibe.
Is there much to eat in Marine itself?
Honestly, no — Marine is a small rural village of about 900, so you're looking at roughly three independent spots plus a Casey's gas-station pizza counter. That's normal for a town this size, and it's the charm.

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
Marthasville is a tiny Warren County town — barely a thousand people — but it sits in a sweet spot: right on the Katy Trail at mile marker 77, in the heart of Missouri wine country, a short ride from where Daniel Boone was first buried. It's not a town with a long restaurant row. It's a town where cyclists roll in hungry, day-trippers wander through, and locals know the handful of spots that are genuinely worth a stop.
When you're out here and ready to eat, here's what's close — in town and just up the road in wine country.
Marthasville is small, so plan a little: a couple of these keep limited or weekend hours, and one trailside café's status can flip seasonally (call ahead). The town sits on the Katy Trail , minutes from the Daniel Boone Monument and original burial site and a short drive from the Augusta/Dutzow wineries — so it's easy to build a half-day around a single meal here.

### Philly's Pizza
The in-town anchor. Philly's Pizza is the locally owned pizzeria right on the Katy Trail — pizza, pasta, salads, and wings, with a Chicago-style deep dish as the signature (first topping's free). Delivery, takeout, and outdoor seating make it the easy refuel after a ride.
📍 207 Depot St, Marthasville, MO 63357

### Cori's Twin Gables Bar & Grill
Cori's Twin Gables is the family-owned, home-cooking bar and grill a few minutes' walk from the trail — burgers, a praised steak sandwich, calamari, daily specials, and a full bar, with live music every weekend . The community hangout where the town actually gathers.
📍 101 MO-47, Marthasville, MO 63357

### KT Caboose
The most charming stop in town — if it's open. KT Caboose is a healthy, plant-leaning café set inside a vintage 1960s train car right on the Katy Trail: avocado toast, veggie burgers, parfaits, and ice cream, plus $10 tent camping for trail riders (shower and ice cream included). It's a seasonal, weekend-ish operation whose hours can change, so call before you count on it — but when it's running, it's pure Katy Trail magic.
📍 600 Depot St, Marthasville, MO 63357

### Lake Creek Winery
For a sit-down meal with a view, Lake Creek Winery has a full-service restaurant in a restored 1860s farmhouse on the Missouri River bluffs — German-leaning plates, a chef's charcuterie board, Missouri wines, and live music, with a deck, patio, and pavilion over a 24-acre lake. It's just outside the town center and worth the few-minute drive.
📍 15088 Boone Monument Rd, Marthasville, MO 63357

### Make a day of it: Blumenhof in nearby Dutzow
Three or four miles west in the historic German village of Dutzow , Blumenhof Winery is one of Missouri's most-awarded family wineries — a tasting room with a big patio, free weekend live music, and a Brat Haus grill on weekends. It's a different town, but it's the natural "extend your wine-country afternoon" stop from Marthasville.
📍 13699 S Hwy 94, Dutzow, MO 63342

### Why this little town matters
Marthasville is exactly the kind of place the big sites skip — too small to register — but it's a genuine Katy Trail and wine-country gem, sitting where Daniel Boone spent his last years and was first laid to rest. The honest truth is it's a handful of spots, not a dozen: a deep-dish pizzeria, a family bar with weekend bands, a café in a train car, and a bluff-top winery restaurant. For a cyclist or a day-tripper, that's everything you need to know.

### FAQ
Is there food right on the Katy Trail in Marthasville?
Yes — Philly's Pizza (deep-dish, on the trail at Depot St) and, when it's open, KT Caboose (a plant-leaning café inside a vintage train car, with $10 trail camping). Cori's Twin Gables is a short walk away.
Where can I eat with a wine-country view near Marthasville?
Lake Creek Winery, just outside town, has a full restaurant in a restored 1860s farmhouse on the bluffs. Blumenhof Winery in nearby Dutzow adds a weekend Brat Haus grill.
Is Marthasville a big restaurant town?
No — it's a small Katy Trail town of about a thousand people. The handful of spots here are genuine and local, perfect for cyclists and day-trippers, with more wine-country dining a short drive away.
What's the Daniel Boone connection?
Daniel Boone spent his last years in this area and was originally buried near Marthasville; the Daniel Boone Monument and original burial site are minutes from the Katy Trail.

### Plan your Marthasville visit
Deep dish at Philly's, a burger and a band at Cori's, and a glass on the bluff at Lake Creek — with Blumenhof in Dutzow to extend the day. For more local spots across Warren County and the St. Louis metro, explore St Louis Near Me Directory .

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
Part of North County — explore the whole region in our North County restaurant guide .
Maryland Heights has two food worlds. There's Westport Plaza — a genuine walkable dining-and-entertainment hub off I-270 with hibachi, the original Drunken Fish sushi, and a brand-new wood-fired Italian room. And there's the Dorsett Road corridor, where the workaday locals live: a 20-year family taqueria, a deep-menu Thai kitchen, a char-grill counter, and a Gioia's hot-salami walk-up window. Plus a lakeside bar and grill right on the Creve Coeur Park trail.
From a tableside hibachi show to a century-old hot salami, here's where to eat in Maryland Heights.
Two zones: Westport Plaza (63146, date-night and groups) and the Dorsett Road corridor (63043, everyday and carryout). A few spots are dinner-only or closed early in the week. Some park-area addresses read “St. Louis 63146” but are inside Maryland Heights city limits.

### Basso on the Plaza
Basso is Westport's newest dining anchor (opened 2025) — the second location of the local Basso, doing wood-fired steaks and pizzas. Get the marrow-butter Wood-Fire Burger or the hot-honey pepperoni pizza, and finish with the Spumoni Sundae. Date-night caliber. Closed Sunday and Monday.
📍 545 West Port Plaza Dr, Maryland Heights, MO 63146

### Drunken Fish — Westport Plaza
Drunken Fish is the very first one — the Westport location that launched a St. Louis sushi brand in 2003 — with happy hour three times a day and weekend DJ nights. Rolls and sake on the plaza's second level.
📍 639 Westport Plaza Dr, Maryland Heights, MO 63146

### Kobe Steak House of Japan
Kobe has done tableside teppanyaki since 1985 — your dinner cooked and performed by your own chef, onion volcano and flying-rice tricks included. Built-in dinner-and-a-show, great for groups and celebrations.
📍 645 Westport Plaza Dr, Maryland Heights, MO 63146

### Gioia's Deli (Maryland Heights window)
Gioia's is a century-old St. Louis legend, and this is its to-go walk-up window — order the Original Hot Salami, house-ground and served hot on a crusty Italian loaf with pepperoncini and spicy mustard. A true only-in-St.-Louis bite. Weekday lunch only, carryout.
📍 11855 Adie Rd, Maryland Heights, MO 63043

### Casa Juárez Mexican Town
Casa Juárez is the 20-plus-year family Mexican fixture on Dorsett — street tacos come four to a plate instead of three, with a full bar and margaritas. The weekly-regular neighborhood spot.
📍 12710 Dorsett Rd, Maryland Heights, MO 63043

### Thai Kitchen
Thai Kitchen is the owner-run Thai spot with a no-shortcuts menu — well over 100 items, including some 30 curries and 47 noodle and rice dishes. The kind of from-scratch range you only get when the owner's in the kitchen. Closed Mondays.
📍 2031 Dorsett Village, Maryland Heights, MO 63043

### Off The Grill
Off The Grill is the independent char-broil counter built for the Dorsett lunch crowd — char-broiled burgers and steakhouse-quality sirloin tips without the steakhouse bill. Closed Sundays.
📍 11640 Dorsett Rd, Maryland Heights, MO 63043

### Creve Coeur Lakehouse Bar & Grill
Creve Coeur Lakehouse sits right on the trail at Creve Coeur Park with lake views and a dog-friendly patio — pull off a bike ride and eat lakeside, burger and fried tilapia in hand. Family-owned since 2006. Closed Mon–Tue.
📍 2160 Creve Coeur Mill Rd, Maryland Heights, MO 63146

### Trainwreck Saloon — Westport
Trainwreck is an Old-West rustic saloon (a St. Louis-area tavern group, not a national chain) — Wreck Wings, a pub-cheddar burger, fried pickles, toasted ravioli, live music, and a kitchen open late. The plaza's go-to game-day and late-night spot.
📍 314 West Port Plaza Dr, Maryland Heights, MO 63146

### Why this town matters
Maryland Heights gives you a walkable entertainment plaza and a workaday local corridor — hibachi and wood-fired Italian on one end, a century-old hot-salami window and a four-to-a-plate taqueria on the other. The chain apps see a highway interchange; we map both food worlds.

### FAQ
What's the best restaurant in Maryland Heights, MO?
For date night, Basso on the Plaza (wood-fired Italian) or Kobe hibachi. For a hyper-local bite, the Gioia's hot-salami walk-up window on Adie Rd.
What is Westport Plaza?
A walkable dining-and-entertainment hub off I-270 packed with independent and local concepts — Basso, Kobe hibachi, the original Drunken Fish sushi, Trainwreck Saloon — plus events like the monthly “Parties on the Plaza.” The best one-stop area for a group.
Where do locals eat everyday in Maryland Heights?
The Dorsett Road corridor — Casa Juárez (Mexican, 20+ years), Thai Kitchen, Off The Grill, and the Gioia's hot-salami window — generally more affordable than the Plaza.
Is there lakeside dining in Maryland Heights?
Yes — Creve Coeur Lakehouse Bar & Grill sits right on the Creve Coeur Park trail with lake views and a dog-friendly patio.

### Plan your Maryland Heights visit
A Gioia's hot salami for lunch, a lakeside afternoon at Creve Coeur Lakehouse, and a tableside hibachi dinner at Kobe in Westport. For more local spots across the metro, explore St Louis Near Me Directory .

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
Maryville is a small Metro East town wedged between Collinsville, Glen Carbon, and Edwardsville, and its food scene is exactly what you'd expect from that — tight, honest, and strung along one road. North Center Street (Route 159) is the whole story: a frozen-custard institution with lines down the lot on summer nights, a veteran-owned BBQ kitchen, a sit-down cantina, and a big-portion family diner, all within a few blocks. It's not deep, but it's real — and three bigger food towns sit minutes away.
From an hourly-made custard ritual to scratch comfort food from a veteran's kitchen, here's where to eat in Maryville.
Maryville's independents line up on North Center Street (Route 159) (62062), with one just off it — a genuine park-once cluster. The scene is honestly on the thin side, so we keep this list to the real, verified spots and point you to Edwardsville, Glen Carbon, and Collinsville (all 5–10 minutes away) for more range. This is Maryville, Illinois — not Tennessee.

### Bobby's Frozen Custard
The local landmark. Bobby's makes its custard fresh by the hour, and on warm summer nights the walk-up window draws lines down the lot. The famous Turtle Sundae is the order, the concretes the close second. It's the Maryville summer ritual.
📍 2525 N. Center St., Maryville, IL 62062

### Boogie's Restaurant & Sports Bar
Boogie's is the locally owned New American sports bar with genuinely award-winning wings (a regional People's Choice winner) — plus steaks and burgers, big screens, darts, and house-made ranch worth the wing dunk.
📍 2082 Vadalabene Dr., Maryville, IL 62062

### Mariachi's Mexican Restaurant & Cantina
Mariachi's is the locally owned sit-down cantina where the margaritas are built for the table and the fajita platters come out loud and steaming — the kind of order the whole room turns to look at. The go-to Mexican night.
📍 2922 N. Center St., Maryville, IL 62062

### Red Apple Family Restaurant
Red Apple is the locally owned 6 a.m.-to-3 p.m. breakfast-and-lunch diner where the portions are big enough that “I'll just take half home” is the standard line — clean, busy, old-school home cooking.
📍 2625 N. Center St., Maryville, IL 62062

### Betty Lou's Table
Betty Lou's Table is a disabled-veteran-owned BBQ and scratch-comfort kitchen built around gathering back at the family table — pulled pork, ribs, bacon-wrapped meatloaf, chicken and dumplings, hush puppies, and a daily-special board (beef and noodles) that sells out.
📍 2719 N. Center St., Maryville, IL 62062

### Why this town matters
Maryville is a tight, honest little cluster on Route 159 — a custard institution, a veteran's BBQ table, an award-winning wing bar — surrounded by three bigger food towns. We won't pad the list to hit a number; we map the real five and tell you exactly where to go next door.

### FAQ
What's the best-known place to eat in Maryville, IL?
Bobby's Frozen Custard — home of the Turtle Sundae, with custard made fresh hourly. It's the dessert destination people drive into Maryville for and the most recognizable local food name in town.
Is Maryville's food scene big?
It's honestly compact — a tight cluster of about five real independents on North Center Street. The upside: Maryville sits in the middle of a strong dining triangle, 5–10 minutes from Edwardsville, Glen Carbon, and Collinsville.
Where can families eat in Maryville?
Without leaving town: Red Apple (big-portion breakfast and lunch), Betty Lou's Table (scratch BBQ and comfort), Mariachi's (sit-down Mexican), and Bobby's for after-dinner custard — a full kid-friendly day on one street.
Is this Maryville Illinois or Tennessee?
This is Maryville, Illinois (Madison County, ZIP 62062, on Route 159 in the Metro East) — not the better-known Maryville, Tennessee.

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
Mascoutah is a small German-founded town near Scott Air Force Base, and it's got something a lot of Metro East suburbs don't: a genuine, walkable Main Street with real locally-owned spots a few blocks apart. Two family Mexican restaurants, a cocktail lounge inside a restored 1890 bank, a veteran-and-woman-owned coffee shop, and a hometown bar-and-grill — all downtown. The old German restaurant has closed, so that heritage is history now, but the Main Street is very much alive.
From a cocktail bar inside an 1890 bank vault to parmesan-crusted tacos, here's where to eat in Mascoutah.
Mascoutah's independents pack into a few blocks of Main Street (62258), genuinely walkable for a small town. It serves a steady mix of locals and Scott AFB families. For more variety, O'Fallon and Belleville are a short drive west. (The old German spot, Roemertopf, has closed — heritage only.)

### The Vault
The town landmark. The Vault is a craft-cocktail and burger lounge set inside the restored 1890 First National Bank of Mascoutah building — you sip a bourbon where townsfolk once cashed checks, in a downtown landmark renovated by local owners. The in-house “Hawkins Burger Bar” handles the food.
📍 28 E. Main St., Mascoutah, IL 62258

### Camino Real Authentic Mexican Restaurant
Camino Real is the Main Street Mexican standby — authentic plates with a tortilla soup reviewers call “the most refreshing and relaxing,” local enough that the Mascoutah Heritage Museum has a history page on the building. Open seven days.
📍 9 W. Main St., Mascoutah, IL 62258

### El Sombrero Mexican Restaurant
El Sombrero is the second locally-owned Mexican kitchen a few doors down — chimichangas, quesadillas, and classic plates. That tiny Main Street supports two independent Mexican spots is a real point of local pride. Closed Mondays.
📍 215 W. Main St., Mascoutah, IL 62258

### Skootr's Restaurant & Bar
Skootr's is the family-owned hometown bar and grill — pulled pork, pork steak, ribeye, a bacon cheeseburger, and a Friday fish plate, with late-night hours and karaoke Thursdays. The kind of place where the kitchen closes but the bar keeps going till 2 a.m.
📍 323 E. Main St., Mascoutah, IL 62258

### The Juicy Peanut Bar & Grill
The Juicy Peanut is the bar and grill whose tacos come on freshly fried, parmesan-cheese-crusted shells with a house “Valentine” hot sauce — a small-town twist locals come back for, plus wings and a pork tenderloin sandwich, and $1.75 Taco Mondays.
📍 724 W. Main St., Mascoutah, IL 62258

### St. Louis Coffee World
St. Louis Coffee World is the woman-, veteran-, and minority-owned Main Street coffee shop — specialty espresso, breakfast and lunch, boba, and ice cream. Owner “Richie” gets named in the reviews; the opposite of a faceless drive-thru.
📍 200 E. Main St. #100, Mascoutah, IL 62258

### Why this town matters
Mascoutah has what a lot of bigger suburbs lost — a real, walkable Main Street where the independents sit a few doors apart: two family Mexican rooms, a cocktail lounge in an 1890 bank, a veteran-owned coffee shop. The apps don't capture a small-town Main Street; we do.

### FAQ
What's the standout place to eat in Mascoutah, IL?
The Vault — a craft-cocktail and burger lounge inside the restored 1890 First National Bank building, the town's most “destination” independent. Camino Real is the Main Street Mexican go-to.
Is downtown Mascoutah walkable for food?
Yes — a few blocks of Main Street pack in Camino Real, El Sombrero, Skootr's, The Vault, and St. Louis Coffee World, genuinely walkable for a small town.
Is there still German food in Mascoutah?
Mascoutah was founded by German immigrants, but the German restaurant (Roemertopf) has closed — so today's flavor leans Mexican, American bar-and-grill, and coffee rather than schnitzel.
Where's more food near Mascoutah?
You're minutes from Scott Air Force Base, and O'Fallon, IL and Belleville are a short drive west with much deeper restaurant rows — see our O'Fallon IL and Belleville guides.

### Plan your Mascoutah visit
A coffee at St. Louis Coffee World, parmesan-crusted tacos at The Juicy Peanut, and a cocktail in the old bank vault at The Vault. For more local spots across the Metro East, explore St Louis Near Me Directory .

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
Part of South County — explore the whole region in our South County restaurant guide .
Mehlville is the heart of South County — Lemay Ferry Road running straight through it — and the food is classic, unpretentious St. Louis: toasted ravioli, Provel-square pizza, brain sandwiches, affordable steakhouses, and a nationally famous donut. This is neighborhood-tavern and family-kitchen territory, value-priced and proud of it, with addresses that bleed across Mehlville, Lemay, and Tesson Ferry.
From a nationally ranked "Cinnamon Glob" to an old-school brain sandwich, here's where to eat in Mehlville.
The independents string along Lemay Ferry Rd and the Tesson Ferry corridor (63125/63128). Because Mehlville is an unincorporated area, addresses often read St. Louis, Lemay, or Oakville — all the same South County dining spine. A few keep early or odd hours (the donut shop sells out by midday).

### The Donut Stop
The Donut Stop has made donuts on Lemay Ferry since 1953 — and earned national fame for the Cinnamon Glob , a dense, hole-less ball of fried dough that Saveur and The Daily Meal both honored (it ranked #19 among America's best donuts). Open 4:30 a.m.; the best globs sell out early. Closed Mon–Tue.
📍 1101 Lemay Ferry Rd, St. Louis, MO 63125

### Fergie's Bar & Restaurant
Fergie's is a Lemay institution since 1990 — and one of the last places in St. Louis where you can still order an old-school fried brain sandwich on rye. The fried chicken is the house specialty; regulars call it the best in town. Two longtime employees bought it from the founder in 2020.
📍 1699 Lemay Ferry Rd, St. Louis, MO 63125

### Tucker's Place South County
Tucker's Place South County is the family-run South County fixture for ~40 years — hand-cut steaks at a fair price, house-made toasted ravioli, breaded mushrooms with homemade marinara, and a house salad dressing with a following. Closed Sunday.
📍 3939 Union Rd, St. Louis, MO 63125

### Liliana's Italian Kitchen
Liliana's is the family kitchen Tim and Kathy named for their daughter — house-made toasted ravioli, fried calamari, and a celebrated St. Louis-style square ("quadrangle") pizza. The old-school red-sauce-and-Provel-square Italian South County grew up on. Closed Monday.
📍 11836 Tesson Ferry Rd, St. Louis, MO 63128

### Thai Orchid
Thai Orchid is the unassuming strip-center storefront South County locals quietly guard as their go-to for real Thai — authentic curries and noodle dishes on the Lemay Ferry strip. Closed Monday.
📍 3027 Lemay Ferry Rd, St. Louis, MO 63125

### La Fiesta Mexican Restaurant
La Fiesta is the family-run Mexican spot tucked into the Home Depot plaza off S. Lindbergh — fresh-made traditional plates and margaritas, the neighborhood's weeknight fajitas-and-margaritas stop for over a decade.
📍 7439 S Lindbergh Blvd, Mehlville, MO 63125

### Lemay Wok
Lemay Wok is the strip-mall Chinese hidden gem where a regular will argue with anyone that the General Tso's chicken and crab rangoon are the best in town. Opens at 2:30 p.m. (no lunch); closed Sunday.
📍 4530 Lemay Ferry Rd, St. Louis, MO 63129

### Why this town matters
Mehlville is classic, unpretentious St. Louis — toasted rav, Provel squares, a brain sandwich, a 1953 donut shop ranked among America's best. This is family-kitchen and neighborhood-tavern country, value-priced, and the chain apps don't get the culture. We map the Lemay Ferry spine the locals actually drive.

### FAQ
What's the most famous place to eat in Mehlville, MO?
The Donut Stop on Lemay Ferry (since 1953) — nationally famous for its "Cinnamon Glob," a hole-less fried-dough ball that made Saveur 's 50 favorites and The Daily Meal 's 25 best donuts in America.
Where's the classic South County food in Mehlville?
Lemay Ferry Road is the spine — Fergie's (fried chicken, brain sandwich), Tucker's Place (affordable steaks + toasted rav), Liliana's (Provel-square pizza), Thai Orchid, and Lemay Wok all sit on or just off it.
Can you still get a brain sandwich in St. Louis?
Yes — Fergie's in Lemay is one of the last spots still serving the old-school fried brain sandwich on rye, a genuine St. Louis throwback.
Is Mehlville the same as Oakville and Lemay?
They overlap — Mehlville is an unincorporated area, so "Mehlville" restaurants often carry St. Louis, Lemay (63125), Oakville (63129), or Tesson Ferry (63128) addresses. They share one South County dining corridor.

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
Cross the river and climb the bluffs about twenty-five minutes from downtown St. Louis and you reach Millstadt — a German farming village so thoroughly settled by immigrants from the Rhineland-Pfalz that an 1881 county history claimed only seven English families were left in town. They came in 1834, named it Centreville, got overruled by the post office, and ended up Millstadt. Nearly two centuries later, the German bones still show — in the church names, the festival in Liederkranz Park, and the tavern-and-fish-fry food culture.
This is a walkable little Main Street town where nearly every good spot sits within a few blocks on Washington Street — a cash-only corner tavern with a famous fish stand, a gas-station-turned-brewery, an ice cream shop pulling Kaldi's espresso, and a Cajun gastropub that has no business being this far from New Orleans. Here's where to eat in Millstadt.
Most of these line up on Washington Street , so you can park once and graze. A heads-up: Ott's is cash only (ATM on site), and a couple of the breakfast spots close Mondays. If you want the town at full volume, come for Millstadt Homecoming over Labor Day weekend at Liederkranz Park — parades, food, and the kind of small-town turnout that tells you the place still has a heartbeat.

### Ott's Tavern & Millstadt Fish Stand
Start at the institution. Ott's is the classic Metro-East corner tavern — burgers, wings, pizza — with an attached fish stand turning out the famous fried cod, house slaw, and jalapeño hush puppies. There's a beer garden out back, daily lunch specials at the bar, and a strict cash-only policy that somehow makes it taste better. Pure small-town tavern culture.
📍 20 E Washington St, Millstadt, IL 62260

### Millpond Brewing
The newest reason to drive out: Millpond Brewing turned a former Shell gas station into the town's hometown craft brewery — lagers, hazy IPAs, barrel-aged beers, rotating food trucks on weekends, and a homebrewer "incubator" where local brewers scale up their recipes on Millpond's system. Community-sourced beer in a town that's all community. You can even bring in food from the other Main Street spots.
📍 308 E Washington St, Millstadt, IL 62260

### Reinhardt's Restaurant & Lounge
Reinhardt's is the old-school family restaurant-and-lounge — crispy fried chicken, country-fried steak, sausage gravy, and fish, served in a neighborhood-gathering room with a pool table. The German surname fits the town, and so does the stick-to-your-ribs cooking.
📍 201 W Madison St, Millstadt, IL 62260

### Good Morning Cafe
For breakfast and brunch, Good Morning Cafe partners with local coffee roasters, bakes its own goods, and runs a Tex-Mex streak through the morning menu — the "GM Slam," huevos rancheros, banana pancakes. There's even a rear drive-thru window for the running-late crowd. Closed Mondays.
📍 725 W Washington St, Millstadt, IL 62260

### Sunrise Pancake House
The other morning option, Sunrise is the family-owned-and-operated breakfast-and-lunch diner doing old-fashioned pancakes, French toast, crepes, and cheese omelets — generous, affordable, homestyle. It's been name-checked in "biscuits and gravy worth a road trip" roundups, which is exactly the energy you want from a small-town diner.
📍 548 E Washington St, Ste 8, Millstadt, IL 62260

### Happy Days Ice Cream & Coffee Shop
A Main Street fixture for 25-plus years , Happy Days scoops up to 30 flavors, milkshakes, sundaes, and concretes (a proper St. Louis-region nod) — and runs a full espresso bar on Kaldi's Coffee , the beloved local roaster. The all-ages, year-round, walk-and-cool-off stop in the middle of town.
📍 119 W Washington St, Millstadt, IL 62260

### Spike's Public House
Here's the curveball — a Cajun/Creole gastropub in a German village. Spike's does muffulettas, fried crawfish tails, a crawfish po'boy, plus calzones and tacos, right in the Washington Street core. Unexpected, a little rowdy, and a fun break from the fish-fry-and-fried-chicken default.
📍 4 E Washington St, Millstadt, IL 62260

### Mariachi's Mexican Restaurant & Cantina
Rounding out the town, Mariachi's fills the full-service Mexican niche — a locally run, sit-down cantina on the west end of Washington Street, the place for fajitas and a margarita after a Main Street stroll.
📍 717 W Washington St, Millstadt, IL 62260

### Why this little town matters
Millstadt is a 190-year-old German village on the bluffs that most St. Louisans have never once driven through — and it quietly fields a cash-only tavern with a legendary fish stand, a brewery in an old gas station, a 25-year ice cream shop pulling Kaldi's espresso, and a Cajun gastropub, nearly all of it walkable on one street. That's a real Main Street, the kind the national apps reduce to a couple of misfiled listings.

What's the most famous place to eat in Millstadt, IL?
Ott's Tavern & Millstadt Fish Stand — a cash-only corner tavern with a beer garden and a fish stand known for fried cod and jalapeño hush puppies.
Does Millstadt have a brewery?
Yes — Millpond Brewing, built inside a former gas station, pours craft beer with weekend food trucks and runs a homebrewer incubator program.
Where do locals get breakfast in Millstadt?
Good Morning Cafe (local-roaster coffee, Tex-Mex breakfast, closed Mondays) and Sunrise Pancake House (family-owned homestyle diner). For coffee and ice cream, Happy Days has been on Main Street 25-plus years.
Is there a German restaurant in Millstadt?
Despite the deep German heritage, there's no standalone German restaurant or bakery in town today — the heritage lives on in the festivals, the church and family names, and the tavern-and-fish-fry food culture rather than a dedicated German menu.

Mt Olive is a small town of about 2,000 on a historic alignment of Route 66 — and notably home to the Union Miners Cemetery and the Mother Jones Monument, the only union-owned cemetery in the country. The food scene is small but entirely local: there are no sit-down chains here, just four genuine independents and a small-batch coffee roaster. People in Mt Olive get hungry too, and this is horseshoe country — the central-Illinois open-face specialty shows up on the menus.
From an 1982 tavern's horseshoes to scratch coconut cream pie, here's where to eat in Mt Olive.
The independents sit downtown around East/West Main Street and out on Route 138 (62069). It's a tiny scene — no national franchises with a dining room — so for more variety, neighbors up and down I-55 (Staunton, Gillespie, Litchfield) are short drives. A diner stop pairs naturally with a Route 66 / Mother Jones day trip.

### Tilley's Tavern
The standout. Tilley's has been Mt Olive's premier bar and grill since 1982 — known across the area for its horseshoe platters (the open-face Illinois specialty: meat on Texas toast, piled with fries, smothered in cheese sauce) and signature burgers, with pool, darts, and gaming. Open daily till 2 a.m.
📍 303 E. Main St., Mt Olive, IL 62069

### Route 138 Cafe
Route 138 Cafe is the home-style diner just off the highway (formerly Sunset Restaurant, renamed under new ownership) where the pies are scratch-made — coconut cream is the one locals call "amazing" — alongside french toast, catfish nuggets, and chicken and dumplings. Closed Mondays.

### Little Italy's Pizza
Little Italy's is the small-town pizzeria that also scoops ice cream — hand-tossed and thin-crust pizza, plus pasta, subs, wings, and salads, with later weekend hours for the after-the-game crowd.
📍 110 W. Main St., Mt Olive, IL 62069

### Mel's Place
Mel's Place is the remodeled neighborhood tavern — the after-work gathering spot for "friendly faces, good music, and cold drinks," with karaoke every Friday night. The local watering hole.
📍 208 E. Main St., Mt Olive, IL 62069

### Why this town matters
Mt Olive is a 2,000-person Route 66 town with zero sit-down chains — just an 1982 horseshoe tavern, a scratch-pie diner, a pizzeria, and a corner bar, plus a coffee roaster. Pair it with the Mother Jones Monument and you've got a genuine small-town stop. Nobody writes about Mt Olive's food. We do.

A central-Illinois open-face sandwich: meat on Texas toast, piled with fries, smothered in cheese sauce. Mt Olive is horseshoe country, and Tilley's is the place to try one.

New Baden was built by German immigrants in 1855 and named, plainly enough, after Baden, Germany — and the town never let go of that thread. The main drag is Hanover Street (a German place-name itself), St. George Catholic Church anchors the skyline, and after an 1896 tornado leveled the place, the neighboring German villages helped rebuild it bigger than before. Today it's a tidy town of about 3,400 that eats far better than its size suggests.
This is genuine small-town German heartland: a homestyle diner famous for fried chicken, a bakery some call the best donuts in Illinois, a nonprofit café with a real mission, and a couple of authentic Mexican spots for good measure. Here's where to eat in New Baden.
Most of the good stuff is on Hanover Street , so it's an easy crawl. The bakery keeps early hours and closes Mondays; the nonprofit café is daytime-only — check before you go. And one honest note: this is a homestyle-diner-and-bakery town, not a fine-dining one, which is precisely its charm. Want to make a day of it? By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
For a town of about 2,400 people, New Haven has no business being this good. It sits on a bluff above the Missouri River out in Franklin County wine country, a tidy historic main street facing a riverwalk — the kind of place a man named John Colter, the Lewis and Clark expedition's “first mountain man,” chose to settle down after he'd seen the whole frontier. He's honored on a bluff just outside town. You'll understand the choice about an hour into your visit.
Here's the part that surprises people: this little river town fields an estate winery older than most of us, a craft distillery, a riverfront brewery, an 1880s Old-West resort restaurant, and a downtown coffee-and-artisan shop — all within a short stroll of the water. It's a genuine wine-country day trip masquerading as a dot on the map. Here's where to eat and drink in New Haven.
Wine-country hours are real hours — several of the best spots here run limited days (weekends, or afternoons only), and the brewery and resort restaurant keep especially tight schedules. Check before you drive. New Haven is roughly 11 miles from Washington and 13 from Hermann, so it slots neatly into a Hermann Wine Trail day — New Haven is the trail's eastern anchor.

### Röbller Vineyard & Winery
Start with the flagship. Röbller is a family estate winery founded in 1988 by Bob and Lois Mueller on an 85-acre farm — and their Norton (Missouri's state grape) won Best in Show and the very first Governor's Cup at the 1994 state fair. Run today by their son Jerry, it pours complimentary tastings on a covered deck over the vines, with cheese-and-sausage picnic plates to go with the view.
📍 275 Röbller Vineyard Rd, New Haven, MO 63068

### Pinckney Bend Distillery
A river town with its own craft distillery — that's New Haven punching above its weight again. Pinckney Bend makes an award-recognized American Dry Gin plus vodka and whiskey, and the tasting room runs distillery tours and even “blend your own” gin and whiskey classes. The kind of hands-on stop you can't get at a chain anything.
📍 1101 Miller St, New Haven, MO 63068

### Paddle Stop Brewery
Right on the historic riverfront, Paddle Stop Brewery pours lagers, IPAs, and stouts with live music indoors and out, and a calendar full of the stuff small towns do best — a Stoutfest, a chili cook-off. It's the riverfront hang, the one with the river-and-adventure spirit baked right into the name.
📍 204 Front St, New Haven, MO 63068

### Town Hall Tap Room at Cedar Creek
This one's pure character. Out at Cedar Creek, Town Hall Tap Room sits on a recreated 1880s Old-West town street — a saloon-and-restaurant with wood interiors, a pool table, local beers and spirits, live music, and wine-country views. It runs weekend-only hours (Friday evening and Saturday), so plan around it, but it's worth the planning.
📍 Cedar Creek, New Haven, MO 63068

### New Day Mercantile
Downtown's morning stop, New Day Mercantile is a coffee shop and local-artisan store run by sisters Rachel and Wilhelmina Bartels — good coffee alongside a curated collection of locally made pottery, jewelry, woodwork, and signs. Caffeine and a souvenir from the same counter, on the historic Front Street block.
📍 123 Front St, New Haven, MO 63068

### Lang-A-Tang Deli, Catering & Charcuterie
For lunch downtown, Lang-A-Tang does coffee, pastries, soups, salads, paninis, and proper charcuterie boards — the kind of from-scratch deli a riverwalk town deserves, with sandwiches locals rave about. A great grab before or after a winery run.
📍 125 Front St, New Haven, MO 63068

### Paddle Stop, Pinckney Bend, and the riverwalk
(For Mexican and pub options, Dos Bros on Front Street and T & T Hilltop Lounge on Highway 100 round out the town — confirm the current name/hours before you go, as the Front Street spot has changed hands recently.) However you fill the afternoon, end it on the restored Front Street riverwalk above the Missouri River, where the John Colter memorial marks the bluff. It's the kind of view that explains why a mountain man stopped wandering.

### Why this little town matters
New Haven is the proof of Lane's whole thesis: a town of 2,400 with a 35-year estate winery, a craft distillery, a riverfront brewery, an 1880s saloon restaurant, and a downtown coffee-and-artisan shop — every one of them independent, every one of them invisible on the national maps that only know chains. A place like this doesn't survive on drive-by traffic. It survives because people find it.

### FAQ
Is New Haven, MO worth the drive from St. Louis?
For wine-country fans, absolutely — it's about an hour out and packs an estate winery, a craft distillery, a riverfront brewery, and a historic riverwalk into one small town. Pair it with Washington or Hermann for a full day.
What's the oldest winery in New Haven?
Röbller Vineyard & Winery, a family estate founded in 1988 and known for its award-winning Norton — Missouri's state grape.
Does New Haven have a distillery?
Yes — Pinckney Bend Distillery, known for its American Dry Gin, with a tasting room, distillery tours, and “blend your own” classes.
Is New Haven on the Katy Trail?
The Katy Trail runs along the north bank of the Missouri River across from town, not directly through downtown — but New Haven is the eastern anchor of the Hermann Wine Trail and an easy add to a Katy Trail or wine-country trip.

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
New Melle is tiny — about 540 people — a German village in western St. Charles County, founded in 1839 by immigrants from Melle, Germany, who named their new home after the one they'd left. It sits at the quiet edge of Missouri wine country, just north of the Defiance corridor and the Daniel Boone Home. You don't come here for a big restaurant row. You come for a couple of genuinely good local spots, a glass of something, and the kind of small-town welcome that's getting harder to find.
When you're out this way and hungry, here's where to eat in New Melle.
New Melle is small, so plan a little: the spots below keep their own hours (a couple are evening-focused), and a newer one or two are worth a quick call first. The town sits minutes from the Defiance / Femme Osage wine corridor and the Historic Daniel Boone Home , so it's easy to build a wine-country afternoon around a meal here.

### Liz's Bar & Grill
Start at the heart of town — and the best story in it. Liz's Bar & Grill is home of "Liz's Famous Half-Pound Burger," plus fried chicken, steak, and Taco Tuesday. Original owner Liz Holloway ran it for nearly 30 years until she passed in early 2025; her friend Zach King, who'd worked for her and talked with her about taking it over, reopened it that October to carry her name forward. Recent regulars say he's done her proud.
📍 3585 Mill St, New Melle, MO 63365

### The Quarry
The destination spot. The Quarry (Quarry Wine Garden & Resort) is a restaurant, wine bar, and live-music venue set in a former quarry — patios, fire pits, sand volleyball, even a floating golf green and indoor golf bays. New owners (one of them a Meier, an old New Melle family name) took over in late 2025, added full table service and a new menu, with a beer garden coming. Wine, bites, music, and golf in one scenic stop.
📍 3960 Highway Z, New Melle, MO 63365

### Die Wasserstelle
The name says it all — Die Wasserstelle is German for "the watering hole," a fitting nod to the village's heritage. It's a pub-style bar and grill doing burgers, chili dogs, wings, and fish tacos — simple, high-quality, with a pet-friendly patio (family-friendly early, adults-only after 9). A good local hang to round out the town.
📍 30 W Hwy D, New Melle, MO 63365

### Make a day of it: the Defiance wine corridor
New Melle's real superpower is where it sits . A short drive south drops you into the Defiance / Femme Osage wine corridor — Defiance Ridge Vineyards, Good News Brewing's Defiance café, and the gateway to the Augusta and Dutzow wineries — with the Historic Daniel Boone Home as the anchor. Eat in New Melle, then chase the afternoon into wine country.

### Why this little town matters
New Melle is a 540-person German village that most maps treat as a dot — but it keeps a beloved bar-and-grill (now lovingly carried on in its founder's name), a genuine quarry-side destination, and a German-named watering hole, all minutes from one of Missouri's best wine corridors. That's a real community, and the honest, human stories behind these places are exactly what a national app will never show you.

What's the story behind Liz's Bar & Grill?
Original owner Liz Holloway ran it for nearly 30 years until her passing in early 2025; her friend Zach King reopened it in October 2025 to carry on her name. (Ignore any old "closed" listings — it's back and well-reviewed.)

Yes — it sits at the northern edge of the Defiance / Femme Osage wine corridor, minutes from Defiance Ridge Vineyards, the Historic Daniel Boone Home, and the road to Augusta and Dutzow.

It was settled in 1839 by German immigrants from Melle, Germany; St. Paul Lutheran Church (1844) and the Meier General Store are both on the National Register of Historic Places.

Oakville is far South County — Telegraph Road running down toward Jefferson Barracks and the Mississippi — and like a lot of the suburbs out here, the highway frontage is chain-heavy. ### Bill Gianino's Restaurant
Bill Gianino's has anchored Oakville Italian since 1975 — home-cooked pastas, St. Louis-style pizza, steaks, and toasted ravioli. Founder Bill passed in 2020, but his sons still run it: over 50 years in the same family. The town's longest-running name.
📍 4571 Chestnut Park Plaza, Oakville, MO 63129

### Frankie G's Grill & Bar
Frankie G's is the Gianino family's grill-and-bar right next to the flagship — open since 1991, and it claims to be the inventor of the “trashed wing.” Two family concepts side by side in one plaza.
📍 4565 Chestnut Park Plaza, Oakville, MO 63129

### Crusoe's Restaurant & Croc's Sports Bar
Crusoe's is the family-owned casual American spot and sports bar tucked in the Oakville Shopping Center — breaded wings, the Crusoe's Party Sub, chicken fettuccine, and toasted ravioli. The neighborhood living-room kind of place.
📍 5591 Oakville Shopping Center, St. Louis (Oakville), MO 63129

### Garvey's Grill
Garvey's is the true corner neighborhood joint that's been pouring and grilling 25-plus years — wings (voted among the best in St. Louis), St. Louis-style Chicken Modiga pizza, and “Super Dave's Smokers” house barbecue, with a $4.95 burger-and-fries Monday special.
📍 5647 Telegraph Rd, St. Louis (Oakville), MO 63129

### Las Fuentes Mexican Restaurant
Las Fuentes has served the area since 1996 — Northern Mexican, with tacos al pastor, sizzling fajitas, and house-made margaritas. The vibrant, family-friendly go-to Mexican on Telegraph for nearly 30 years.
📍 6025 Telegraph Rd, Oakville, MO 63129

### Nubby's Telegraph
Nubby's is the locally owned barbecue-and-pizza spot owner Matt Hines opened in 2021 in a long-vacant space — smoked ribs and burnt ends, but also the talked-about crab rangoon pizza and brisket egg rolls, plus down-home German plates like dumplings with sauerkraut. 📍 6039 Telegraph Rd, St. Louis (Oakville), MO 63129

### Oakville Sports Pub
Oakville Sports Pub is the neighborhood's game-day living room — a wall of HDTVs for Cardinals, Blues, and Mizzou, the Billy Burger, ravioli pizza, and classic St. Louis thin-crust with the Provel-and-Monterey-Jack blend. Open late on weekends.
📍 6348 Telegraph Rd, St. Louis (Oakville), MO 63129

O'Fallon is one of the metro's biggest suburbs — and no, not the Illinois one. Between the breweries downtown and the independents along Highway K, there's a lot more here than the strip-mall surface suggests.
From a family Italian tribute to a Peruvian ceviche worth the drive, here's where to eat in O'Fallon, MO.
Two pockets: the Highway K / WingHaven corridor (63368) and historic downtown on South Main Street (63366), which anchors the brewery scene. A few of the best are dinner-only or closed Mondays. And yes — this is O'Fallon Missouri ; there's a separate O'Fallon, Illinois 40+ miles east, so always check the ZIP.

### Osteria Forto
Osteria Forto is O'Fallon's top-rated independent Italian — chef-owner Dominic Pietoso named it for his father, Chef Fortunato “Forto,” who grew up in Aversa, Italy, and runs it with his wife Elizabeth as a family tribute. Rigatoni Cardinale with shrimp and lobster is the order. Dinner only, closed Sunday and Monday.
📍 2509 Highway K, O'Fallon, MO 63368

### Los Incas Peruvian Restaurant
Los Incas is the family-owned Peruvian spot from a kitchen team with 20 years of experience in Peru — bright ceviche with toasted cancha corn and choclo, and a lomo saltado that co-owner Luis Moreno says he could eat every single day.
📍 4279 Keaton Crossing Blvd, O'Fallon, MO 63368

### The Brass Rail Steakhouse
The Brass Rail is the locally owned steakhouse-and-tavern that's been an O'Fallon staple for years — hand-cut steaks and classic American bar fare, where regulars come for the bar as much as the ribeye.
📍 4601 Highway K, O'Fallon, MO 63368

### Goodwood Brewing & Spirits
Goodwood anchors downtown O'Fallon's Main Street in a historic building (the former McGurk's Public House) — barrel-aged beers, chicken and waffles, and a flower-and-water-feature patio with live music. It's a Kentucky-rooted brewery brand, but this is O'Fallon's Main Street brewpub.
📍 108 S Main St, O'Fallon, MO 63366

### Crossroads Brewery
Crossroads is the locally owned WingHaven brewery running about 30 taps — house beer, cider, mead, even house-made seltzer and margaritas — plus a deep bourbon shelf and standouts like the Dragon Ass Oatmeal Stout. The local craft-beer hub.
📍 9995 Winghaven Blvd, O'Fallon, MO 63368

### CJ's Restaurant & Bar
CJ's is the genuine small family-run neighborhood spot on Highway K — American-Italian plates that read like someone's home kitchen, with a full bar. Closed Mondays. The unfussy local pick.
📍 2974 Highway K, O'Fallon, MO 63368

### The Irish Gypsy
The Irish Gypsy is the independent Irish pub and sports-bar-and-grill open 11 a.m. to 1:30 a.m. daily — making it O'Fallon's go-to late-night kitchen when most of Highway K has gone dark.
📍 1250 Bryan Road, O'Fallon, MO 63366

### George's Diner
The old-St.-Louis standout. George's is a hand-cut-fries greasy spoon where you can watch the owner cutting fresh potatoes — chicken-fried steak with white gravy, the Slinger Plate, breakfast and lunch only. The diner's held this Woodson Road corner under a few names for over 50 years.
📍 2539 Woodson Rd, Overland, MO 63114

### LaJoy's Coffee Cafe
LaJoy's is the Black-owned, woman-owned coffee café owner LaJoy Dabney opened because nothing was within walking distance of her own Overland home — a dirty chai and a house gooey-butter Danish her daughter bakes, bright yellow walls, made-to-order everything.
📍 8909 Lackland Rd, Overland, MO 63114

### Taqueria Durango
Taqueria Durango on Page is a comeback story — a March fire gutted it, then the pandemic hit, and it fought all the way back to reopen in Overland. Birria tacos, gorditas, free unlimited chips with three salsas, and most people eat for under $10.
📍 10238 Page Ave, Overland, MO 63114

### Chimi's Fresh-Mex
Chimi's is the neighborhood Fresh-Mex favorite — the sizzling Molcajete, steak tacos, chimichangas — pulling 1,800-plus reviews at a single small-suburb storefront, regulars naming their servers by name.
📍 2435 Woodson Rd, Overland, MO 63114

### Kitchen 95
Kitchen 95 is the Taiwanese and pan-Asian spot two restaurant veterans opened in 2021, where the proprietress is also the chef — a small, fresh-ingredient kitchen where the cook owns the place. Closed Wednesdays; call ahead on hours.
📍 2336 Woodson Rd, Overland, MO 63114

For a town this size, Pacific's food scene is genuinely independent — a 1963 custard drive-in, grass-fed burgers, BBQ with live blues, and a coffee shop that doubles as an open-mic stage. Here's where to eat in Pacific.

### Hoffman's Drive-In
Start at the institution. Hoffman's Drive-In has scooped frozen custard and ice cream in Pacific since 1963 — burgers and lunch specials too, but the vintage drive-in and the custard window are the point. A genuine multi-generation local landmark.
📍 306 S 1st St, Pacific, MO 63069

### Off The Rails Burger Bar
Downtown on Main, Off The Rails does gourmet grass-fed burgers — they source beef from Crooked Creek Farm — plus rotating specials in the heart of Train Town. Closed Wednesdays; worth planning around.

### Brown Jerry's Blues, Brews and Barbecue
The one with a stage. Brown Jerry's is the slow-smoked BBQ spot founded in 2017 by Jerry Holloway — Southern sides, wood-fired pizza, a full bar, and live blues. Locally voted among the best BBQ around. Closed Monday–Tuesday.
📍 147 W St Louis St, Pacific, MO 63069

### Little Ireland Coffee
Little Ireland Coffee is the downtown coffee-and-bakery spot a block off Route 66 — espresso, biscuits and gravy, pastries, plus open-mic and paint nights. The community gathering corner since 2017.
📍 125 N 1st St, Pacific, MO 63069

### El Agave Mexican Restaurant
El Agave is the locally owned Mexican kitchen just off old Route 66 — handmade tacos, enchiladas, fajitas, and burritos, plus catering. The dependable margarita-and-fajitas pick.

Pacific Brew Haus is the craft-beer bar and grill — sandwiches, wings, fish bites, and a solid draft list. (The name says brew; it's a craft-beer bar rather than a production brewery — either way, a good downtown hang.)
📍 220 S 1st St, Pacific, MO 63069

### Pacific Family Restaurant

Start at the anchor. Uncle Linny's is the family-owned, home-style restaurant locals lean on — breakfast-forward, open early, hearty and unpretentious. It's grown popular enough to add a second spot ("Food & Brews") down the road, but the original on Pontoon Road is the one to know.
📍 4112 Pontoon Rd, Pontoon Beach, IL 62040

### Doit's Village Inn
For the best local-story pick, Doit's Village Inn has been a family-owned neighborhood tavern since 1986 — biker-friendly, big patio, live music several nights a week, and the two things every Metro East tavern lives or dies on: $1–$2 Taco Wednesday and a Friday fish fry .
📍 4015 Pontoon Rd, Pontoon Beach, IL 62040

### Smokey Joe's Tavern
Smokey Joe's comes with real history baked in — the building started as a family home in the early 1940s, became a beloved bar called Zamarioni's, and lived on as the local watering hole before becoming Smokey Joe's. Tavern food, outdoor seating, and a genuine sense of place.
📍 3998 Lake St, Pontoon Beach, IL 62040

### Steel City Cheesecakes
The sweet standout. Steel City Cheesecakes is owner-baker Brooke Maske's independent dessert shop with a drive-through — cheesecakes in every form, plus cinnamon rolls, gooey butter bars, and cannolis, with a soda machine pouring SKI (the regional cult soda) over nugget ice. The "Steel City" name nods to Granite City's steel-mill roots.
📍 4025 Pontoon Rd, Pontoon Beach, IL 62040

### 3 De Mayo Mexican Restaurant
3 De Mayo is the family-run authentic Mexican spot on Highway 111 — full bar, kids' menu, patio, and a loyal local following. The dependable sit-down taco-and-margarita option in town.
📍 3710 IL-111, Pontoon Beach, IL 62040

### Why this little town matters
Pontoon Beach is a young river-bottoms village that the apps can barely distinguish from Granite City — which means its genuine local spots get lost in the shuffle. But the real ones are here: a family diner everyone knows, a 1986 tavern with a Friday fish fry, an old-house-turned-bar with decades of history, a cheesecake baker pouring SKI soda. Both share ZIP 62040 and blend together, so map apps mislabel businesses constantly. Everything in this guide is confirmed to be in Pontoon Beach proper — but you'll often see these spots tagged "Granite City" online.
