### Q. What is the most neglected car maintenance?
A.  Brake fluid and coolant, which have service intervals that are easy to forget. Alignment after a collision repair, cabin air filters and tire rotation come next. After body work, sensor recalibration is the item most often skipped and the one you should confirm.

## Auto Detailing in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/auto-detailing

### Detailing is not a car wash, so ask what the package includes: interior shampoo, clay bar decontamination and paint correction are separate services with separate labor.
### Common questions
### Q. How to choose a good car detailer?
A.  Shortlist two or three and interview them. Say what you want fixed, whether that is swirl marks, a stained interior or pet hair, and ask what their package actually includes and how long the car stays. Look at their own photos of correction work, and ask what products they use.
### Q. What is the correct order to detail a car?
A.  Interior first so dust does not settle on finished paint: vacuum, clean surfaces, treat leather. Outside, wheels and tires come before the body. Then wash, decontaminate with iron remover and clay, dry, correct the paint by machine, and finish with wax, sealant or coating. Glass last.
### Q. Is there a downside to ceramic coating a car?
A.  Yes. It costs far more than wax or sealant, and it locks in whatever the paint looks like, so proper correction and prep have to happen first. It is not scratch proof, still needs washing with the right products, and removal means polishing it off rather than stripping it.

## Auto Glass Repair in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/auto-glass-repair

### A chip smaller than a quarter and outside the driver’s line of sight can usually be resin-repaired in under an hour, so fix chips before they spread.
### Common questions
### Q. What are the red flags when choosing an automobile repair shop?
A.  No written estimate, no warranty in writing, vague answers about parts, and pressure to approve work on the spot. For glass specifically, a shop that cannot tell you whether your vehicle needs camera recalibration afterward has told you enough. Shortlist two or three and interview them.
### Q. What not to do when getting a new windshield?
A.  Do not drive before the adhesive has cured, do not slam doors, and do not remove the retention tape early. Skip car washes and rough roads for a couple of days, and do not let the shop hand the car back without confirming any camera recalibration was completed.
### Q. Why can’t you wash your car after windshield replacement?
A.  The urethane adhesive needs time to cure fully, and high pressure water can force its way into the fresh seal or lift the retention tape. Automatic washes add brushes and vibration on top of that. Waiting about two days, or whatever the installer specifies, avoids leaks and wind noise.

## Auto Parts in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/auto-parts

### Three grades, three trade-offs: OEM fits exactly, aftermarket ranges from better than original to worse, and salvage suits body and trim — bring your VIN.
### Common questions
### Q. What is the 30-60-90 rule for cars?
A.  It refers to scheduled maintenance at thirty, sixty and ninety thousand miles, when filters, fluids, belts and plugs come due in groups. Your owner manual is the real authority, since intervals differ by vehicle. Knowing the next milestone tells you which parts to buy ahead of time.
### Q. How to choose the right auto parts?
A.  Match the grade to the job. OEM parts come from the vehicle manufacturer and fit exactly. Aftermarket ranges from better than original to considerably worse. Used or salvage parts suit body panels, trim and interior pieces. Bring your VIN, then check the warranty and the core charge.
### Q. What are the three C’s of auto repair?
A.  Concern, cause and correction — the shorthand a shop uses to document what you reported, what they found, and what they did about it. Asking for all three in writing is reasonable, and it makes a warranty claim or a second opinion far easier later.

## Auto Repair in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/auto-repair

### Get a written estimate before work begins and require authorization before anything is added, the one habit that prevents most billing disputes.
### Common questions
### Q. What are the red flags when choosing an automobile repair shop?
A.  No written estimate, work added without calling you first, refusing to return old parts, a warranty that is verbal only, and pressure to decide on the spot. Shops that cannot say whether technicians are ASE certified, or which makes they specialize in, are worth passing on.
### Q. How to find a mechanic that won’t rip you off?
A.  Shortlist two or three shops worth interviewing, tell each what you want done and what you expect on warranty, then compare that against what they will actually commit to. Ask for authorization before anything is added, request your old parts back, and start with a small job.
### Q. What are the three C’s of auto repair?
A.  Concern, cause and correction. The concern is what you reported, the cause is what the shop diagnosed, and the correction is what was actually done. A repair order written that way tells you the shop found a root cause rather than replacing parts until the symptom stopped.

## Auto Salvage Yards in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/auto-salvage-yards

### Full service yards pull the part for you at a higher price, while self service yards charge admission and you bring tools and pull it yourself for far less.
### Common questions
### Q. What are red flags when buying a salvage car?
A.  Check the title brand and the reason behind it, since flood and structural damage are far harder to repair well than cosmetic damage. Get an independent inspection before money changes hands, look for mismatched panel gaps and paint, and confirm airbags were replaced rather than reset.
### Q. What’s the difference between a salvage yard and a junkyard?
A.  Little in practice, though salvage yard usually implies parts are inventoried and resold while junkyard implies scrap. What matters more is whether the yard is full service, meaning staff pull the part for you, or self service, where you pay admission and pull it yourself.

A.  It depends on the damage type, the repair cost relative to what the car would be worth once fixed, and whether the title becomes branded rebuilt, which affects resale and insurance later. Get an independent inspection and a written repair estimate before committing, and confirm structural and airbag repairs were done correctly.

## Bankruptcy Attorney in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/bankruptcy-attorney

### Chapter 7 discharges most unsecured debt in months and has an income test, while Chapter 13 reorganizes debt into a three-to-five-year repayment plan.
### Common questions
### Q. What not to tell the attorney?
A.  Nothing, in the sense that matters: hiding assets, recent transfers to family, side income or a second account is the fastest way to lose a case and face fraud allegations. Your conversations are privileged. What to leave out is speculation and secondhand opinion, not facts.

Common barriers include income above the means test threshold for your household size, a prior discharge inside the statutory waiting period, failure to complete the required credit counseling course, and conduct the court treats as bad faith. ## Banks in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/banks

### Compare banks on the terms that set the real cost — monthly maintenance fees, what waives them, overdraft policy and out-of-network ATM charges — then confirm deposits are federally insured.
### Common questions
### Q. How to choose a bank that’s right for you?
A.  Start with how you actually bank. If you rarely walk into a branch, weight the app, mobile deposit limits and transfer speed. If you do, check real lobby hours, since drive-thru, lobby and weekend hours are usually three different answers. Then compare fees and overdraft policy side by side.
### Q. What to look out for when choosing a bank?
A.  Monthly maintenance fees and the balance or direct deposit that waives them, overdraft and non-sufficient funds policy, out-of-network ATM charges, and minimum opening deposits. ### Q. Which bank gets the most complaints?
A.  Complaint counts track size more than service quality, so the largest institutions usually top any raw list. ### Common questions

A.  Historically a tavern served food and often lodging while a bar served drinks. Today the words mostly signal atmosphere: tavern suggests a neighborhood room with a kitchen, bar suggests drinks first. Licensing categories differ by state, so the names on the sign vary.

Avoid choosing fixtures after demolition starts, skipping proper waterproofing behind tile, and paying in full up front. A deposit with progress payments is the normal arrangement.
### Q. What bathroom renovation mistakes do contractors see most often?
A.  Undersized or missing ventilation, tile set over a substrate that was never waterproofed, and no plan for shutoffs and access panels. The other one is scope drift: work added mid-job without a written change order, which is how a two week bathroom becomes a two month one.

## Beauty Supply in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/beauty-supply

### Professional lines assume you know how to use them, and some stores restrict certain items to licensed cosmetologists, so bring your license for trade pricing.
### Common questions
### Q. What should a beginner buy for makeup?
A.  Start small: a moisturizer, a base matched in daylight rather than store lighting, a concealer, a setting powder, a brow pencil, mascara and a cream blush. Add one blending sponge and one brush. Buy the base last and ask staff to match it against your jaw, not your hand.
### Q. What is the correct order to apply makeup for beginners?
A.  Skincare and primer, then base, then concealer, then set with powder. Eyes next: shadow, liner, brows, mascara. Then blush, bronzer and highlighter, then lip liner and lip color, then setting spray. Cream products go before powder ones, or the powder will lift and go patchy.
### Q. What are 20 essential makeup items?
A.  Cleanser, moisturizer, sunscreen, primer, foundation, concealer, setting powder, blush, bronzer, highlighter, brow pencil, eyeshadow palette, eyeliner, mascara, lash curler, lip balm, lip liner, lipstick, setting spray and a blending sponge. Add brushes as you go, and expect to use half of that on an ordinary day.

## Boats in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/boats

### Match the hull to the water and the use, then budget for the trailer, storage, insurance, registration and winterizing, which together often exceed expectations.
### Common questions
### Q. What is the 1/3 rule in boating?
A.  It is a common fuel guideline: use one third of your fuel getting out, one third returning, and hold the last third in reserve for wind, current or a change of plan. Treat it as a minimum cushion, not a target, and check fuel before every trip.
### Q. What are good questions to ask when buying a boat?
A.  Ask the engine hours and service history, whether it has been in salt water, and what the loaded trailer weighs against your tow rating. Ask about title and lien status, which differ by state for boats and trailers. For anything used, arrange a marine survey and a sea trial first.
### Q. Is it difficult to get approved for a boat loan?
A.  Boat loans are secured by the boat and underwritten much like an auto loan, so approval depends on credit history, income, existing debt, the down payment and the age of the boat. Older boats and long terms are harder to place. Lenders vary widely, so compare several offers.

## Book Stores in the St. Louis Metro

### Common questions
### Q. What is the future of bookstores?
A.  Independent shops are holding on by leaning into what online retailers cannot offer, like curated staff picks, author events, and a browsing experience people enjoy in person. Stores that build community around reading, rather than just selling titles, tend to stay open longest.
### Q. How to pick a book at the bookstore?

A.  Ask what drew someone to the book, which character or idea stood out, and whether the ending felt earned. Questions about pacing, tone, and how the book compares to similar reads spark deeper conversation. Open ended prompts work better than yes or no questions for a lively discussion.

## Bowling in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/bowling

### Pricing works two ways, per game per person or hourly for the whole lane, and for a group hourly is usually cheaper and less rushed.
### Common questions
### Q. How do I know which bowling ball is right for me?
A.  Fit first, then weight, then surface. A pro shop measures your span and drills to your hand, which matters more than the ball itself. House balls have generic holes, so grip suffers. Plastic balls go straight and suit spares and beginners, reactive coverstocks hook for players learning to throw one.
### Q. Should I get a 14 or 15 pound bowling ball?
A.  Pick the heavier one only if you can repeat your swing with it late in a session. Fatigue wrecks accuracy and shoulders, so if your form breaks down, go lighter. Many bowlers throw 14 pounds with more speed and control than they can manage at 15. Try both first.
### Q. Do any pro bowlers use 14 lb balls?
A.  Yes. Plenty of competitive and professional bowlers throw 14 pounds, and some throw lighter still. Ball speed, rev rate and accuracy move the pins more than raw weight does, and a lighter ball is easier to repeat. Weight is not a measure of skill, so pick what you control.

## Brake Repair in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/brake-repair

### Shortlist two or three brake repair shops, describe the noise, pulling, or pedal feel you are noticing, and compare how each one explains the cause before recommending a fix.
### Common questions
### Q. Which brakes usually go bad first?
A.  Front brakes typically wear faster because they handle more of the stopping force during normal braking, especially in stop-and-go driving. Pads wear before rotors in most cases, so a shop should check pad thickness and rotor condition together rather than only replacing whichever part seems obviously worn.
### Q. What is the average lifespan of car brakes?
A.  Brake life depends heavily on driving style and conditions: stop-and-go city driving wears pads much faster than steady highway miles. Aggressive braking, towing, and hilly terrain also shorten lifespan. A shop can measure remaining pad and rotor thickness directly, which tells you far more than a general estimate.
### Q. How long does a brake repair take?
A.  A standard pad and rotor replacement usually takes under two hours once a bay is available, though drop-off wait times can add to that. More involved jobs, like caliper or brake line work, take longer. Ask for a time estimate upfront so you can plan your day around it.

## Breakfast & Brunch in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/breakfast-brunch

### Ask whether breakfast is served all day and whether reservations are taken, because weekend brunch is the busiest service most restaurants run.
### Common questions
### Q. What do you serve at a breakfast brunch?
A.  Build around one hot main, one baked item and one cold plate: eggs or a casserole, pastries or biscuits, and fruit with yogurt. Add a savory anchor such as bacon or sausage, coffee and juice, and one cocktail if you want a bar. Anything make-ahead saves the morning.
### Q. What’s a good time to host a brunch?
A.  Late morning works best, roughly between ten and noon, which lets guests sleep in and still leaves the afternoon open. Set a two to three hour window on the invitation. If you are going out instead, before nine or after one avoids the worst of the weekend wait.

A.  Pick dishes that hold: egg casseroles, baked oatmeal and anything you can assemble the night before. Set the drinks station away from the food so the line keeps moving, label anything with nuts or dairy, and put out more coffee than you think you need.

## Breweries in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/breweries

### A production brewery pours in a small taproom, a brewpub is a restaurant that brews, and a taproom without a kitchen often allows outside food.
### Common questions
### Q. What should I know before visiting a brewery for the first time?
A.  Check whether there is a kitchen, because many taprooms have none and either allow outside food or host a rotating truck. Order a flight to cover ground quickly, ask what was kegged most recently, and arrange a ride home. Many taprooms are family friendly early and busier later.
### Q. What is the easiest beer for a beginner?
A.  Light lagers, cream ales, wheat beers and fruited sours go down easiest, since they carry little bitterness. Hazy pale ales sit a step up, and roasty stouts or heavily hopped beers are usually an acquired taste. A flight lets you test four styles before committing to a full pour.
### Q. Is 7 beers in 2 hours a lot?
A.  Yes, that is a heavy pace. The body clears roughly one standard drink per hour, so anything faster stacks up rather than wearing off. Arrange a ride before the first pour, drink water between beers, and remember that taproom pours are often stronger than a standard lager.

A.  Something old, something new, something borrowed and something blue, from an old rhyme that closes with a sixpence in her shoe. It is tradition, not requirement. Most brides cover it with jewelry, a family heirloom, or a ribbon stitched inside the hem where nobody else sees it.
### Q. What does FoB mean in a wedding?
A.  Father of the bride. You will see it in planning threads and vendor paperwork alongside MoB for mother of the bride, FoG and MoG for the groom side. Salons use the shorthand when scheduling fittings and coordinating what the wedding party wears with the gown.

## Building Supplies in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/building-supplies

### Lumber yards usually beat big-box stores on grading consistency, advice and delivery, and most improve their pricing at volume even for a homeowner.
### Common questions
### Q. How to select building materials?
A.  Start with the load, the exposure and the code requirement for that part of the structure, then choose within what qualifies. Compare grade and moisture content, not just price, and confirm lead times early, since engineered and custom items drive most schedule delays.

A.  Concrete, wood, steel, brick, stone, cement, aggregate, glass, insulation and drywall cover most residential and commercial work. Most building supply dealers stock the common grades and special order the rest, so ask what is on the shelf before you plan around it.

## Burgers in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/burgers

### The cooking method decides the burger more than the toppings do, since a thin smash patty and a thick grilled pub patty are different products.
### Common questions
### Q. What is the key to a good burger?
A.  Fat content and heat. A patty with enough fat and a surface hot enough to build crust beats any topping list. After that it is seasoning on the outside right before cooking, a bun that holds up, and not pressing a grilled patty flat while it cooks.
### Q. What is the secret ingredient in a good burger?
A.  There is not one, and kitchens that grind their own beef will tell you the same. Salt on the outside just before cooking, coarse ground beef with real fat, and a hot flat-top or grill do the work. Ask whether the beef is ground in house.
### Q. What are the three types of burgers?
A.  There is no fixed set, but menus usually sort by how the patty is cooked. A smash patty is pressed thin on a flat-top and cooked through. A thick pub-style patty is grilled and can be served pink. Diner griddle patties sit between the two.

## Business Attorney in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/business-attorney

### Insist on a defined scope and deliverables rather than an open retainer, and ask who actually does the work, the person pitching or a junior.
### Common questions
### Q. What are good questions to ask a consultant?

### Q. What are the three C’s of consulting?

## Butcher in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/butcher

### A butcher cuts to order, so thickness, trim, grind blend and portion size are yours to specify rather than whatever happens to be in the case.
### Common questions
### Q. What are good questions to ask a butcher?
A.  Ask where the meat comes from, how long the beef has been aged and whether that was wet or dry, and what came in fresh today. Ask what they can cut to order, whether they grind to your blend, and how much notice large or holiday orders need.

## Cafes in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/cafes

### Cafes serve two crowds and rarely both equally, so if you plan to stay, check outlets, wifi, table size, noise and any busy-period time limit.
### Common questions
### Q. What is a fancy word for cafe?
A.  Coffeehouse, espresso bar, bistro, brasserie, patisserie and tearoom all get used. The word usually signals the offering: a patisserie leads with pastry, a bistro serves full plates, an espresso bar is built for a quick standing coffee. Read the name as a hint about what the visit will be.
### Q. What does Gen Z look for in a coffee shop?
A.  Somewhere worth staying: outlets, seating that suits a laptop or a group, and wifi that holds up. Mobile ordering, non-dairy milk options and clear sourcing information matter too, along with a room that photographs well. Cafes courting that crowd usually advertise all of it on the door.
### Q. Is it okay to sit in a cafe without buying anything?
A.  Etiquette depends on how busy the space is and how long you plan to stay. During a quiet stretch, resting at a table for a short while is usually fine, but during a busy rush, tables are meant for paying customers, so buy something small or free up the seat for others.

## Cajun Food in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/cajun-food

### Shortlist two or three Cajun kitchens, ask what goes into their roux and seasoning, and compare that against the plate that actually lands on your table.
### Common questions
### Q. What is the difference between Cajun food and Creole food?
A.  Cajun cooking grew out of rural Acadian settlers and leans on rustic, one-pot dishes built from local ingredients, while Creole cooking developed in the city and often adds tomatoes and richer, layered sauces. Many kitchens blend both traditions, so the line between them can blur on a menu.
### Q. What is the holy trinity of Cajun food?
A.  The holy trinity refers to onion, celery, and bell pepper cooked together as the flavor base for gumbo, jambalaya, and many other dishes. It plays a role similar to mirepoix in French cooking, giving Cajun food its familiar aromatic backbone before other ingredients are added to the pot.
### Q. What to bring to a Cajun potluck?
A.  A hearty side or dessert travels well and is always appreciated, since the main dishes like gumbo or jambalaya are often handled by the host. Bringing your own serving spoon and a dish that holds up at room temperature makes things easier for everyone at the table.

## Campgrounds in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/campgrounds

### Sites differ by what they supply: primitive has no hookups, standard adds water and electric, and full hookup adds sewer for RVs.
### Common questions
### Q. What is the 3-3-3 rule when camping?
A.  A travel guideline for RV campers: drive no more than about three hundred miles in a day, arrive by three in the afternoon, and stay at least three nights. It keeps setup out of the dark and turns a drive-through trip into an actual stay.
### Q. What is the 200 rule for camping?
A.  A leave-no-trace guideline: camp, wash dishes, and bury human waste at least two hundred feet from any lake, stream or spring. That distance keeps soap, food scraps and waste out of the water. Many campgrounds also require using established sites rather than clearing a new one.
### Q. What not to bring on a camping trip?
A.  Firewood from home, since transporting it moves tree-killing pests and many campgrounds ban it outright. Also leave behind scented toiletries and food stored loose, anything glass, and speakers you plan to run past quiet hours. Check the fire ban before packing anything that burns.

### Shortlist two or three candy shops worth visiting, decide what treats and selection you want, then compare that against what each shop actually stocks and offers.
### Common questions

A.  Look for a shop with a wide selection, fresh stock, and staff who know their inventory. Check if they carry the treats you actually want, from bulk bins to specialty imports, and read recent reviews for cleanliness and service before you commit to becoming a regular customer.
### Q. What exactly is a candy shop?
A.  A candy shop is a retail store that specializes in sweets, offering bulk bins, packaged treats, and often handmade or imported items you will not find at a general store. ### Q. What candy to stay away from?

Check expiration dates on chocolate and gummies, and read labels closely if you have food allergies, since cross contact with nuts or dairy is common in bulk bins. ## Cannabis Store in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/cannabis-store

### Bring valid government photo identification, know whether the store is medical or recreational, and ask about form and dosage rather than potency alone.
### Common questions
### Q. How to tell if cannabis is high quality?
A.  Look and smell. Quality flower is trimmed neatly, feels slightly sticky rather than dry and crumbling, and carries a strong fresh aroma; a harsh, hay-like smell suggests age or poor curing. Check the label for the testing lab, the packaging or harvest date, and cannabinoid content.
### Q. What to buy at dispensary for beginners?
A.  Start with a low dose and a form you can control. Ask the budtender about onset and duration rather than potency alone, since edibles can take up to two hours to take effect and are where people overdo it. Bring valid government photo identification, because everyone is carded.
### Q. Is sativa or indica better for beginners?
A.  Neither label is a reliable predictor. The split describes plant type more than effect, and what you experience depends on the individual, the product and the dose. Describe what you want to a budtender, ask about form and dosage, and start low regardless of what the label says.

## Car Dealerships in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/car-dealerships

### Negotiate the out-the-door price rather than the monthly payment, since a payment can be made to look good by stretching the term over more years.
### Common questions
### Q. What not to tell a dealership when buying a car?
A.  Avoid leading with a monthly payment target, a trade-in, or the fact that you have no other options. Settle the out-the-door price first, then raise the trade separately, then financing. Bring your own loan quote so the dealer offer has something to be measured against.
### Q. What is the red flag rule for car dealers?
A.  It is a federal requirement, not a negotiating tactic. Dealers that arrange financing must run a written identity theft prevention program that spots warning signs of fraud in credit applications. It is why a dealer asks for identification and may pause a deal when application details do not match.
### Q. How to outsmart a car dealership?
A.  Do the work before you arrive. Get financing quoted elsewhere, shortlist two or three dealers worth contacting, ask each for an out-the-door figure on the same vehicle, and compare those. For used cars, ask for the history report and arrange an independent pre-purchase inspection.

## Car Insurance in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/car-insurance

### Compare on coverage limits rather than the monthly premium, since state minimum liability is usually far below what a serious accident actually costs.
### Common questions
### Q. How to decide what car insurance is right for you?
A.  Compare on coverage limits first, not the monthly premium. Look at bodily injury and property damage liability, then uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage, then the deductibles on collision and comprehensive. Quote the same limits at every company so the numbers are comparable, and confirm what each policy excludes.
### Q. What are 5 important questions to ask your car insurance agent?
A.  What are my liability limits and what would exceed them. Which discounts am I eligible for that are not applied. Is a rental car covered while my vehicle is repaired. Does the policy cover delivery or rideshare driving. How does a claim affect my renewal, and is the agent independent or captive.
### Q. Is it better to carry comprehensive or collision?
A.  They cover different events, so it is not a choice between them. Collision responds to impact with another vehicle or object. Comprehensive responds to theft, fire, hail, flood, falling objects, animal strikes and glass. Lenders and leasing companies generally require both while the vehicle is financed.

## Car Rental in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/car-rental

### Shortlist two or three rental counters, ask about mileage limits, insurance, and fuel policy, and compare that against the total you actually pay at pickup.
### Common questions
### Q. What questions should I ask before renting a car?
A.  Ask about mileage limits, what insurance you already have through your own policy or card, fuel return rules, and any fee for an additional driver. Confirming pickup and drop-off times in writing also helps avoid a surprise late charge when you return the vehicle a little late.
### Q. What are the hidden fees when renting a car?
A.  Common extra charges include underage driver fees, airport location surcharges, additional driver fees, and steep refueling charges if the tank is not returned full. Reading the full agreement before signing, not just the advertised rate, is the best way to see the true total cost.
### Q. Should you prepay for gas when renting a car?
A.  Prepaying locks in a rate but only pays off if you plan to return the car close to empty, since unused fuel is not refunded. If you can return it full yourself, skipping the prepay option and refueling nearby right before drop-off is usually the cheaper choice.

## Car Wash in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/car-wash

### The three wash types treat paint differently: touchless is gentlest on delicate finishes, soft-cloth cleans better, and hand washing is the slowest but the most careful.
### Common questions
### Q. What is the least damaging car wash?
A.  Touchless is the least likely to scratch, because nothing but water and detergent touches the finish. It trades that for stronger chemistry and a film left behind on heavy dirt. A careful hand wash with two buckets and a clean mitt is gentler still, and far slower.
### Q. How to tell if a car wash is good?
A.  Watch the cars coming out instead of reading the sign. Streaks, water spotting on glass, and dirt still sitting along lower panels and rocker trim mean weak rinsing or tired equipment. Check that cloth strips look clean rather than gritty, that dryers actually dry, and that the vacuums work.
### Q. When should you not get a carwash?
A.  Skip it on fresh paint or a new clear coat repair, on a vinyl wrap the shop has not cleared, and when trim, mirrors or a windshield are already loose or cracked. In freezing weather, wash midday and dry the door seals so nothing locks shut.

## Cardiologists in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/cardiologists

### Chest pain, pressure, shortness of breath, fainting or a racing heart with sweating are emergency symptoms; call 911 rather than booking a cardiology appointment.
### Common questions
### Q. How do you know if a cardiologist is good?
A.  Check board certification in cardiology and the subspecialty that fits your issue, whether general, interventional, electrophysiology or heart failure. Look at hospital affiliation, since that determines where any procedure happens. In the room, a good sign is a doctor who explains the test options and what each result changes.
### Q. What not to do before seeing a cardiologist?

### Q. Why does a cardiologist look at your hands?

A physician may check nail bed color and capillary refill, look for clubbing of the fingertips, splinter hemorrhages under the nails, swelling and temperature, and compare pulse strength at both wrists. It is a quick part of the physical exam, not a diagnosis on its own.

## Carpet Cleaning in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/carpet-cleaning

### Hot water extraction cleans deepest but leaves carpet damp for hours, while low-moisture encapsulation dries in an hour or two and suits light soiling.
### Common questions
### Q. What type of carpet cleaning is most effective?
A.  Hot water extraction removes the most soil, which is why it is the method usually recommended for deep cleaning. Low-moisture encapsulation is the better call for light soiling, quick turnarounds and rooms you need back the same day. Match the method to the job, not the marketing.
### Q. What are the common mistakes in carpet cleaning?
A.  Over-wetting, using too much detergent and leaving residue that attracts dirt back within weeks. Scrubbing a spill instead of blotting sets it. Walking on damp carpet in street shoes undoes the work. For pet odor, cleaning only the surface fails, because the source is usually the pad beneath.
### Q. What are the disadvantages of steam carpet cleaning?
A.  Drying time is the main one: hours, sometimes most of a day, and furniture has to stay off the carpet until it is dry. Poor extraction can leave the backing wet enough to smell or, rarely, to shrink some carpet. Ask what airflow the crew leaves behind.

## Carpeting in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/carpeting

### The installed price is the only number worth comparing, and it should cover carpet, pad, tack strip, transitions, furniture moving and removal of the old floor.
### Common questions
### Q. What to avoid when buying carpet?
A.  Avoid comparing quotes that are not installed prices. The number should include carpet, pad, tack strip, transitions, furniture moving and haul away of the old floor. Also avoid pairing good carpet with a cheap pad, and check how stairs are charged, since they are usually billed per step.
### Q. Should your carpet be lighter or darker than your walls?
A.  Either works, so decide on light and traffic rather than a rule. Darker carpet hides soil in busy areas and grounds a room with pale walls; lighter carpet opens a small or dim space. Take samples home and look at them in the actual room at different times of day.
### Q. Is 20 year old carpet unhealthy?
A.  It can be. Carpet that old holds dust, dander and allergens that vacuuming does not fully remove, and the pad underneath has usually flattened and broken down. Replace it sooner if there is a lingering odor, visible matting, or any history of water damage underneath.

## Chicken Wings in the St. Louis Metro

### Common questions
### Q. What are the two types of chicken wings called?
A.  Chicken wings are typically split into two parts for cooking: the flat, which has two thin bones and a rectangular shape, and the drumette, which looks like a miniature drumstick. Some restaurants serve both mixed together, while others let you order a specific type by request.
### Q. Which wings are better, flats or drums?
A.  It comes down to preference: flats have more surface area for sauce and are easier to eat neatly, while drums offer more meat and a familiar handheld shape. Ordering a mixed batch is a simple way to compare both before deciding which one you reach for first.
### Q. What are the different cuts of chicken wings?
A.  A whole wing breaks down into three parts: the drumette, the flat, and the wingtip, which is usually trimmed off before cooking since it has little meat. Most menus serve drumettes and flats, either separately or mixed, while the tip is often saved for stock instead.

## Childcare in the St. Louis Metro

### For any licensed provider, ask to see the license and the most recent inspection report, then check ratios, staff turnover, background checks and the illness policy.
### Common questions
### Q. What are some important questions to ask when choosing a daycare?

## Children's Clothing in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/childrens-clothing

### Shortlist two or three childrens clothing shops, ask about sizing, fabric, and return policy, and compare that against how the pieces actually hold up in wash.
### Common questions
### Q. Is a size 4 the same as 5T?
A.  No, these come from two different systems. Regular sizing like 4 or 5 is cut for a leaner, taller kid frame, while toddler sizing like 5T is cut fuller through the middle for a younger build. Checking the size chart for each brand is the surest way to get a proper fit.
### Q. Does a 2 year old wear 2T or 3T?
A.  It depends on the individual child, since kids of the same age can vary quite a bit in height and build. As a general guide, 2T tends to fit a smaller or younger toddler while 3T fits a taller or older one. Check the brand size chart and try items on when you can.
### Q. How much clothes do kids actually need?
A.  Most families do fine with about a week of everyday outfits, a couple dressier pieces, proper outerwear for the season, and enough sleepwear to get through laundry day. Kids grow fast, so buying too much at once often means unworn items get outgrown before they are ever used. Buy in small batches instead.

## Chimney Sweep in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/chimney-sweep

### Shortlist two or three chimney sweeps, ask how they inspect the flue and handle soot, and compare that against the cleanup you actually get afterward.
### Common questions
### Q. How do I choose a good chimney sweep?
A.  Look for a sweep certified by a recognized chimney safety organization who will inspect the full flue, not just brush the firebox opening. A written summary of what they found, including any cracks or creosote buildup, shows they are being thorough rather than rushing through the visit.
### Q. What is the 3-2-10 rule for chimneys?
A.  This is a common guideline for chimney height: the top should extend at least 3 feet above the roof penetration, and at least 2 feet higher than anything within 10 feet of it. Getting this height right helps smoke and sparks clear the roofline safely instead of drifting back down.
### Q. What happens if you never clean your chimney?
A.  Creosote and soot build up along the flue walls, raising the risk of a chimney fire and blocking proper airflow. Over time this can also let more moisture and animals into the structure, so regular sweeping protects both the safety of the fireplace and the chimney itself.

## Chinese Food in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/chinese-food

### Chinese cooking is strongly regional, so ask how hot a dish actually is and ask for the separate menu if the kitchen keeps one.
### Common questions
### Q. How many dishes should I order at a Chinese restaurant?
A.  A common rule for family style is one dish per person plus one extra for the table, with rice separate. Balance the order rather than doubling up: something braised or saucy, something crisp, a vegetable and a soup. For two people, two dishes and rice is plenty.
### Q. How to figure out if a Chinese restaurant is good?
A.  Ask whether there is a second menu and order from it. A kitchen cooking one region well beats one listing everything, tables ordering dishes you do not recognize is a strong signal, and staff who will tell you honestly how hot something is usually cook honestly too.
### Q. What is the healthiest dish to order in a Chinese restaurant?
A.  Steamed or braised beats fried, and asking for sauce on the side cuts most of the sodium and sugar. Look for dishes built on vegetables and lean protein, choose steamed rice over fried, and split one order between two people rather than eating a full portion alone.

## Civil Law Attorney in the St. Louis Metro

### Shortlist two or three civil law attorneys, ask about their experience with cases like yours, and compare that against how clearly each one explains your options.
### Common questions
### Q. How much does a civil lawyer usually cost?
A.  Fees vary based on the complexity of the case, how it is billed, and how much time it takes to resolve, so a single number rarely applies. Ask each attorney to explain their fee structure and what is included before you decide, so you can compare options clearly.
### Q. What not to tell the attorney?

## Clothing in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/clothing

### Check fiber content, seam finishing, pattern matching and fabric recovery before the price tag, because measurements beat size labels across brands every time.
### Common questions
### Q. What is the 3-3-3 rule for clothes?
A.  It is a wardrobe exercise: pick three tops, three bottoms and three pairs of shoes, then build every outfit for a stretch of days from only those nine pieces. It exposes which items actually earn their space and which colors in your closet refuse to work together.
### Q. How to find the right clothing style for you?
A.  Start from the clothes you already reach for and name what they share: fit, neckline, fabric weight, color family. Photograph the outfits that work. Then buy to measurements rather than size labels, and budget for alterations, because fit reads as style far more than any label does.
### Q. What two colors should not be worn together?
A.  No pairing is truly banned, and the old rules about navy with black or brown with black are mostly gone. What actually looks off is two shades so close they read as a mistake, or two loud saturated colors at equal strength. Let one carry, the other support.

## Comic Books in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/comic-books

### Condition drives value, so for anything expensive ask whether the book has been professionally graded and whether it has been restored, which changes value substantially.
### Common questions
### Q. What is the 180 rule in comics?
A.  It is a staging convention borrowed from film. Artists keep the imaginary camera on one side of a line drawn between two characters, so those characters stay on consistent sides of the panel and the action reads clearly instead of appearing to flip between panels.
### Q. What is the main purpose of a comic book?
A.  A comic book tells a story primarily through sequential art, pairing images with dialogue and captions so plot and emotion come across visually rather than through prose alone. Beyond entertainment, the format has been used for education, satire and cultural commentary, and it remains a serious collecting hobby for many readers.
### Q. How much does it cost to get comics appraised?
A.  Cost depends on the appraiser, how many books are evaluated, and whether you want a casual opinion or a written appraisal for insurance or resale. Some shops give informal estimates at no charge, while a certified appraiser usually charges a per item or hourly fee. Ask upfront what documentation is included.

## Commercial Real Estate in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/commercial-real-estate

### The lease structure decides your real cost: gross rent bundles most expenses, while triple net adds taxes, insurance and common area maintenance on top of base rent.
### Common questions
### Q. What are some good questions to ask when buying commercial real estate?
A.  Ask about zoning and permitted use for your business, the condition of roof, structure and mechanical systems, and what the current operating expenses actually run. Ask about existing tenants and lease terms you inherit, environmental history of the site, and access, parking and loading. Have an attorney review before signing.
### Q. What are the seven key characteristics of real estate?
A.  Three are physical: property cannot be moved, land cannot be destroyed, and no two parcels are identical. Four are economic: scarcity, the effect of improvements, permanence of investment, and area preference, meaning the pull of one location over another. Together they explain why identical buildings rarely carry identical value.
### Q. What are the risks of owning commercial property?
A.  Vacancy risk sits at the center, since a single empty unit can wipe out months of income, especially with fewer tenants than a residential building. Add exposure to shifting demand for the property type you own, maintenance costs that fall on the owner, financing that resets at higher rates, and tenant defaults.

## Computers in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/computers

### For repair, ask for a diagnostic fee up front and whether it applies to the work, and back up your own data before handing the machine over.
### Common questions
### Q. What are five things to consider when buying a computer?
A.  Match the machine to the work rather than the spec sheet. Consider memory, storage size, screen and keyboard quality, battery life, and whether the parts can be upgraded later. Memory and storage matter more than raw processor speed for most people, and both are hard to change on modern laptops.
### Q. What is the easiest computer for an older person to use?
A.  The easiest machine is usually the one that matches what the person already knows, so keep the same operating system if there is one. Beyond that, look for a large bright screen, a full-size keyboard, and a local shop that will set it up and answer questions later.
### Q. What laptop to stay away from?
A.  Avoid machines sold at the minimum specification, since memory and storage are soldered on most modern laptops and cannot be increased later. Also be wary of anything with no local repair support or no parts availability. Ask a shop what it can actually service before you buy.

## Concrete in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/concrete

### A compacted sub-base and correct thickness matter more to whether a slab cracks than the finish does, so ask about the base as much as the pour.
### Common questions
### Q. What questions should you ask a concrete contractor?
A.  Ask about sub-base preparation and compaction, slab thickness, reinforcement, and where control joints will be cut and how far apart. Ask about curing and sealing, what the warranty covers, and whether a permit is required for the work you want.
### Q. How to pick a concrete contractor?
A.  Shortlist two or three and talk to each one. Say what you want, where it goes and how you expect it to hold up, then compare that against what each is prepared to deliver. Confirm licensing and insurance, and get the scope in writing.
### Q. What is the 421 rule for concrete?
A.  It describes a common hand mixed proportion of four parts gravel, two parts sand and one part cement, plus water. Ready mix delivered to a site is batched to a specified strength instead, which is what a contractor should be quoting for structural work.

## Cosmetic Dentists in the St. Louis Metro

### Cosmetic dentistry is not a recognized specialty, so judge on before-and-after cases the dentist treated personally and on how often they do your procedure.
### Common questions
### Q. What are some red flags that might indicate a dentist is bad?
A.  Stock before-and-after photos rather than their own cases, pressure to decide the same day, a treatment plan that jumps straight to veneers or crowns when something reversible would do, and vague answers about how many of your procedure they do each year or what replacement will cost later.
### Q. What’s the difference between a regular dentist and a cosmetic dentist?
A.  Training is the same. Cosmetic dentistry is not a recognized dental specialty, so any general dentist may use the term. What separates them is case volume and focus, so judge on before-and-after work they treated themselves and on how often they do your specific procedure.

A.  Not on their own. A veneer does not stop decay, so the tooth underneath can decay at the margin if brushing, flossing and checkups slip. Veneers and crowns also remove tooth structure permanently and have a finite lifespan, so ask what replacement involves before you commit.

## Counselor in the St. Louis Metro

## Courthouses in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/courthouses

### Confirm which courthouse and division handles your matter before you go, since civil, criminal, family, probate and traffic cases are often heard in separate buildings.
### Common questions
### Q. What are the three main types of courts?
A.  Courts are usually grouped as trial courts, appellate courts, and a court of last resort. Trial courts hear evidence and decide cases, appellate courts review those decisions for legal error, and the highest court takes a limited number of appeals. Clerks can explain procedure but cannot give legal advice.
### Q. Can I just walk into a courtroom?
A.  Usually yes. Most court proceedings are open to the public, though juvenile, adoption and sealed matters are not, and a judge can close a hearing. Expect airport-style security screening at the door, leave weapons at home, and check the posted rules on phones, cameras and recording before you enter.
### Q. What to never say to a judge in court?
A.  Avoid interrupting, arguing, sarcasm and anything you cannot support. Address the judge as Your Honor, answer only the question asked, and do not speak while someone else is speaking. If you have a lawyer, let them talk. Guessing on the record is worse than saying you do not know.

## Credit Unions in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/credit-unions

### A credit union is a not-for-profit cooperative owned by its members, which is why loan rates and fees often run lower and savings rates higher.
### Common questions
### Q. What is the downside of using a credit union?
A.  Branch and ATM reach was the historical drawback, along with a smaller product menu and sometimes slower technology. Shared branching and surcharge-free ATM networks answer most of the access problem, so confirm which networks a given credit union belongs to before you move anything.
### Q. Is my money safer in a bank or a credit union?
A.  Both carry federal deposit insurance at the same coverage level per depositor, per institution, per ownership category — banks through one federal agency and credit unions through another. Safety comes down to confirming the institution is federally insured and that your balances sit within the coverage limits.
### Q. What happens to my money if a credit union fails?
A.  Insured deposits are protected up to the federal coverage limit, and members are typically made whole quickly, often because another credit union assumes the accounts and the money simply moves. Anything above the coverage limit is the part at risk, which is why the limit is worth knowing before you deposit.

## Dance Schools in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/dance-schools

### Recreational classes, competition teams and adult social dance differ enormously in commitment, so ask how students are placed by level rather than age before enrolling.
### Common questions
### Q. Why do dancers go 5 6 7 8?
A.  Music for most dance styles is organized in eight-count phrases. Counting the back half of that phrase out loud gives the room a shared start point and sets tempo, so everyone lands on the same beat without the teacher stopping and restarting the track.
### Q. What are some questions to ask about dance?
A.  Ask how instructors were trained, how classes are leveled, and how large a class gets. Ask what a full year costs once recital costumes, tickets and photos are counted, whether the floor is sprung, and what happens if your child wants to stop mid-season.
### Q. What is the hardest dance style to learn?
A.  Ballet gets named most often, since the technique is unforgiving and progress is measured in years rather than months. Tap and fast percussive styles are close behind for footwork speed. The harder truth is that any style is difficult at a high level and forgiving at a beginner one.

## Dance Studios in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/dance-studios

### Recreational classes, competition teams and adult social dance are very different commitments, since competition adds travel, costumes and fees well beyond tuition.
### Common questions
### Q. How to pick a dance studio?

### Q. Why do dancers go 5 6 7 8?
A.  Most dance music is counted in groups of eight, so the second half of a count gives everyone a shared entry point. Calling out the back half sets tempo and marks exactly where the movement starts, which keeps a room of dancers together without stopping the music.
### Q. What are the 7 most popular types of dance?
A.  Ballet, tap, jazz, hip hop, contemporary, ballroom and salsa cover most class schedules. Ballet is the usual foundation and shows up inside the others. Studios differ in which they teach well, so ask which styles the studio is actually known for rather than which appear on the list.

## Day Spas in the St. Louis Metro

### A day spa offers massage, facials and nail services from licensed staff, unlike a medical spa, which works under physician supervision and offers injectables and lasers.

### Q. What are red flags to watch for at a spa?

## Delis in the St. Louis Metro

A.  A large treatment plan presented on a first visit with no images or explanation, pressure to decide the same day, vague answers about cost and insurance, or reluctance to give you your own records and X-rays when you ask for them.
### Q. What is the 2 2 2 rule in dentistry?
A.  It is a shorthand for brushing twice a day for two minutes each time and seeing a dentist twice a year. It is a general baseline, not a clinical standard, and a dentist may set a different visit schedule based on your history.
### Q. What destroys teeth the most?
A.  Frequency matters more than quantity: sugary or acidic drinks sipped over hours keep enamel under acid attack far longer than the same amount at one sitting. Plaque left along the gumline, dry mouth from medications, and grinding also do steady damage.

## Department Stores in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/department-stores

### The advantage is breadth under one roof plus services that are easy to overlook: alterations, personal shopping, gift registry and in-store pickup for online orders.

A.  Full line stores carry apparel, home, beauty and often furniture under one roof. Discount department stores add groceries and hard goods at lower price points. Upscale stores narrow the range and add service. Off price chains sell overstock and past season goods, with thinner sizes and no reorder.
### Q. Where do wealthy people buy their clothes?
A.  Mostly the same upscale department stores and designer boutiques anyone can walk into, plus tailors and made to measure. The difference is service rather than the door: a personal shopper who keeps your sizes, private appointments, alterations included, and early access before a season hits the floor.
### Q. What do you get at a department store?
A.  One stop access to clothing, shoes, home goods, cosmetics and often a bit of furniture, all organized into distinct departments under a single roof. Many also offer services worth asking about directly, including alterations, gift registry, personal shopping help, and pickup counters for orders placed online ahead of a visit.

## Departments Of Motor Vehicles in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/departments-of-motor-vehicles

### Check whether your office takes appointments and bring more documentation than you think you need, since originals are usually required rather than copies.
### Common questions
### Q. Are all DMVs the same?
A.  No. Offices differ in what they handle, since licensing and vehicle registration are often split between separate locations with separate hours. Appointment policies, accepted payment methods and which document copies are accepted also vary by office, so confirm all of that with the specific branch before you go.
### Q. What color not to wear for driver’s license?

A.  Sometimes, and only while you are still at the counter. Many offices will take a second photo if you ask before the record is finalized, but once the card is issued you are usually paying a duplicate fee for a new one. Ask at the camera, not afterward.

## Dermatologists in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/dermatologists

### Medical dermatology such as skin cancer screening, acne and mole checks is generally covered by insurance, while cosmetic work such as fillers and lasers usually is not.
### Common questions
### Q. What is a red flag in dermatology?
A.  A mole that is asymmetric, has an irregular border, uneven color, is larger than a pencil eraser or is changing. Also a sore that will not heal, a spot that itches or bleeds, and any lesion that looks different from the rest. Say those words when booking to be triaged sooner.
### Q. Is a do or MD better for dermatology?
A.  Neither is better. Both complete medical school, a dermatology residency and board certification, and both are fully licensed physicians. What matters is board certification, how often the practice treats your condition, and whether biopsies are read by a dermatopathologist. Verify the license through the state board.
### Q. What are the four types of dermatologists?
A.  Generally medical, surgical, cosmetic and pediatric, with dermatopathology as the lab specialty that reads biopsies. Many practices cover more than one. Say which you are booking, because a cosmetic visit and a medical visit are coded and billed differently, and a mole check may need a different appointment length.

## Desserts in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/desserts

### Dessert places specialize: patisserie and cake, ice cream and frozen custard, pastry and pie, or a late-night dessert bar with plated courses.
### Common questions
### Q. Can you give me some questions about desserts?
A.  Useful ones to ask a dessert shop: what is made in house that day, how far ahead a cake must be ordered, and how it travels, since buttercream holds up in heat far better than whipped cream or mousse. For allergies, ask about shared equipment rather than only ingredients.
### Q. What are the 9 common desserts?
A.  Lists vary, but the ones named most often are cake, pie, cookies, brownies, ice cream, cheesecake, pudding or custard, doughnuts, and fruit-based desserts such as cobbler or tart. Most shops specialize in one or two of these rather than doing all of them well.
### Q. What’s a dessert that everyone loves?
A.  For a group, ice cream or frozen custard is the safest pick, because everyone chooses a flavor and portions scale easily. Warm chocolate desserts and fruit cobbler are close behind. Order one dairy-free or fruit-based option alongside, and ask about shared equipment if anyone has a nut allergy.

## Diagnostic Imaging in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/diagnostic-imaging

### A freestanding imaging center often costs far less than a hospital outpatient department for the identical scan, because the hospital adds a facility fee.
### Common questions
### Q. What are different types of diagnostic imaging?
A.  The common ones are X-ray, ultrasound, CT, MRI, mammography, nuclear medicine and PET. Each shows different tissue: X-ray and CT are strongest on bone and lungs, MRI on soft tissue and the nervous system, ultrasound on organs and blood flow without radiation.
### Q. What are some common questions I should ask about radiology?
A.  Ask whether the scan needs prior authorization, what the cash price is alongside the insured price, and who reads the images. Also ask how quickly results reach your doctor, whether prior scans should be sent for comparison, and how to obtain a copy of the images.
### Q. Which gives better imaging, CT or MRI?
A.  Neither is better overall, they answer different questions. CT is fast and excellent for bone, bleeding, lungs and emergencies, but uses radiation. MRI gives far more detail in soft tissue, the brain and joints, takes much longer, and is loud and enclosed. Your doctor orders the one that fits.

A.  Breakfast items tend to be the most ordered, especially eggs, pancakes, and omelets, since diners built their reputation on serving breakfast any time of day. Classic lunch plates like a burger and fries also stay popular, giving most diners a strong pull at both ends of the day.

## Doctors in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/doctors

### Confirm the practice is accepting new patients and in your insurance network with the office itself, then ask how refills and messages are handled between visits.
### Common questions
### Q. What are red flags for a doctor?
A.  Practice level warnings rather than medical ones: a doctor who interrupts before you finish, dismisses a symptom without examining it, cannot explain the reason for a test, or leaves no way to ask a question between visits. Disorganized records and unreturned refill requests count too.
### Q. What are 10 questions to ask a doctor?
A.  What is this, and what else could it be. What is the test for and when do results arrive. What are the options, and what happens if I wait. How will this interact with my other medications. What side effects should I watch for. When should I come back.
### Q. Why do doctors ask to see your tongue?
A.  The tongue and the back of the throat are the easiest window into hydration, swelling, coating and color changes, plus the tonsils. Asking you to stick it out also tests one of the cranial nerves, since a tongue that pulls to one side signals a problem worth checking.

A.  Glazed yeast donuts consistently top preference lists for their light texture and simple sweetness, followed closely by chocolate frosted and jelly-filled varieties. Popularity still comes down to personal taste, so sample a few types from a shop that bakes fresh throughout the day rather than once each morning.
### Q. What is the #1 donut in America?

### Q. What is the healthiest type of donut to eat?
A.  No donut is truly a health food, but baked or whole grain options with less sugar glaze tend to be lighter than deep fried, cream filled varieties. Portion size matters more than type, so pair a smaller donut with protein and treat it as an occasional item, not breakfast.

## Driving Schools in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/driving-schools

### Confirm the school is state-licensed and that its course satisfies the requirement you actually need, since teen, adult refresher and court-ordered classes differ.
### Common questions
### Q. What are some red flags for a driving instructor?
A.  No state license or certification, no written curriculum, and vague answers about hours and pricing. Also watch for a car without dual controls or visible insurance, cancelled or shortened lessons, texting or shouting behind the wheel, and pressure to prepay a large package before a single lesson.
### Q. Does it matter which driving school I take?
A.  It matters for the certificate. Confirm the course satisfies the exact requirement you need, whether that is a teen program tied to a permit, an adult refresher, or a court-ordered class, because those are different certificates. It also matters whether the school supplies a car for the road test.
### Q. What is the hardest part of driving school?
A.  For most students it is behind the wheel rather than the classroom, and usually highway merging, judging gaps in traffic, and parking maneuvers such as parallel and reverse. Nerves during the test itself are the other common hurdle. Extra supervised practice hours fix both faster than more theory.

## Drugstores in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/drugstores

### Pricing for the identical generic varies between pharmacies, so ask for the cash price as well — it is sometimes lower than your copay.
### Common questions
### Q. How to pick a preferred pharmacy?
A.  Check which pharmacies your plan lists as preferred, since that tier usually costs less. Then compare hours, whether they deliver or sync your refills, and how easy it is to reach a pharmacist. Using one pharmacy lets them catch interactions across everything you take.
### Q. What are red flags for pharmacists?
A.  Pharmacists are legally required to check prescriptions for signs such as early refills, overlapping controlled substances from several prescribers, and unusual doses. If you are asked questions at the counter, it is a routine verification step, not an accusation, and answering plainly usually resolves it.
### Q. Which is better for prescriptions, CVS or Walgreens?
A.  Neither wins across the board. What matters is whether the pharmacy is preferred under your plan, the cash price for your specific drug, the hours, and the wait. Independent pharmacies often beat both on price and on service, so check one nearby before defaulting to a chain.

A.  Many elder law attorneys offer a free or low cost initial consultation to discuss your situation before any fees apply. After that, billing varies by attorney and case type. Ask upfront how they charge, what the first meeting covers, and whether a flat fee applies to simple matters.

## Electricians in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/electricians

### Confirm the license and insurance, and know that panel work, service upgrades, new circuits and EV charger installs typically need a permit and an inspection.
### Common questions
### Q. How to tell if an electrician is good?
A.  The license and insurance check out, the person on site is a licensed electrician rather than an unsupervised apprentice, and permits get pulled for panel work, service upgrades, new circuits and EV chargers. Anyone offering to skip the permit and inspection is the wrong hire.
### Q. What are good questions to ask an electrician?

### Q. Do electricians expect a tip?
A.  No. Licensed trades price the job, and tipping is not part of the transaction. If the work was good, a detailed review, a referral and calling the same company back are worth far more to them. Coffee or cold drinks on a long job are always welcome.

## Employment Agencies in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/employment-agencies

### A legitimate agency is paid by the employer, never by you, so be cautious of anyone charging a job seeker a placement fee.
### Common questions
### Q. What are red flags to watch for in job agencies?
A.  Any fee charged to you, vague answers about which employers they place into, or a refusal to name the client before you interview. Sending your resume out without asking first is a serious one, as are pay rates that keep changing.
### Q. What questions should I ask an employment agency?
A.  Ask whether the role is direct hire, temp, or temp to hire, since that decides who employs you and which benefits apply. Ask which employers and industries they actually place into, who handles payroll and taxes, and whether a conversion fee applies.
### Q. What not to tell a recruiter?
A.  Do not give a current salary figure you are not required to share, and do not name the lowest offer you would accept, because that becomes the ceiling. Do not authorize blanket resume submissions, and keep confidential details about your current employer to yourself.

## Employment Attorney in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/employment-attorney

### Employment claims run on short deadlines, since discrimination charges often must be filed with an agency within months, so ask about your deadline on the first call.
### Common questions
### Q. What not to say to an employment lawyer?
A.  There is nothing you should hide. Leaving out the unfavorable facts is what damages a case, because the other side will find them anyway. Avoid guessing at dates or exaggerating what was said. Bring your offer letter, handbook, written warnings and your own dated notes instead.
### Q. What is the cost of an employment attorney?
A.  Fee structure varies more than the total. Some employee-side cases run on contingency, meaning the fee comes out of any recovery; others bill hourly against a retainer, and a document review may be flat fee. Ask which applies to your matter and whether filing and expert costs are billed separately.
### Q. When to get an employment lawyer involved?
A.  Contact one as soon as you suspect discrimination, harassment, retaliation, wrongful termination or a wage dispute, since evidence and witness memory fade quickly and many claims carry short filing deadlines. It is also worth a call before signing a severance agreement, since that document can waive rights you did not realize you had.

## Endodontists in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/endodontists

### Shortlist two or three endodontists, ask about their experience with cases like yours, and compare that against how clearly each one explains the treatment plan.
### Common questions
### Q. How do you know if an endodontist is good?
A.  Look for board certification, clear before and after explanations of your treatment, and a willingness to discuss options like retreatment versus extraction. A good endodontist also uses updated imaging technology and takes time to answer your questions rather than rushing through the appointment.
### Q. Is it better to have a root canal done by a dentist or endodontist?
A.  A general dentist can handle many straightforward root canals, but an endodontist specializes in this exact procedure and handles more complex root systems every day. For a difficult tooth, a curved canal, or a retreatment case, the added specialty training often makes a real difference.
### Q. Do roots grow back after a root canal?
A.  No, once the nerve and pulp tissue are removed and the canal is sealed, that tissue does not regenerate. The tooth still relies on the surrounding bone and ligament for support, which is why keeping up with regular checkups after treatment still matters for the long term.

## Estate Planning Attorney in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/estate-planning-attorney

### A basic plan usually means more than a will: a durable power of attorney for finances, a healthcare directive, and often a funded trust.
### Common questions
### Q. What not to tell the attorney?
A.  The opposite is the useful answer: hold nothing back. Communications with your attorney are privileged, and a plan built on partial information about assets, debts, prior marriages or family conflict often fails to work as intended. Bring account lists, deeds and beneficiary designations to the first meeting.
### Q. What should you not put in a will?
A.  Assets that already pass by other means: retirement accounts and life insurance with named beneficiaries, payable-on-death accounts, property held jointly with survivorship, and anything titled to a trust. Funeral instructions are often read too late to help, so leave those separately. Rules vary by state, so ask an attorney.
### Q. What assets are not considered part of an estate?
A.  Generally, anything that transfers by operation of law or contract: accounts with a named beneficiary, payable-on-death and transfer-on-death registrations, property held jointly with right of survivorship, and assets already titled to a funded trust. Definitions differ for probate and for tax, so confirm with an attorney.

## Family Practice in the St. Louis Metro

### Q. What are the signs of a good family physician?

## Fast Food in the St. Louis Metro

### Q. What are 5 major problems from eating fast food?
A.  Typical concerns are high sodium, calorie density, saturated fat, added sugar in drinks and sauces, and very little fiber or produce. Portion size compounds all five. Occasional meals are one thing; the issue is frequency, so grilled options, water instead of soda and a smaller size help.
### Q. What does fast food do to the body?
A.  Most fast food items run high in sodium, saturated fat and refined carbohydrates while offering little fiber, which can leave you hungry again quickly. Eaten often, that pattern is linked to weight gain and strain on the heart over time, so many nutrition guides suggest treating it as an occasional meal.

## Fertility in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/fertility

### General guidance is to seek evaluation after a year of trying, or after six months if the female partner is over 35, and sooner with known conditions.
### Common questions
### Q. What questions should I ask a fertility specialist?
A.  Ask for live birth rates by age group rather than pregnancy rates, and for a written cost breakdown, since monitoring, medication, retrieval, lab work and storage are billed separately. Ask whether both partners will be evaluated, and who you will actually see at each visit.
### Q. What age is a female most fertile?
A.  Fertility is generally highest in the twenties, declines gradually through the early thirties, and more noticeably after the mid thirties. That is a population pattern rather than a prediction for any individual. Evaluation covers both partners, and a semen analysis is quick, inexpensive and often skipped.
### Q. What I wish I knew before starting IVF?
A.  Two things come up most. The medication schedule is demanding and makes up a large share of the total, and coverage varies enormously, so get the breakdown in writing before you start. Also ask what happens between cycles, since monitoring visits and the emotional load are easy to underestimate.

## Financial Advising in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/financial-advising

### Ask two questions and get both answers in writing: are you a fiduciary at all times, and exactly how are you paid.
### Common questions
### Q. What to ask when selecting a financial advisor?
A.  Ask whether the adviser is a fiduciary at all times, how they are paid, and what the total cost includes once fund expenses sit on top of the advisory fee. Ask which credentials they hold, who holds your money, and how often you will actually meet.
### Q. How do I choose the right financial advisor for me?
A.  Shortlist two or three and interview them. Say what you actually want, whether that is one-time planning, retirement income or ongoing management, then compare what each proposes to deliver. ### Q. What is a red flag for a financial advisor?
A.  Refusing to put fiduciary status or compensation in writing is the clearest warning. Others include pressure toward one product, guaranteed returns, vague answers about fees, custody of your money in their own name rather than an independent custodian, and a disciplinary history you find in public records.

Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/financial-planner

### Ask whether they are a fiduciary at all times and get it in writing, then ask how they are paid, because fee-only, fee-based and commission carry different incentives.

### Q. What would be 5 great questions to ask if you are selecting a financial advisor?

A.  Fine dining generally means a refined menu built around quality ingredients, attentive table service, a polished atmosphere, and thoughtful details like plating and pacing between courses. ## Fire Departments in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/fire-departments

### Call 911 for any emergency; station lines are for administrative business such as smoke alarm programs, car seat fitting and burn permits.
### Common questions
### Q. What are good questions to ask firefighters?
A.  Ask what a shift actually looks like, how many calls are medical rather than fires, how to check smoke alarm placement at home, when an extinguisher needs replacing, and what they wish people did differently before a fire. Children usually want the gear and a walk around the truck.
### Q. Can I walk into a fire station and ask questions?
A.  Usually yes. Crews are on duty and often glad to talk, though they may be out on a call or resting between runs, so a quick call ahead saves a wasted trip. Many stations also handle car seat checks and station tours by appointment.
### Q. Can I call a fire department to ask a question?
A.  Yes, using the administrative or non emergency line rather than 911. That line handles burn permits, alarm questions, inspection records, car seat appointments and tour requests. If anyone is in danger, or you smell smoke or gas, hang up and call 911 instead.

## Fishing in the St. Louis Metro
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/fishing

### A license comes first and rules differ by water, since size limits, daily bag limits and open seasons vary by species and location.
### Common questions
### Q. What are some good questions to ask about fishing?
A.  Ask a local bait and tackle shop what is biting this week, what bait or lure is working, and which water is producing. Ask whether the spot has a boat ramp or is bank only, what the size and daily limits are, and whether it is catch and release.
### Q. What does a beginner need to start fishing?
A.  A valid license, a medium spinning rod and reel already spooled, a small box of hooks, split shot, bobbers and a couple of soft plastics, plus pliers and a line cutter. Live bait outfishes most lures at the start. Add sun protection and a way to carry water.
### Q. What does 3000 or 4000 mean on a fishing reel?
A.  Those numbers describe spool size and line capacity, not power. A 3000 is a light all around size for panfish and bass on lighter line, while a 4000 holds more and heavier line for bigger fish. Larger numbers mean a larger spool and more retrieve per turn.
