### Frequently asked questions
### Q. What 5 jobs will survive AI?
A.  Rather than five titles, use three tests: does somebody have to be physically present, does the state license a named person for the work, and is that person answerable later. Ask those three questions of any trade, and the ones that pass all three are the safest. In Missouri, plumbing in larger cities has required an examined certificate since 1939, which is about as durable a moat as work gets.
### Q. What are 10 jobs that AI can’t replace?
A.  Most lists like this are guesswork. A defensible version is any work where a licensed person must be on site and answerable: plumbers, electricians, HVAC technicians, roofers, veterinarians, dentists, nurses, cosmetologists, barbers and home inspectors. The common thread is not difficulty. It is that the law names a person who must show up, carry insurance and accept responsibility.
### Q. What job is most safe from AI?
A.  The safest work combines three things: physical presence, a state license in a person’s name, and personal liability for the result. Missouri’s veterinary law, for example, requires that the veterinarian has assumed the responsibility for making medical judgments about the animal. Software cannot assume responsibility, so that work stays with a human.
### Q. Which jobs will AI replace in 5 years?
A.  No credible source can name them with a date, and even the most-cited research on the topic says it does not make predictions about adoption timelines. What is honest to say is which tasks are exposed now: drafting, summarizing, first-pass customer questions, scheduling admin and marketing copy. If a role is mostly those, it is changing already. If it needs a person in a crawlspace, it is not.
### Q. What job is most at risk from AI?
A.  Judged by task overlap rather than headlines, the most exposed work is text-heavy and screen-based. The Eloundou research found the effects span all wage levels, with higher-income jobs potentially facing greater exposure, which flips the usual assumption. For a trade business, the bigger risk is not losing the work but losing the call, which is why owners list on St Louis Near Me Directory, where a listing can be indexed and cited by AI.
### Q. What jobs will still be around in 10 years?
A.  That is a prediction, and this page will not make one. The structural answer is more useful: work stays with people where the law requires a licensed individual, where the task is physical, and where someone must carry insurance and answer for the result. Those rules live in state statute, and they move at the speed of a legislature, not a software release.

## AI for a Small Business: The $20 Seat Is the Cheap Part
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/blog/what-ai-actually-costs-a-small-business
The card statement sits on the kitchen table under a ring of truck keys, and the work boots by the back door still smell like a crawlspace. Between the supply-house charge and the gas station there is a line for $20. ChatGPT Plus. For a plumber running a small crew out of that kitchen, the question after the last call of the day is plain: does that line earn its keep, or is it one more thing that renews while nobody opens it?
Here is what makes the line strange. OpenAI, the company that sells that $20 seat, ran a workshop for small business owners with SCORE at the Missouri Athletic Club downtown, on Washington Avenue, and its event page told attendees they would receive three free months of ChatGPT Plus. Breakfast. Coffee at check-in. A laptop or tablet on the table. That workshop has already happened, and the page now reads “Event has finished.” But it settled the kitchen-table question anyway. When the seller can hand the seat out with the coffee, the seat is the cheap part.
The expensive part is everything a pricing page leaves off: the evenings spent learning the tool after a shift, the minutes spent reading every draft before a customer sees it, and the money that leaks to people selling “AI strategy” to owners who are already stretched thin. Anyone running a trade on top of a full week, maybe on top of a second job, feels the push from every side. The webinar invite. The guy at the networking breakfast saying everyone is falling behind. Six browser tabs, one saying $20, one saying $200, one swearing it is all free. That isn’t falling behind. That’s being marketed to. Here is the real bill, with receipts.
### How much does it cost to use AI for a business?
For the tools a small business actually uses, somewhere between $0 and about $25 per person per month. ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini each list a free plan. ChatGPT Plus is $20 a month. ChatGPT Business and Claude Team both list a standard seat at $20 per user per month billed annually, or $25 billed monthly. Prices change often, and each provider’s own page is the only one that counts.
That range looks wide because it covers two different products. A consumer seat is one person with a login. A business seat is the same assistant plus central billing, admin controls and, on ChatGPT Business, no training on your business data by default. Above that sits a tier built for people who run the tool all day, the kind of seat that starts around $100 a month. A three-person plumbing crew does not need it.
For that crew the math fits on the back of a supply-house receipt. Three ChatGPT Business seats billed monthly come to $75 a month, $900 a year. Billed annually at $20 a seat, the same three seats come to $60 a month, $720 a year. That is the whole software bill for the van, the office and the kitchen table combined.
The rest of the field, read straight off each provider’s own page. Claude: Free is $0, Pro is $17 a month on an annual plan ($200 billed up front) or $20 monthly, and Max starts from $100. Google’s Gemini app is $0 a month with a Google Account, Google AI Plus is $4.99 a month, Google AI Pro is $19.99, and Google AI Ultra starts at $99.99. OpenAI’s own launch post put ChatGPT Go at $8 a month in the US. That $4.99 Google tier is the cheapest paid step on this page, which matters when all a crew wants is the limits raised a little.
Then there is the AI you may already be paying for without noticing. Google Workspace’s Business Starter plan lists the Gemini AI assistant in Gmail among what it includes. On the Microsoft side, Microsoft 365 Business Standard with Copilot is $23.50 per user per month paid yearly, and Business Premium with Copilot is $32.00. If one of those invoices already lands on the statement on that kitchen table, an assistant may already be paid for. A second one means two invoices for the same room.
Our broader take on how St. Louis businesses can actually use AI makes the same point in fewer words. This is the version with the arithmetic.
### The two costs nobody quotes
The first is learning time. Nobody gets good output on day one. They get something that sounds like a press release wrote it, all polish and no plumbing. Getting past that takes a few sessions of feeding the tool your real specifics: where you work, how you price, the questions every customer asks, the way you actually talk on the phone. That is unpaid time, usually at the kitchen table after the last service call, hands still smelling of pipe dope, and it is the most expensive month of the whole experiment.
The second is the review step, and it decides whether AI is worth anything to you at all. AI output is sometimes confidently wrong: hours you changed, a service you dropped, a warranty you never offered, a price that is not your price. If that reaches a customer, you did not save time. You manufactured a callback. So somebody reads every draft first, and when that somebody is the owner, tired, at the end of a long day, that reading time belongs on the bill too.
The test that sorts good tasks from bad ones is simple. Compare the time to check a draft against the time to write it yourself. A short reply to a review is fast to check and slow to write from a blank screen, so AI wins. A water heater quote where every line has to match the cost sheet can take longer to check than to type. Same tool, same $20, opposite result.
A crew’s whole AI bill
Most small-business seats run $0 to about $25 per person a month. For a three-person crew on ChatGPT Business, that is $720 a year billed annually or $900 billed monthly. What moves it: how many people actually open the tool, annual versus monthly billing, and whether a Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 plan already includes an assistant.
### Is it worth paying for AI?
Only once there is a wall on the free tier that has a name. Thirty days on one weekly task, timed before and after, minus the minutes spent checking the output, shows whether the wall exists. No wall, no bill.
The hour has a price. Missouri’s minimum wage is $15.00 an hour, adjusted each year by the Missouri Department of Labor, and Illinois law guarantees $15.00 an hour for workers 18 and older. At $15 an hour, a $20 seat has to give back 80 minutes a month just to break even, and a plumber’s hour is not billed at the floor, so the minutes needed shrink. Close is still a no. Close means the gain is inside your own measuring error, and that is exactly the subscription that renews for years while nobody opens it.
The free tier also comes with two warnings worth more than the money saved. Consumer and business plans can treat your data differently, which is part of why business plans exist. And free tools need no purchase order, so the people who work for you may already be using them. That is its own subject, covered in what happens when your staff is already using AI.
### Where the real money leaks
Not in the seat. In the packages wrapped around it. Be careful with a setup fee for work that takes an afternoon, a bundle of “secret prompts,” a guaranteed result, or a certificate no customer of yours will ever ask to see. The pitch usually lands the same way: a slide deck, a countdown, a number with no named source behind it. That is a sales line, not a finding, and you do not owe it your card.
Training itself is not padding. A few hours that get you past the press-release stage can be cheaper than months of paying for a tool you use badly. The test is what you walk out with: your own work, improved, or a folder of somebody else’s templates.
Three levers actually move the bill:
Seat count. Per-user pricing is brutally linear. Buy for the people who open it every day, not the ones who might.
Annual billing. Claude Pro drops from $20 to $17 a month on an annual plan, and ChatGPT Business drops from $25 to $20. Lock in only after the thirty-day test has given you the answer.
Duplication. A separate $20 assistant on top of the one inside your Workspace or Microsoft 365 plan is sometimes worth it. Often it is just two invoices.

### Q. What is the best AI for pricing?
A.  None of the general assistants. ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini do not know your labor rates, your material costs or your drive times, so any number they hand you is a guess in confident clothes. They are useful for explaining a quote clearly to a customer. Setting the number stays your job, off your own cost sheet.
Refuse to be invisible.

## $2 a Pound: Where to Buy Craft Supplies in St. Louis
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/blog/where-to-buy-craft-supplies-in-st-louis
Two dollars a pound. That is the price of the sound a scoop of buttons makes hitting the bottom of a paper bag, like hard rain on a car roof, and most St. Louis families have never heard it.
It happens in Ballwin, at 930 Kehrs Mill Road, inside the Barn at Lucerne. The St. Louis Teachers’ Recycle Center says its main room is stocked with items that can be picked by the pound, at a service fee of $2.00 a pound. Not per sheet. Not per skein. Per pound. And despite the name, the center says it is open to the public and to all.
At a craft chain you pay for the label on the package. Here you pay for gravity. Ten dollars is five pounds, and five pounds of ribbon, felt and construction paper is a bag you can barely fold shut. Five pounds of glass jars is a handful of jars. Same ten dollars. That one idea is the whole game.
### Where is the cheapest place to get craft supplies?
Usually a creative reuse center, where donated materials sell by weight instead of by the piece, so the lightest things in the room are the biggest bargains. In St. Louis County that means the Ballwin center’s $2.00-a-pound main room. Thrift stores and estate sales come next. Big-box basics come last, and only when you compare unit price, not shelf price.
The reason is simple math. A craft chain buys wholesale and marks up. The Teachers’ Recycle Center says it gathers creative materials from local communities, business and industry that are landfill-bound, and has been keeping usable materials out of landfills since 1993. Nobody manufactured that stock for a shelf. That is exactly why it is cheap, and exactly why it is unpredictable.
Beyond the by-the-pound main room, the center says its ReMarket fills 2 other rooms, priced as marked. So the poster board due tomorrow, the thirty-of-something for a classroom, the four bins from a grandmother’s sewing room with nowhere to go: one building handles all three.
### When you can actually shop
Reuse centers run on volunteer hours, so the calendar is tighter than a chain store’s. The center’s site lists shopping hours of 1:00pm-6:00pm on Tuesday and Wednesday and 11:00am-4:00pm on Saturday, and it is closed to shoppers the rest of the week. Call (636) 227-7095 before you drive out, since hours like these move.
### How to shop a room that sells by the pound
Shop it backwards from a big-box aisle. Walk in with a material in mind, not a finished product, because the bins decide what is possible today. Bring your own bags or bins, a list of properties instead of brand names (“something blue and flat,” not “12 felt squares in cobalt”), and give yourself an hour. Rushing a reuse center is how you leave with nothing.
Weight is the whole pricing model, so learn which categories win. A fistful of ribbon or a stack of construction paper barely moves a scale. Glass jars, ceramic tile, books and wood blocks feel heavy in the bag and price that way. Outfitting a classroom, a scout troop or a rainy week of summer break? Stay in the light bins.
Substitution is the skill. You wanted twelve matching blue squares. There are nine, plus teal. Either the project bends or the trip fails. People who shop reuse well pick the palette after the trip, and treat each bin as a prompt rather than a catalog.
The trap nobody warns you about is over-buying. Cheap per pound is still money if it sits in a closet, and five pounds of someone else’s good intentions can live in a basement for years. Buy for a project already started. The same rule holds in vintage, thrift and antique shops around the metro, where the temptation is identical and the storage problem is bigger.
### Bring the kids, not just the list
Here is the part of the Ballwin center most shoppers walk right past. The center also runs Play Your Art Out, which the center describes as a space for all ages to experience and develop respect for each other and our planet through art and play. The center lists all play sessions at $15.00 per person, and each one runs approximately 2 hours.
That changes the math on a rainy weekend. Two hours of glue, cardboard and somebody else’s cleanup, then a pass through the by-the-pound room on the way out so the project can keep going at the kitchen table. Kids who just spent two hours turning a paper towel roll into a rocket tend to shop the bins differently. They stop asking for the kit on the end cap and start asking what the bin of buttons could become.
The center also takes birthdays. Its studio page says it will organize a guided play and art session followed by a party, complete with a reflective slideshow of the day. For a parent who has priced a party venue lately, that is worth a phone call.
Teachers and troop leaders should know about VanGO, the center’s mobile unit. The center says it brings workshops and community outreach to schools, libraries, community events and organizations, and that it hands out free children’s books at community events. Booking runs through the same number, 636-227-7095. If your school’s budget for art supplies is a shoebox and a prayer, that van is the closest thing to a field trip that comes to you.
### Is Hobby Lobby or Walmart cheaper for craft supplies?
Neither wins across the board, and a page that says otherwise is guessing. The answer flips by category and by whatever happens to be on sale this week. General-merchandise stores tend to hold the line on commodity basics. A craft chain usually wins on specialty stock nobody else carries.
So compare unit price, not shelf price. Per yard, per sheet, per ounce, per skein, done on your phone while you stand in the aisle under the fluorescent hum. Package sizes are hard to line up on purpose. A bigger package at a higher sticker is often the cheaper one, and a small one on sale often is not.
Then price the drive, which almost nobody does. Two stores twenty-five minutes apart to save four dollars is a losing trade once you count gas and an evening you do not get back. The families that spend least on crafts are rarely chasing the lowest sticker. They consolidate trips and shop from a written project list.
### What to always buy new
Three categories, every time: anything with chemistry in it, anything that touches skin or food, and anything that has to match across a big surface. Almost everything else is fair game secondhand.
Glue is the one people learn the hard way. Adhesives, sealants and resins keep curing in the bottle whether anyone opens them or not. A donated bottle can look fine and pour out stringy, or not pour at all. Acrylic paint goes rubbery. Elastic loses its snap. You usually find out the night before the project is due.
The safety tier is not negotiable. If it will touch skin, touch food, or land in front of a small child, buy it new and labeled: earring findings, glazes for anything that holds food, candle fragrance oils, eye protection, materials meant for toddlers. The label is the first thing a donation bin loses. And yarn from two dye lots looks identical in the store and obviously different across a finished blanket, so buy the full amount at once, plus one extra.
Would rather be taught than left with a shelf of supplies? Here is what a St. Louis candle making class actually involves.

Scout troops go through felt and glue at a rate you have to see. Community theater costume shops will take fabric, trim and anything that fastens. Sort by material, bag like with like, and keep out anything dried, rusted, mildewed or leaking. A donation that fits their shelf is worth more than one that is merely large.

## Buying a Used Boat in Missouri: The Trailer Gets 30 Days
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/blog/what-to-know-before-buying-a-used-boat-in-missouri
The boat gives you 60 days. The trailer it rides on gives you 30.
That is the Missouri rule almost nobody mentions while you are standing in a stranger’s driveway, palm flat on a sun-warm hull, listening to the outboard cough and settle on a garden hose. You shake hands, drop the safety chains over the ball with that heavy clank, and tow home feeling like the hard part is done. It isn’t. Three clocks just started, and the shortest one belongs to the piece you barely looked at.
According to the Missouri Department of Revenue, you have 60 days from purchase to title a boat or outboard motor, and a late boat title costs $10 on the 61st day, topping out at $30. The trailer runs on a different track: 30 days to title it and pay the sales tax, a $25 penalty on the 31st day, then another $25 every 30 days up to $200. Miss the trailer by a summer and it can cost more than the boat paperwork ever could.
If you live in St. Louis City or County, three local checks do most of the work, and they are all below: the free Highway Patrol serial number check, the public ramp at Columbia Bottom for an honest water test, and the City of St. Louis tax calendar that decides whether you can renew next time.
### Do boats need titles in Missouri?
Yes, and usually more than one. The Missouri State Highway Patrol puts it plainly: state law requires all motorized vessels, sailboats over 12 feet long, and gasoline powered outboard motors to be titled within 60 days of purchase. The outboard is its own titled item, with its own fee. Trolling motors and electric outboards are the exception.
That is the part that trips up anyone who has only bought cars. With a car, one title covers the whole machine. Here the hull, the motor bolted to its transom and the trailer under it are three separate pieces of property, and the license office handles them as three. One handshake. Three stacks of paper.
So the first question for a private seller is not about engine hours. It is this: do you have the title for the boat, the motor and the trailer, in your name, in your hand, today? If any one of those gets a shrug, you have not found a bargain. You have found a paperwork project with a boat attached.
Then match the paper to the metal. Under federal rules the primary hull identification number sits on the starboard outboard side of the transom, within two inches of the top. Crouch down, run a thumb across the plate, and read every character out loud against the title. A digit that does not match is not a typo you fix later. It is the whole deal.
One exception: vessels documented by the U.S. Coast Guard are not required to be titled in Missouri, but they still must be registered. If a seller hands you a federal certificate of documentation instead of a state title, call the Department of Revenue before any money moves.
### Can I buy a used boat without a title?
You can hand somebody cash for almost anything. Whether you can then put that boat in the water under your own name is a different question. A missing title is the most expensive problem in a used boat deal. Not the motor. The paper.
The clean fix costs you nothing: the seller sorts out the title in their own name first, then signs it over to you at closing. A seller who resists that is telling you something. Maybe the boat is not theirs to sell. Maybe a lien is still open. Maybe they bought it on a handshake too, and the problem is already three owners old.
Broken paper trails do have a way back. The Highway Patrol notes that when a boat, motor or trailer has an incorrect title, or comes from a state that does not require one, the Department of Revenue requires a serial number inspection before you can apply for title or registration. Buy a project like that with your eyes open, never by surprise.
### Do you pay sales tax on a used boat in Missouri?
Yes, and you pay it when you title the boat, not in the driveway, usually in one number you were not braced for. The Department of Revenue charges state sales tax of 4.225 percent plus local sales tax on the purchase price, less any trade-in allowance. The outboard is taxed the same way, separately.
The line that surprises people: local sales tax is the rate where you live, not where you bought the boat. Drive across the river for a better pontoon and you still pay your own Missouri address’s rate. Run the number through the Department’s online sales tax calculator before you agree to a price, while you can still negotiate.
There is one real break. No tax is due if the boat was registered and operated in another state for at least 90 days before you title it in Missouri. Ask the seller for that registration history and keep a copy.
And the thing people mutter about by the trailer hitch: writing a lower price on the bill of sale to shrink the tax. Don’t. You save a little once and carry a false purchase record on an asset you may want to insure, finance or sell later.
### How much is personal property tax on a boat in Missouri?
The bill comes from where you live. Missouri wants the receipt from your county of residence or the City of St. Louis, and the local Assessor’s Office sets the value. What you can pin down is the calendar.
Take the City of St. Louis. Its Assessor lists boats and trailers among the personal property that has to be declared. Declarations are due by April 1st, and a late or missing form draws a 10% penalty. The Collector mails bills in November, and they are due by December 31st.
Here is why it matters at the dock. Missouri wants a paid personal property tax receipt, or a statement of non-assessment, from your county or the City of St. Louis for the previous year before it will register or renew a boat. The first summer feels free. The paperwork catches up the next spring, about the time you smell the first sunscreen of the season and want to get on the water.
Price the year, not the boat. Tax, insurance, registration, storage and winterizing are the recurring number, and that number decides whether you still own it in three years.
Nothing to do with boats, and a lot cheaper: metro farmers markets, town by town.
### Can you register a boat in Missouri with just a bill of sale?
Generally, no. The Department of Revenue asks for the Certificate of Title properly signed over to you, or a Manufacturer’s Statement of Origin on a new boat. A bill of sale proves what you paid. It does not prove you own anything.
Two documents, two jobs. The title says who owns it. The bill of sale says what changed hands and for how much. A good one names both parties, lists the hull number, the motor serial and the trailer, prices each of the three separately, carries the date and both signatures. Splitting the price is not busywork, since each piece is taxed and titled on its own.
### The free check most buyers never use
The Missouri State Highway Patrol will inspect a boat, motor or trailer for a proper number and confirm it is not reported stolen, and the service is provided at no cost to the public. You bring proof you own it, such as a bill of sale, along with the actual boat, motor or trailer.
For this metro, the Patrol lists Troop C under St. Louis at 636-300-2800. Call ahead to schedule. A number that has been ground down, painted over or covered by a plate that sits a little crooked turns up there, under a trooper’s flashlight, instead of in your garage two seasons later.
### What should you check on the boat itself?
Paperwork costs you money you did not plan on. Condition costs you weekends. Most of the expensive failures announce themselves to anyone willing to spend twenty unglamorous minutes before writing a check.
### The walkaround
Step onto the deck and feel for softness or flex under your feet, because a wet, rotting core is the repair that turns a good deal bad. Look in the bilge for standing water, an oily sheen, or fresh paint over a repair. Check the steering for slop and the wiring for household-grade splices. On the trailer, read the tire date codes, look for cracked springs, and spin each wheel by hand: grit you can feel through your fingers means bearings.
Then the motor. Ask for hours and service records, and treat a compression test as normal, not nosy. Pull the cowling and look for chalky corrosion around the powerhead. On a sterndrive, look hard at the bellows. A boat that has been run and maintained beats a low-hour boat that sat on a side yard and “just needs a battery” nearly every time.
### The water test
Never buy a powerboat you have not run on water. A hose proves the engine starts. It does not prove the boat gets on plane, shifts clean, charges the battery or tracks straight. Meet at a public ramp. On the north edge of the metro, the Missouri Department of Conservation’s Columbia Bottom Conservation Area in North St. Louis County has a boat ramp that puts you in to the Missouri River, and the Department notes that public access there is currently limited to the boat ramp while levee work goes on, so call its St. Louis Regional office at 636-441-4554 before you tow out. Back the trailer down, feel the river lift the hull off the bunks, run it up, let it idle long enough to surface a cooling problem, shut it down, and restart it hot. If the seller will not put it in the water, you have your answer.
The habit that protects you on a used car works here too. Our walkthrough of how to check a used car before you hand over the money covers that discipline. If the boat is mostly for fishing, read the best free public water around St. Louis before you decide how much boat you need.
Line up the shop before you buy the boat. Compare local businesses and services across the St. Louis metro on St Louis Near Me Directory, then put two calls on your list before you hitch up: a marine mechanic for an inspection, and your license office about the trailer’s 30-day clock.
If you’re the marine mechanic, the trailer shop or the storage lot buyers call in a panic every spring, a Gold listing puts you in front of more customers right when they are searching. See what Gold includes.
### Why the shop matters before the sale
Boating season around here is short, and good marine mechanics fill their calendars early. A boat bought late in the summer with a problem nobody caught can sit under a tarp, smelling of old fuel, until the water turns cold. A dealer who knows the model, a mechanic who works on your engine brand, a trailer shop, an upholstery place, somewhere to store it for the winter: line those up the week before you buy, not the morning something breaks.
A used motorcycle runs into the same title trap, only worse. See what to avoid when buying a used motorcycle in Missouri before you hand anybody cash on a gravel lot.

### Frequently asked questions
### Q. Do you pay sales tax on a used boat in Missouri?
A.  Yes, including a private sale. Missouri charges state sales tax of 4.225 percent plus local sales tax on the purchase price, less any trade-in, on the boat and on the outboard motor. The local rate is where you live, not where you bought it. No tax is due if the boat was registered and operated in another state for at least 90 days first.
### Q. Can I buy a used boat without a title?
A.  You can pay for one. Getting it titled in your name is the hard part. The clean fix is having the seller sort out the title in their own name first, then sign it over to you. If the title is wrong or the boat came from a state that does not title boats, expect a Highway Patrol serial number inspection first.
### Q. Can you register a boat in Missouri with just a bill of sale?
A.  Generally no. The Department of Revenue wants the Certificate of Title properly signed over to you, or the Manufacturer’s Statement of Origin on a new boat. Keep the bill of sale anyway, because it documents the price the tax is figured on.
### Q. How much does it cost to register a boat in Missouri?
A.  The boat title fee is $7.50 and the outboard motor title fee is $5, plus processing fees. The boat registration decal fee is based on the boat’s length, so check the Department of Revenue fee chart for your exact boat. Budget for the sales tax too, which is usually the biggest line.
### Q. How much is personal property tax on a boat in Missouri?
A.  It depends on where you live and what your local assessor says the boat is worth. In the City of St. Louis, boats and trailers must be declared by April 1st, late forms draw a 10% penalty, and bills mailed in November are due by December 31st.
### Q. Can I renew my boat registration online in Missouri?
A.  The Department of Revenue says to renew at any Missouri license office, by mail, or by phone at 573-751-1957. Registration renews every three years and expires June 30th of the year on the decal, there is no late renewal penalty, and outboard motor decals never need renewing.

## St. Louis Health Food Stores: The Discounts With No Tag
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/blog/how-to-shop-a-health-food-store-in-st-louis
The basket says “inglorious.” Inside it is produce with blemishes, bruises and the small physical imperfections that keep it out of the main display. Pick one up and the weight in your palm is the same as the pretty one next to it. At Local Harvest Grocery, the independent grocer at 3108 Morganford Road in the city, the markdowns on those baskets start at 25%. Nothing at the door tells you to go looking for them.
Then there is the case discount. The store’s special-orders page says practically any item it carries can be ordered in bulk with a case discount of 10%. You ask an employee in the store or call 314-865-5260. The words to use are short. “Can I special order a case of this?”
For a tight budget, this one matters most. Shoppers paying with SNAP/EBT get 50% off produce, up to $25 a day, taken off at the register with no sign-up and no forms. You just tell the cashier at the start of the transaction. The store is open every day, 9 AM to 8 PM.
Meanwhile the price tags you can see are quieter than they look. The bin tag gives you a price per pound. The supplement bottle gives you a price, a green leaf and the words “clinical strength.” Neither tells you whether it is a good deal or whether the capsule holds what the label says. That is the whole lesson of a health food store. The best deal is usually something you ask for. The safe bottle is something you check for. The shelf hands you neither.
### Where is the safest place to buy vitamins?
Safety here is a label question, not a store question. Under the Dietary Supplement Health and Education Act of 1994, the FDA is not authorized to approve dietary supplements for safety and effectiveness before they are marketed. That holds whether the shelf is at a co-op, a chain pharmacy or a website you found at midnight.
Hold the bottle and turn it slowly in your hand, past the leaf and the big promise, to the small type that wraps around the curve. The weight of the responsibility is printed right there, if you know where to look. The FDA says manufacturers and distributors have initial responsibility for making sure their supplements meet the safety standards. And when a label makes a claim about what the product does for your body, the law requires a disclaimer saying the FDA has not evaluated that claim, and that the product is not intended to “diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease.” Most people read straight past that line. It is the most honest sentence on the package.
None of this makes supplements dangerous, and it is no knock on the people who run health food stores. It just moves the checking onto you. Same regulatory floor in every store in the metro. So the real question was never where. It is how you check.
### The seal that does the checking the FDA does not
According to the National Institutes of Health Office of Dietary Supplements, several independent organizations offer quality testing and allow products that pass to display a seal of quality assurance indicating the product was properly manufactured, contains the ingredients listed on the label, and does not contain harmful levels of contaminants. Organizations that offer quality testing include ConsumerLab.com, NSF International and U.S. Pharmacopeia.
Read the next sentence on that same page twice, because it is the one the marketing skips. Those seals do not guarantee that a product is safe or effective. A seal tells you the capsule holds what the label says. It does not tell you the capsule will do anything for you.
### Before you buy anything you swallow
Find the seal. Then find the small print: an FDA rule says supplement labels must give a domestic address or domestic phone number for reporting serious adverse events. A bottle with neither is a bottle to put back.
Then the step that costs nothing and matters most. If you take a prescription, tell your pharmacist what you are about to start. The Office of Dietary Supplements warns that supplements can interact with some medicines in ways that might cause problems, and gives a plain example: vitamin K can reduce the ability of the blood thinner warfarin to prevent blood from clotting. This is shopping advice, not medical advice, and that is exactly why the pharmacist is the stop that counts.
### Where’s the best place to buy bulk food?
Best depends on which bulk you mean, because two different things wear the same word. One is the self-serve bin, where you scoop what you want and pay by weight. The other is large format: the big sack, the case of cans, the warehouse multipack. They solve opposite problems.
Bins win when you want a small amount. Stand at the spice bins and it makes sense right away. Two spoonfuls of smoked paprika cost a sliver of a full jar, and you are not adopting a jar that will still be in the back of the cabinet years from now, faded to the color of brick dust. Bins are the only sane way to buy an ingredient once, for one recipe.
At Local Harvest, the bulk section works like this. If you bring your own containers, staff weigh them before filling so you are not charged for the weight of your container. Free reused containers sit on the shelf already washed, sanitized and pre-weighed, and paper and plastic bags are free too. You fill up, carry it to the register, and they weigh it and do the math. No PLUs, no labels, no twist ties to write on.
Large format wins on the things you burn through: rice, flour, oil, canned tomatoes, pet food. The case discount is where these two worlds meet. If you go through oats every week, asking for the case is the bulk bin and the warehouse club rolled into one, at a store that is already on your way home.
One practical note on any bin, anywhere. A bin with no scoop, a cracked lid or no label is a real signal, not a nitpick. Mention it to staff, or skip that bin.
### What is the cheapest place to buy in bulk?
The cheapest place is whichever one wins on price per ounce after you subtract what you throw away. That second half is where bulk savings quietly die. The EPA cites a U.S. Department of Agriculture estimate that 31 percent of the food available at the retail and consumer levels was not eaten.
### Run the comparison standing in the aisle
Put everything in the same unit, then divide. Bins are usually priced per pound and packages are labeled in ounces, so divide the bin price by sixteen and hold it against the package price per ounce. That is the whole technique. It takes ten seconds on your phone, and it beats every rule of thumb anyone will hand you at the register.
Most shelf tags print a unit price in small type under the big number, which does the division for you. Check that the units match, though. A tag reading “per ounce” next to one reading “per count” is not a comparison.
### The waste you never priced in
A big bag at half the unit price is a bad deal if half of it goes stale in the pantry. Divide by what you actually finish, not by what you carried to the car. Be honest with yourself here. Nobody enjoys it, and everybody needs it.
Nuts, nut flours, whole grain flours, seeds and ground spices carry oils or volatile flavor that fades and turns. You can smell it when it happens: a flat, crayon-like note where there used to be toast. Buy those small, from a bin, and buy them again soon. White rice, dried beans, sugar and salt keep a long time sealed and dry. Buy those big.
Different aisle, same rule about asking first: what is actually worth buying at a beauty supply store.
### Four things genuinely worth buying at a health food store
Spices and dried herbs by weight. The clearest win in the building. You spend less, you cook with fresher spice, and you stop keeping a graveyard of half-used jars.
Staples you already go through. Oats, rice, lentils, dried beans, popcorn. If you know you finish them, buy an exact amount instead of whatever size a manufacturer picked, and ask about the case price for the one you buy every month.
Things a conventional store will not carry. Gluten-free flours, nutritional yeast, allergen-specific products, herbal teas by weight. If your household is living with celiac disease or a serious allergy, selection is the value, and the price comparison is mostly beside the point.
Supplements you have already checked. Staff who can point to the seal and walk you through a label are worth something. Just remember the seal does the work, not the storefront. The same tested bottle is the same tested bottle anywhere.
Usually not worth the markup: national-brand packaged goods you can buy at any grocery store, bottled drinks, paper products, and anything you picked up because a shelf talker was persuasive rather than because you checked first.
### What is the 3-3-3 rule for groceries?
It is a meal-planning shortcut people pass along to each other. The common version: pick three proteins, three vegetables and three starches for the week and rotate them. Versions differ from one telling to the next.
It works best with a bin section, because the starches and some of the proteins come by weight. Local Harvest’s own bulk inventory list includes Cahokia High Protein Brown Rice, steel cut oats and red quinoa, and the store asks shoppers to call and confirm what is in stock. Three starches, scooped to the ounce, for a week. That is a 3-3-3 week that starts at a scoop, not a cart.
Here is why it pairs so well with bulk shopping, which almost nobody mentions. Variety is what creates waste. Nine ingredients you cook on repeat get finished. Twenty-two ingredients bought with Saturday enthusiasm end up as a soft bag of something in the crisper drawer. If you want the bins to pay off, shrinking your rotation for a few weeks does more for the bill than any coupon app. Run it for a month, learn what your household really eats, then loosen up and keep the knowledge.
### Is $100 a week too much for groceries?
It depends on how many people you feed and how old they are, and there is a federal ruler built for exactly this question. The USDA produces four food plans at successively higher cost levels, the Thrifty, Low-Cost, Moderate-Cost and Liberal plans, and publishes what each one costs every month.
Here is the detail almost every budget article skips. Those costs are given for individuals in 4-person households, and USDA suggests adjustments for other sizes: 1-person, add 20%; 2-person, add 10%; 3-person, add 5%; 5- or 6-person, subtract 5%; 7 or more, subtract 10%. A person living alone pays more per head for the same food, and the government’s own math says so. If $100 a week feels tight for one person, you are not imagining it.
USDA’s method is to sum the food costs for each individual in the household and then apply the adjustment factor for household size. Do that, then hold that number against your last three bank statements. That second number is the only one actually about you.
The Thrifty plan matters for another reason: USDA says the cost of the Thrifty Food Plan each June serves as the basis for SNAP benefit allotments for the following federal fiscal year. If the budget is under real pressure, that program is worth understanding before you optimize anything else, and we walk through the paperwork in our guide to applying for SNAP in Missouri. Pair it with that 50% produce discount on Morganford and the same benefits buy noticeably more fruit and vegetables. Seasonal produce is its own lever, and the metro’s farmers markets by town are worth working into the rotation.
Want a store near you with bins, a case price and someone who will answer a label question? Start with the health food stores and markets listed across the metro on St Louis Near Me Directory, check the hours, then bring the divide-by-sixteen math with you.
If you run the co-op, the spice shop or the neighborhood market, this is the reader you want. Shoppers who ask about case prices come back every month. A Gold listing puts your bins, your special orders and your hours in front of the St. Louis customers already searching for them. See how a listing brings you more customers.
### What is the slowest shopping day of the week?
There is no single answer for every store, and a national average will not tell you much about the one you actually drive to. The better tool is free and already on your phone. Google may show popular times, live visit information and typical visit duration on a business’s listing in Maps and Search, hour by hour, for that specific store.
A quiet hour buys you things that matter in this kind of store. Staff have time to tell you which bin is which, whether they can order you a case, and when the shelf gets restocked. You can read a label without someone reaching across you for the almonds.
Now the contrarian half. For bulk bins, a busy store is often the better store, because turnover is freshness. Nuts and seeds go stale sitting still. A bin that gets emptied and refilled all week tastes like it. So the ideal is a busy store at a quiet hour, which is exactly what that graph lets you find. A store open seven days, like Local Harvest at 9 AM to 8 PM, gives you a lot of hours to choose from. While you are there, ask two questions: which day the bulk order comes in, and where the marked-down items go. At Local Harvest, the answer to the second is a central display by the registers.
### What this looks like from behind the counter
A bulk program is thinner than it looks from the shopper’s side. Somebody fills those bins, washes the returned jars, and throws out what did not sell. At Local Harvest, even the containers are a program: a blue collection bin just inside the front doors takes containers that have an opening at least 2 inches wide, a tight-fitting lid and all labels removed, and they go back out on the shelf for the next shopper. Knowing that changes how you shop. Bring the jar back. Ask for the case. Buy the bruised peach. Those are the habits that keep a small store open, and a small store is the one place in the city where the person at the register can tell you which lentils actually sold this week.
### Frequently asked questions
### Q. Where’s the best place to buy bulk food?
A.  It depends on which kind of bulk. Self-serve bins are best for small amounts, especially spices, because you pay by weight for exactly what you need. Large-format buying is better for staples you finish fast. The overlooked middle option is a case order: Local Harvest Grocery on Morganford Road says practically any item it carries can be ordered in bulk with a 10% case discount.
### Q. What is the cheapest place to buy in bulk?
A.  Whichever store wins on price per ounce after you subtract what you waste. Divide a per-pound bin price by sixteen and compare it to the package price per ounce, then divide by what you actually finish. The EPA cites a USDA estimate that 31 percent of food at the retail and consumer levels was not eaten, and that gap is where most bulk savings disappear.
### Q. What is the 3-3-3 rule for groceries?
A.  A meal-planning shortcut people pass along. The usual version is three proteins, three vegetables and three starches a week, rotated. It works mostly as a limit on variety, and less variety is what keeps bulk purchases from turning into waste.
### Q. Is $100 a week too much for groceries?
A.  For one adult it is often workable; for a family it gets tight fast. Use the USDA food plan costs: sum the food costs for each individual in the household, then apply USDA’s household-size adjustment, which for a 1-person household is to add 20%. Then compare that to your own bank statements.
### Q. What is the slowest shopping day of the week?
A.  It varies by store, so check the popular times graph on the store’s Google listing in Maps or Search for an hour-by-hour picture of that exact location. For bulk bins, remember that a busy store often has fresher nuts, seeds and flours, so aim for a busy store at its quiet hour.
### Q. Does a seal on a supplement mean it works?
A.  No. According to the NIH Office of Dietary Supplements, quality seals from groups such as ConsumerLab.com, NSF International and U.S. Pharmacopeia show a product was properly manufactured, contains what the label lists and does not contain harmful levels of contaminants, but they do not guarantee that a product is safe or effective. Ask your pharmacist about interactions with anything you already take.

## What a Locksmith Costs in St. Louis, and the Scam to Avoid
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/blog/what-a-locksmith-costs-in-st-louis
The deadbolt clicks home behind you, and in the same half second you can see the keys. On the counter. Through the glass. Your phone is in your hand, the battery icon is going red, the porch light is buzzing, and the first page of results all say the same three things: open 24 hours, minutes away, a price so low it should make you suspicious and somehow doesn’t.
Here is the part nobody puts on that screen. Missouri does not license locksmiths. There is no state card for the person who shows up to open your door, no state exam behind the word on the van. But if you live in the City of St. Louis, there is still a public record you can check from that same dying phone. City code says any person who engages in any trade within the City limits is required to have a business license, and the License Collector keeps a St. Louis business license search you can run by business name or by city address.
The catch is what the search runs on. Licenses are issued under legal names. So the very first question that unmasks a fake, “what is the legal name of your business?”, is also the key that opens the city’s record. A real shop answers it without a pause. A call center stalls, or reads you a name that matches nothing.
That is the whole job of this page: a handful of questions, asked in the driveway, that turn a midnight gamble into a price you agreed to. And if you are not locked out tonight, the same questions make the scheduled jobs (a rekey after a move, a new deadbolt, a door that turns halfway and stops) cheaper and calmer.
### How much should locksmiths charge?
A locksmith should charge you a number you agreed to before the van left, built from three visible lines: a service call or trip charge, labor for the actual work, and hardware if any. After-hours and holiday work carries a premium. Anything quoted as a single teaser figure with the rest revealed at your door is not a quote.
There is no honest single figure for this metro. Any page that prints one is recycling a national average or selling you something. Price moves with five things: the hour you call, how far the vehicle drives, what the lock actually is, whether the door or frame took damage, and how many cylinders end up in the job.
The hour matters more than people expect. A lockout late at night is a callout, a drive across the county, and a technician who is awake because you called. The same lock, rekeyed on a weekday afternoon, is a scheduled stop between two other scheduled stops. Same skill. Same person. A completely different product, and it should be priced like one.
So the useful question is never what locksmiths charge in general. It is what this job costs, from this shop, at this address, before anybody gets in a vehicle. That number exists, and somebody at an honest shop can say it out loud.
### The four lines a real quote says out loud
You should hear all four before you agree to anything. The service call or trip charge, which covers getting there. The labor for the work itself. The hardware, if a lock or cylinder is going in. And the after-hours rate when it applies, stated as an actual amount rather than a vague warning that nights cost more.
Ask for the all-in total with tax, then ask what would change it. A straight answer sounds like a condition, not a hedge: the number holds unless the door has been forced, unless the cylinder turns out to be high-security, unless we have to drill. A shop that cannot name a single condition has not thought about your job. A shop that names three has done this job many times over.
Then get it in writing, and a text counts. Ask the person on the phone to send the quoted total to your number before anyone is dispatched. It costs nothing. It turns a voice on a phone into something you can hold up under the porch light when somebody explains why the number grew on the walk from the van.
Two more items belong in the same call. Ask whether the price includes replacing the lock if drilling is required, because a drilled cylinder means new hardware, and that is the second charge people never see coming. And ask what payment the shop takes. Cash only, at your door, after midnight, is the oldest tell in this trade.
### How the teaser-price lockout works
It works because the sale, the dispatch and the work are three different parties. You call a number attached to a very low advertised price. A dispatcher who is not a locksmith, and may be nowhere near Missouri, takes your address. Someone arrives in an unmarked car, looks at the lock for a few seconds, and announces that this one has to be drilled. The advertised price covered showing up.
Every piece of it is built for the moment you have the least leverage. It is late, it is cold or it is raining, you are outside, and your choices are the person standing in front of you or starting the whole search over. The pressure is not a side effect of the model. The pressure is the model.
The tells are consistent, and you can check most of them from the sidewalk. A phone number with no business name attached. A dispatcher who will not say which company is coming. No local street address anywhere on the listing. A vehicle with no company name on it. A technician with no identification and no invoice. And the price moving after the work has started rather than before it.
One more is quieter and catches careful people. A result looks local because it carries a neighborhood name, and the address behind it turns out to be a mailbox, a vacant suite or a parking lot. A shop you could drive to on a weekday is a different business from a phone number that only surfaces when you are desperate.
### How do you price a lockout before anyone is dispatched?
Six questions, in this order, standing in the driveway. It works for a boring reason: a call center in another state cannot answer the first three without giving itself away.
One: what is the legal name of the business, and what is the street address? Two: am I talking to the locksmith or to a dispatch service? Three: is the technician an employee or a subcontractor? Four: what is the all-in total for a residential lockout at this address at this hour, trip charge and tax included? Five: what would change that number? Six: will you text me the total before you send anyone?
While you wait for the text, take the legal name you were given and run it. Inside city limits, the License Collector’s search shows whether the business has been issued a business license for the current fiscal year, and you only need part of the name. Out in the county, the same page points you to the Missouri Secretary of State to verify whether a business is registered with the state at all. A name that shows up nowhere is your answer.
Then set two conditions rather than ask them. Tell them you will want photo identification and the company name on the invoice when the technician arrives. And tell them plainly that you are not authorizing drilling without a new price agreed first. Both are ordinary requests. Both make a bait-and-switch operation lose interest in your address remarkably fast.
A range is a fine answer and often the honest one. “We can’t say until we see it” on a standard residential lockout is not, so keep calling. The shops willing to commit to a number over the phone tend to be the ones with a sign on a building and a name they intend to keep using next year.
Different kind of key entirely: the best bank for small business checking in St. Louis.
### Does Missouri license locksmiths?
No. Missouri is not on the list of states that require locksmith licensing. There is no state license to look up, no state exam behind the title, and no state board reviewing complaints about a locksmith’s work. The vetting lands on you, which is exactly why the driveway questions matter more here than they would in a licensing state.
Across the river the rules flip: Illinois is one of the states that require locksmith licensing. If the job is in Belleville or Edwardsville, ask for the Illinois license number before anyone drives out, and check it in the state’s license lookup.
On the Missouri side, use the checks that do the same work. The city license search inside city limits. A physical address you can find on a map and, if the job can wait a day, drive past. Proof of general liability insurance, since somebody is about to put a drill to your door. Then check that three names match: the one on the listing, the one on the invoice, and the one on the vehicle. It is a low bar, and call-center operations trip over it constantly.
Address is also why a directory listing beats a star rating for this trade: you can compare locksmiths across the St. Louis metro by whether there is a real place behind the phone number. And if it goes wrong anyway, the complaint still has somewhere to go. The Missouri Attorney General enforces Missouri’s Merchandising Practices Act, which covers deception, false promises and misrepresentation in connection with the sale of merchandise, and the office takes consumer complaints directly. In Illinois, you can file a complaint with the Illinois Attorney General. Pay by card rather than cash wherever you can, because a card leaves you a dispute path and cash leaves you nothing.
### Is it cheaper to rekey or replace locks?
Rekeying is almost always cheaper, because you are buying labor on hardware you already own. The locksmith pulls the cylinder, swaps the pin stacks so a new key turns and the old one doesn’t, and slides it back. Nothing gets purchased but pins and keys. Replacing means new hardware on top of the same labor, so it costs more by definition.
Rekey when the locks work fine and the real problem is who has a key. A move-in. A lost keyring. A contractor who never gave one back. A roommate who left on bad terms. It is also how you get a house that opens on one key, which is a labor line rather than a shopping trip when the locks already share a keyway.
Replace when the hardware itself is the problem. A bolt that binds and needs your shoulder to throw. A cylinder worn loose enough to turn with the wrong key. A knob where a deadbolt belongs. Builder-grade hardware chosen because it was cheap in bulk. Replace, too, when the keyway is obsolete or the brand is one nobody stocks pins for anymore.
One caution people learn too late: not every lock can be rekeyed at your door. Restricted and patented high-security cylinders are serviced through authorized dealers, and some cheap hardware is not really rebuildable at all. Read the brand off the face of the lock and say it on the phone. It changes the quote, and occasionally the trade you need.
### What’s the average price to change a door lock?
No honest average exists for this metro, and inventing one would be a guess dressed up as research. What is knowable is what moves the number: hardware grade, whether the door is already bored, how many locks are in the job, whether you want them keyed alike, and when you want the work done.
Hardware grade is the biggest lever, and the one you fully control. Under the BHMA standards accredited by ANSI, locks are assigned one of three grades, with Grade 1 the highest level of performance and Grade 3 considered the least secure. You can feel the difference in the store: the heavier grade has a bolt that throws with a solid, oiled clunk instead of a tinny snap, and the price climbs right along with it.
Volume works in your favor. The trip charge gets paid once whether the technician changes one lock or six, so a whole-house change in a single visit costs less per door than the same six doors spread across three appointments. Moving in? Book the front, the back, the side and the garage entry together and ask for them keyed alike.
Then the two questions that decide the labor. Is the door already drilled for what you are installing, or does it need a new bore? And is anything about it non-standard: a steel door, a mortise lock in an older brick two-family, a storm door in the way, a jamb that has shifted. Say all of it on the phone and the quote will survive contact with the actual door.
### How much does a handyman charge to replace door locks?
Usually less per hour than a locksmith, and the comparison that matters is scope, not rate. A handyman installs the lock you bought. A locksmith can rekey a cylinder, key four doors alike, originate a key when there is no original, and open a lock without wrecking it. If your job is unboxing a deadbolt and driving screws, the cheaper trade really is cheaper.
The line moves the moment anything is not standard. Boring a door that has never had a deadbolt. A strike that will not line up. An old mortise body. Any request to make two different locks open on one key. That is locksmith work, and paying a handyman rate for it usually turns into two trips and both bills.
Whoever you hire, the vetting is the same. Inside city limits, anyone who conducts business must obtain a city business license, so the same search works on whoever you hire. Proof of liability insurance and a written scope are worth more than any title printed on a business card.
### Can I replace a door lock myself?
Often, yes, on a standard residential door that is already bored. Modern deadbolts and knobsets are built for it: two screws through the cylinder, a bolt assembly in the edge of the door, a strike plate on the jamb. If the new lock matches what came out, it is a short job and the only tool you need is a screwdriver.
Measure before you buy. Backset is the distance from the edge of the door to the center of the bore, and standard backsets are either 2-3/8 or 2-3/4 inches. Measure the bore itself and the hole in the door edge too, and match them to the box. Many retail locks ship with an adjustable latch that handles either backset.
While the strike plate is off, do the upgrade that costs almost nothing. Pull the short screws, feel how little they were holding, and drive long screws that reach through the jamb and bite into the framing behind it. A kicked door almost never fails at the lock. It fails at the jamb, in a spray of splinters. A few minutes here may be the best use of a screwdriver in this whole article.
Call somebody when the door needs a new bore, when the hardware is mortise, when the door is steel or fire-rated, when the strike will not align because the frame has moved, or when you want several doors on one key. Cutting a spare is a separate errand, covered in our guide to St. Louis hardware stores.
Want a locksmith with a real address, not just a phone number? Browse locksmiths across the St. Louis metro on St Louis Near Me Directory, then ask the same three things every time: the legal business name, the street address, and the all-in total texted to you before anyone is dispatched.
If you run a lock shop with a sign on a real building, this is the reader looking for you. A listing puts your legal name and street address where a locked-out neighbor can check them, which is how an honest shop gets more customers from the people burned by the teaser price. List your shop here.
### Can I get my locks changed for free?
Rarely, and only in situations where somebody else pays. None of them involve a locksmith working for nothing. Free lock work almost always means the cost moved onto a landlord, a builder, an insurer or a program. Knowing which one applies to you is the difference between asking and paying.
If you rent, read the lease before you call anyone. The lock is the landlord’s hardware, and many leases require written permission plus a copy of any new key. Ask in writing, keep the reply, and ask directly who pays. A landlord who already rekeys between tenants has answered the whole question before you spend a dollar.
If you just bought the house, check the closing packet, because a rekey is sometimes included by the builder or bundled into a first-year warranty plan. If your keys were stolen or the house was broken into, read the homeowners or renters policy: lock replacement is covered on some, sits under a deductible that makes a claim pointless on others, and only the policy can tell you which. If you are changing locks for safety reasons, ask a local victim-services agency what help it offers.
What should be free is the diagnosis. A locksmith worth hiring will tell you over the phone whether your situation is a rekey or a replacement, without sending anybody or charging for the call. If the lock change is really the first move in a bigger decision about doors, sensors and monitoring, what a home security system actually includes covers the wider version of the same question.
### Why the late-night number is higher
A locksmith sells drive time and tooling, not parts. The cost that quietly eats the day is the unbillable driving between jobs: fuel, the interstate, and no invoice in between. Add the van full of tooling: key machines, code software, pinning kits, transponder and fob programmers, and enough parts to finish a job on the first visit instead of the third.
Locked out after hours tonight? Here’s what an emergency locksmith costs in St. Louis.
So a fair after-hours premium is not greed. It is a person pulling on boots in a dark house because you called, and a shop paying for someone to be reachable at all. The premium you should refuse is the one that appears only after the door is open. Stated up front, texted to your phone, tied to a legal name you could look up: that is a price. Everything else is a surprise.
### Frequently asked questions
### Q. Is it cheaper to rekey or replace locks?
A.  Rekeying is cheaper nearly every time, because it is labor on hardware you already own: the pin stacks change, the old key stops working, nothing is purchased but pins and keys. Replace when the hardware itself is worn, binding, obsolete or the wrong type for the door. Restricted and high-security cylinders are the exception, since those are serviced through authorized dealers.
### Q. What’s the average price to change a door lock?
A.  No reliable average exists for the St. Louis metro, and any single figure published for it is a guess. Five things move the price: the ANSI/BHMA grade of the hardware, whether the door is already bored, how many locks are in the job, whether you want them keyed alike, and the time of day. Doing every exterior door in one visit spreads the trip charge across all of them.
### Q. How much does a handyman charge to replace door locks?
A.  Generally a lower hourly rate than a locksmith, which is genuinely cheaper when the job is installing hardware you already bought on a door that is already drilled. It stops being cheaper the moment the work needs a new bore, an old mortise body, a misaligned strike, or several doors keyed alike. Ask for proof of liability insurance and a written scope either way.
### Q. Can I replace a door lock myself?
A.  Usually, on a standard residential door with an existing bore. Measure the backset first: standard backsets are either 2-3/8 or 2-3/4 inches, from the door edge to the center of the bore. While the strike plate is off, swap the short screws for long ones that reach the framing. Call a professional for new bores, mortise hardware, steel doors or keyed-alike work.
### Q. Can a handyman install a door lock?
A.  Yes, and on a standard pre-bored door it is routine handyman work. What a handyman typically cannot do is rekey a cylinder, key several doors alike, originate a key when no original exists, or open a locked door without damaging it. Confirm who is buying the hardware, confirm liability insurance, and get the scope in writing before work starts.
### Q. Can I get my locks changed for free?
A.  Occasionally, though it means someone else is paying rather than the work being free. Renters should check the lease, since the lock is the landlord’s hardware and many landlords rekey between tenants. New buyers should check the closing packet and any first-year warranty. After a theft or break-in, read the homeowners or renters policy. The phone diagnosis, at least, should cost nothing.

## What a Life Coach Costs vs $20-an-Hour Therapy at UMSL
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/blog/what-a-life-coach-costs-in-st-louis
Twenty dollars an hour. That is the bottom of the sliding scale for psychotherapy at the University of Missouri-St. Louis Center for Psychological Growth, in the University Eye Center Building at 7840 Natural Bridge Rd. The top of the scale is $125. You bring your most recent tax return, an intake worker asks a few questions over the phone, and your fee is set by your household income and how many people live under your roof.
Now hold that number next to the tab you have open. The coach with the soft-lit headshot, the calendar link, the “transformation package” and no price anywhere on the page. You can feel the knot already: you want help, you are not sure what kind, and the one thing you are sure of is that you cannot afford to pay twice.
If that number is the one you needed, you can act on it before you close this tab: call (314) 516-5771, tell intake you want adult therapy, and have your most recent tax return within reach so they can set your fee on the call.
Here is the part nobody puts on a sales page. In Missouri, the person with the lower price may be the one with years of supervised clinical training behind them, and the person with the higher price may have needed nothing at all to start charging. Coaching and therapy are not two flavors of the same thing. One sits under state licensing law. The other does not. That line decides what you pay, whether insurance touches any of it, and whether the help you buy fits what is actually wrong.
### What is a life coach not allowed to do?
Missouri law says no person may call themselves a psychologist, a professional counselor or a counselor, or practice psychology or professional counseling, without a state license. So a life coach without one of those licenses has to stay out of that work. When a session turns clinical, a good coach refers you to a licensed therapist instead.
Put the two screens side by side and the difference stops being abstract. On one, a booking page: a pastel button, a box for your card number, maybe a checkbox saying coaching is not therapy, and nothing else between you and the charge. On the other, a phone ringing in an office on Natural Bridge, a person asking how many people live in your house, and a fee that moves with your answer. Only one of those two is answerable to the state.
Missouri’s rules for the second one live in Chapter 337 of the state statutes, which covers psychologists, professional counselors, social workers, and marital and family therapists. Section 337.505 says no person may use the title “professional counselor” or “counselor,” or practice professional counseling here, without the license. And section 337.510 sets the bar: a master’s, specialist’s or doctoral degree with a major in counseling, and for someone with a master’s, at least two years of acceptable supervised counseling experience after the degree.
Two years of a supervisor reading your case notes and asking why you said what you said. That is what stands behind the word “counselor” on a Missouri office door. Behind “life coach” stands whatever that coach chose to do. Some trained hard and logged real hours. Some bought a domain name last month. On a website the two look identical.
So read a coach’s site the way you would read a lease. “Trauma work” is clinical territory. So is an offer to help you “heal” anxiety, depression, PTSD or an eating disorder. So is any hint that you could taper off a medication, or that therapy is something you have outgrown. None of that is style. It is someone standing on the wrong side of the only line the field has.
### What a coach costs, and why nobody can tell you
The UMSL clinic puts its fee range in writing: $20 to $125 an hour for psychotherapy. If a coach’s page shows no price at all, take that as your cue to ask for one, and ask two or three coaches the same question before you choose, because the answers for what sounds like the same hour can land far apart.
That is why the honest move is to stop comparing session rates and ask for one number: the total cost of the whole engagement, in writing, before your card leaves your wallet. A coach who quotes a modest hourly figure but only sells a long block of sessions has quoted you a much bigger decision than it sounded like on the call. Ask what happens if you want to stop partway. Watch how fast the answer comes.
Then run the comparison most people never run. (For contrast, here is what therapeutic massage costs in St. Louis, a wellness service with a state board behind it.) If your problem is a stuck goal, coaching may be worth whatever it costs you. If your problem is the ceiling you stare at when you should be asleep, the appetite that disappeared, the dread on the drive to work, the price question flips. A sliding-scale clinic on Natural Bridge can cost less per hour than a coach, and the person across from you is training under a licensed system built for exactly that weight.
The Center for Psychological Growth describes itself as the primary practicum training site for graduate students in UMSL’s Doctoral Program in Clinical Psychology. It offers adult therapy, child and family therapy, couples and group therapy, and psychological testing. The fee conversation happens on that first phone call, before you ever sit in a waiting room.
### Will insurance cover a life coach?
Don’t count on it. Before you pay a coach, ask your plan directly whether coaching is covered, and budget as if the answer is no: out of pocket, every session, for as long as you keep going.
Therapy is a different financial product, and that surprises people. According to HealthCare.gov, all Marketplace plans cover mental health and substance abuse services as essential health benefits, including behavioral health treatment such as psychotherapy and counseling. Coverage and cheap are not the same word, so check your own plan’s network and copay before you book. But for an insured adult the therapist is very often the cheaper hour, because a copay is a fraction of a cash rate and a coach has no copay to offer.
“I’ll just hire a coach, it’s cheaper.” People say it all the time. On the arithmetic it is often wrong. If what you needed was treatment, it is always wrong.
Different kind of hunger - here’s where to find the best cheap eats in St. Louis.
One more pot of money is worth one email. Many employers run an employee assistance program that includes a handful of counseling sessions, and some pay for executive coaching out of a separate training budget. Those are two different budgets at the same company. Ask HR about both before you assume you are paying alone.
### Stuck or struggling?
The fastest useful test is one question. Stuck is a working life with a goal you keep not reaching: the job you have not applied for, the business you have not started, the habit that will not hold. Struggling is something pressing on your sleep, your work, your appetite or the people you love. Stuck is coaching territory. Struggling is clinical territory, and that is not a soft suggestion.
The edges blur. Burnout, grief and a hard divorce can look like either one from the outside. Here is the tiebreaker we would use: if it has sat on you for weeks rather than days, if it followed you into the things you used to enjoy, or if someone who loves you has said something out loud about it, start with a licensed clinician. A therapist can rule things in and out. A coach cannot, and is not allowed to try.
It is not either-or forever. Plenty of people see a therapist and a coach at the same time for two different jobs. What matters is the order. Get steady first, then build.
And the part that outranks every price on this page: if you are in crisis or need emotional support, reach out to 988, the national mental health hotline, by call, text or chat. The 988 Lifeline is available 24/7/365, and the conversation is free and confidential. If cost is what stops you from getting ongoing help, our guide to free and low-cost mental health and substance-use help in St. Louis maps the options.
### Ten minutes that tell you who you are paying
You can check a therapist yourself. Before a first appointment, check a counselor, social worker or psychologist with the Missouri Division of Professional Registration at pr.mo.gov, whose home page lists a Licensee Search. If verification matters for whatever you are carrying in the door, that gap is your answer.
For a coach, the free consultation call is the only interview you get. It is a sales call, and that is fine. Use it. Ask these, out loud, and listen for hesitation:
Do you hold any state license, and if so, which one?
What training or credential do you have, and who issued it?
What is the total cost of a full engagement in dollars?
How do we decide we are finished?
What happens if I stop halfway, and is any of it refundable?
What do you do when a client brings you something clinical, and who do you refer to?
Can I read the written agreement before I pay?
Then the red flags. A coach who offers to treat a mental health condition. A coach who talks you out of therapy or medication. A guaranteed outcome. A discount that expires while you are still on the call. A package you can never cancel. A refusal to say a total price. And no written agreement at all, which matters more than it sounds: with no licensing board behind coaching, that document is the only rulebook you will have.
### How long should you have a life coach?
As long as there is a finish line you can name. If you cannot say what would make you stop, you have bought a subscription instead of a service, and the person you are paying has every commercial reason not to bring that up.
Write the exit condition down in the first session, in plain words. Not “feel better about my career,” which never resolves. Something you could check off: applied to a set number of roles, had a set number of conversations, made the decision by a date you pick. Now you can judge the money without consulting your feelings about the coach, whom you will probably like by then. That fondness is exactly why people renew engagements that quietly stopped working.
Some people keep a coach on a light cadence for years, and that can be legitimate when the goal keeps changing. If your sessions a year in sound like your sessions in the first month, the engagement ended a while ago and nobody said it out loud.
Want to compare a coach and a licensed therapist side by side before you spend a dollar? Browse wellness and mental health providers across the St. Louis metro on St Louis Near Me Directory, then ask the first three questions above on your first call.
If you’re the coach, counselor or therapist with the written agreement and the referral list ready, you are exactly who a cautious buyer wants to hire. A Gold listing puts your credentials, your scope and your price structure where people comparing their options are already looking, so you get more customers who already know what you do and what you don’t.
