## St. Louis Winter Date Ideas: A $1 Greenhouse and the Nights That Sell Out
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/blog/st-louis-winter-date-ideas
A dollar each gets two cold pairs of hands into the Jewel Box in Forest Park, and the glass house pays you back fast: a fountain splashing somewhere ahead, scarves coming off, the feeling flooding back into your fingers so fast it almost hurts. On Monday and Tuesday mornings it costs nothing at all.
Its Saturday window is two hours, 9 to 11 a.m., and that’s it. Garden Glow at the Missouri Botanical Garden fails the other way: the Garden says its tickets tend to sell out well in advance.
One date needs an alarm clock. The other needs a calendar.
And this winter the blades come back. “This winter, we’ll enjoy ice skating in Forest Park once again!” is how Forest Park Forever puts it, after the City of St. Louis closed Steinberg Rink for renovations and said plainly that visitors to Forest Park would miss a season of ice skating.
### What are good St. Louis winter date ideas?
Pair a stretch of honest cold with a warm room right after. Stand in the wind at Ted Drewes on Chippewa holding a concrete so dense it can be served upside down, teeth aching. Then the car door slams, the heater roars, and the cold you just stood in becomes the part of the night you both retell.
The rest of this page is the warm half: a dollar greenhouse, two light walks with fire pits, a rink coming back to life and a free hill for when it snows. Each one comes with the hour or the booking rule that decides whether the night works.
### The dollar greenhouse in Forest Park
The Jewel Box sits at Wells and McKinley drives in Forest Park, an Art Deco glass house the city built in 1936, with glass walls rising 50 feet. Admission is $1 per person, and the City of St. Louis parks page says it is free on Monday and Tuesday from 9 a.m. until noon. Two people, two dollars. Or nothing at all, if one of you can slip away on a Tuesday morning.
Step in from the parking lot and the dry sting on your face turns soft and damp. There is a new heating and air conditioning system, so it stays comfortable inside in the coldest weather, and you feel it in your fingers first. A large fountain splashes in the floral display area. Baskets of plants hang overhead. Coats come open, scarves come off, and you can hear the water over the low talk of whoever else wandered in out of the wind.
The catch is the clock. Monday through Thursday it stays open from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., Friday from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., and Sunday from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m. The Saturday window is the short one, so set an alarm: coffee in the cupholder, defrost on high, through the door early, and back out into the cold before brunch. The fountain can be removed for weddings and other events, so call the Jewel Box at 314-531-0080 before you go.
### Which St. Louis winter dates need a reservation?
Your breath hangs in front of millions of lights, and the only warm thing for a hundred yards is the cup in your hands. Garden Glow runs on select nights from November 14 through January 2 at the Missouri Botanical Garden, and the Garden says plainly that it is a limited-capacity event whose tickets tend to sell out well in advance, especially from mid-December through January 1. Adult general admission bought at or after 4:30 p.m. for the same night costs $2 more, and the Glow is closed December 24 and 25, so the “let’s just go on Christmas Eve” idea never makes it past the car.
The night couples should circle is Jingle and Mingle on Friday, November 20, 7 to 9:30 p.m., a Garden Glow experience just for grown-ups with a complimentary drink included with your ticket, and ages 21 and older only after 6 p.m.
The other one is a fire of your own. Public fire pits for warming and s’mores sit at Central Axis and Linnean Plaza, and the Garden warns that smoke and burning embers will be present, so your coat will smell like a campfire until morning. A VIP fire pit is a different animal: it holds up to 20 guests, must be reserved at least 24 hours ahead along with your Glow tickets, and cannot be bought that night.
The path is about a mile and takes 45 minutes to an hour, long enough for the cold to creep into your boots and short enough that nobody turns grumpy. Parking is free in the two lots at Shaw and Vandeventer, with a shuttle running on every Glow evening.
Book the warm half of the night before you plan the cold half. Garden Glow is the one that sells out, so pick your night on the Missouri Botanical Garden’s Garden Glow page first, then fill in dinner from our date-night restaurant guide.
If you run the cafe, the wine bar or the hot chocolate counter couples duck into to thaw out, a listing on St Louis Near Me Directory puts you in front of the customers already searching for the warm half of their winter date.
### The zoo after dark, with s’mores
Sticky marshmallow on cold fingers, woodsmoke caught in your scarf, and light displays strung across Historic Hill. Wild Lights at the Saint Louis Zoo runs on select nights from November 27 through December 30, 5 to 8:30 p.m., with last entry at 8 p.m. The Zoo’s own pitch is to roast s’mores over firepits and meet the big man himself, Santa, and this year the walk has an expanded footprint across Historic Hill.
Tickets are $19 general admission and $16 for Zoo members, and parking is free on both Zoo lots, as available. The Zoo warns that popular dates may sell out quickly. You can still buy online the night of the event if tickets are left, which makes it the better bet for a date you decide on at lunch.
One timing note for couples. Penguin & Puffin Coast closes at 8 p.m., so walk there first while your hands still work, then take the long way back past the lights. There is also a sensory-friendly night on December 7, if a quieter, calmer walk suits the two of you better.
### Is Steinberg Rink back for skating this winter?
It should be. Steinberg is being restored as part of the Glade, a 22.5-acre site with indoor and outdoor spaces for year-round activities in Forest Park, and the City of St. Louis said it would reopen in the fall. The rink keeps its size, and the city calls it the largest outdoor ice skating rink in the Midwest. People have skated there since 1957.
What changes is the part between laps. The Commons is where Forest Park Forever says visitors will shake off the cold in winter, and a long shade structure down the rink’s west side, the Farr Family Lawn Terrace, is meant to be a covered space with fire pits in cooler months. That is a date with the warm half built in. Blades scraping, cheeks burning, then a seat by the fire to watch everyone else wobble.
What I could not find posted anywhere: an opening day or a skate price. Check Forest Park Forever before you promise anyone a night on the ice, and see our page on what ice skating costs in St. Louis for the other rinks in the meantime.
People are asking
### What winter events are on in St. Louis?
The big recurring St. Louis winter events are the light walks. Garden Glow fills the Missouri Botanical Garden with millions of lights on select nights from November 14 through January 2, and Wild Lights runs at the Saint Louis Zoo on select nights from November 27 through December 30, 5 to 8:30 p.m. Both can sell out, so buy tickets ahead. Steinberg Rink in Forest Park is also set to reopen for skating this fall after a season closed for renovations.
### Which St. Louis winter dates cost almost nothing?
Start on Art Hill in Forest Park, home to winter sledding. After a real snow, bring a sled, a thermos and dry socks for the car. Park hours run 6 a.m. to 10 p.m., so a snowy run under the streetlights is fair game as long as you are off the hill by closing.
Add a free Monday or Tuesday morning at the Jewel Box and the whole outing costs you the gas. Snow on your jeans, a fogged-up windshield, two people laughing too hard to find the defrost button.
For a low budget date with a little ceremony to it, go to Ted Drewes on Chippewa. The stand has served frozen custard on Historic Route 66 since 1941, and the Chippewa location lists hours of 11 a.m. to 10:30 p.m. every day. It is a walk-up stand with limited seating, which means you eat it standing in the cold. Your date steals a bite anyway.
From the day after Thanksgiving, Ted Drewes also sells pine and fir Christmas trees. Walk the rows with a cup between your gloves and the air smells like a forest that took a wrong turn onto Chippewa.
Somebody in Missouri is already arguing about which town is the most Christmassy.
### How to stack it into one winter night
On a weekday, start at the Jewel Box before it closes at 4 p.m. and let your hands thaw. If it snowed, take the sled to Art Hill while there is still light. Then drive to Shaw for the Garden Glow night you booked weeks ago, $24 a person on a General Admission night. Depending on the night, the Glow runs 5 to 9:30 p.m. or 4:30 to 10 p.m. End on Chippewa with custard before the window closes at 10:30 p.m. Cold, warm, cold, warm, and a night that feels planned because it was.
Swap the Glow for Wild Lights if you want the zoo instead, and remember the earlier finish: last entry there is 8 p.m. Either way, the order is the trick. Never end a winter date in the cold.

### Q. What do couples do for fun at night?

### Q. What is a lowkey date idea?
A.  A Tuesday morning at the Jewel Box, where it is free until noon, warm inside and quiet except for the fountain. Add a hot chocolate after, and you are home by lunch having spent almost nothing.
### Q. Can we still go to Garden Glow if it snows?
A.  Usually, yes. The Garden holds its events rain, snow or shine unless the weather is dangerous or extreme. If a night is cancelled, you can present your tickets on another Glow evening with no exchange needed; a regular date change otherwise costs a $20 fee per transaction.

## Free Room, $1,000 Bill: St. Louis Restaurants With Private Rooms
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/blog/st-louis-restaurants-with-private-rooms
A ten-seat private dining room can charge no rental fee and still cost you $1,000. That’s the part most people get backwards: the free room is the expensive one, and you learn it after the door clicks shut, the room goes quiet and the check folder lands beside your plate.
### How do St. Louis restaurants with private rooms charge for them?
Most charge one of three ways: a food and beverage minimum your group has to spend, a flat room fee, or a required set menu, and many want a deposit to hold the date. The service charge and sales tax then land on top of whatever the food and drinks came to.
At Cleaver & Cocktail, the 10-person private dining room has no rental fee, but the party must meet a food and beverage minimum of $1,000, and the $250 deposit is non-refundable, though it goes toward your final bill. Put ten people in those ten chairs and you are at $100 a head before anyone has opened a menu.
On the Hill, the LaSorda Room at Charlie Gitto’s seats up to 12 guests and rents in two-hour blocks for a $200 room rental fee. The restaurant also reserves the right to add minimum charges for a private event, so a room fee is not always the whole story.
Then there’s the third model, the set menu. At Helen Fitzgerald’s, the two banquet rooms each seat 45 for dinner, carry a $100 deposit credited to your final bill, and require you to choose one of the preplanned menus. Their smaller Board Room works on spend instead: at least 15 guests and a required $250 food and beverage spend over two hours.
Here is what that money buys. The server pulls the door shut behind the last plate, and the clatter of the main dining room drops to a murmur. For the first time all night, everyone at the table can hear one person talk. Somebody taps a glass with a butter knife, stands up, and nobody at the next table turns around, because there is no next table. At the end of the night the same server sets the check folder at the head of the table, and every model above is waiting inside it.
If you are still weighing a restaurant against a rented hall, start with our guide on how to book a banquet hall in St. Louis. If the answer is a restaurant, keep reading.
### How much does private dining cost per person?
Divide the minimum by the people you expect, and you have your real price per person.
The spread in St. Louis is wide. Helen Fitzgerald’s Tap Room takes 8 to 12 guests with a required $200 food and beverage spend for two hours. Split across eight people, that’s $25 each. At the other end, Vicia seats 8 to 14 guests at its semi-private chef’s grill table beside the wood-fired hearth, with a $105 per person food and beverage minimum and a deposit required. You sit close enough to watch the fire that cooks the larger plates.
Now the trap. A minimum does not shrink when your guest list does. Say you book Cleaver & Cocktail’s ten-person room and two cousins text you the morning of the dinner that they can’t make it. The minimum is still $1,000. Eight people are now carrying it, which is $125 each, and the two empty chairs at the end of the table still have folded napkins on the plates.
So book the minimum against the head count you are sure of, not the one you hope for. If you land short on the night, expect to pay the difference for food nobody ate. Ask ahead of time whether you can put any shortfall toward something you would want anyway, like a bottle for the table or desserts boxed to take home. Asking at the table, with the check folder already in your hand, is the expensive way to learn the answer.
### The 20 percent that sits outside the minimum
Twenty percent, plus sales tax. Helen Fitzgerald’s states plainly that all its banquet menus are subject to sales tax and a 20 percent service charge, and Charlie Gitto’s asks that parties of 6 or more be on one check with a 20% automatic gratuity. Neither number counts toward a food and beverage minimum.
You flip open the check folder, run a finger down to the subtotal, and there’s another line under it. So at Helen Fitzgerald’s rate, a $1,000 food and beverage total plus a 20 percent service charge of $200 comes to $1,200, and the sales tax still lands on top of that.
There’s a Missouri wrinkle almost nobody knows. According to the Missouri Department of Revenue’s catering tax guidance, a mandatory gratuity is exempt from sales tax only when all three conditions are met: it is imposed only on large groups, at least some of the money is paid to employees, and Missouri income tax is withheld from the employees on it. Miss any one of those and the gratuity is taxable. A mandatory gratuity imposed on all sales is taxable too.
That’s why two restaurants with the same 20 percent charge can hand you different totals. When you read the bottom of the quote, look for three numbers stacked under the subtotal, not one. Ask what the charge is called, whether it reaches the servers who carried your plates, and whether tax is figured on it. You are reading the receipt before it exists.
### Will you get the deposit back?
Is a restaurant deposit refundable? Read the exact word on the form. “Credited” means it comes off your bill if you show up. “Refundable” means it comes back if you don’t. Those are two different promises, and a contract can make one without the other.
Helen Fitzgerald’s $100 room deposit is credited to the final bill. Neither of those says you get the money back if the rehearsal dinner moves.
Some places do spell out a refund window. The Hartford Reserve, the private room inside Hartford Coffee Company, takes a 50% deposit to hold your date and refunds it in full if you cancel 5 or more days before. Cancel less than 5 days before and the deposit is non-refundable, and if you book within 5 days of your reservation date, the deposit is non-refundable from the moment of booking. Contact them at least 48 hours before your reservation and they will move your booking to another available date at no charge, one reschedule per booking.
That’s the shape of a clear policy: a deadline, a dollar amount and a reschedule rule. If the room you want can’t tell you all three, you have learned something about it already. The card receipt folded in your wallet should match what the manager said on the phone.
Unrelated, but the person doing your face that morning has a price too.
### What should you ask before you book the room?
Shortlist two or three rooms and call each one. Tell them the date, the head count you are sure of and the all-in number you want to spend, tax and service included, then compare what each one will deliver side by side.
On that call, ask whether the minimum counts before or after tax and the service charge, and what happens if you come in under it. Ask whether you order off the regular menu or pick a set menu. Ask how long the room is yours. At Helen Fitzgerald’s the banquet rooms are allotted 4 hours, each extra hour is $100 and needs a manager’s okay, and decorations can come in no sooner than a half hour before your event. A half hour is enough for a few balloons and a framed photo. It is not enough for a centerpiece project.
Ask about wine and cake. Vicia, for one, lets guests bring a bottle that is not on its list for a $35 charge per 750mL bottle, and waives the fee if you buy a bottle from the list. And ask the plainest question of all: is this room fully private, with a door, or semi-private? Helen Fitzgerald’s calls its Fish Room semi-private, and Vicia’s grill table is semi-private. You will hear the rest of the restaurant from either one. For a toast with a cracked voice in it, that matters.
Where to make those calls, straight from each restaurant’s own private events page:
Cleaver & Cocktail: call 314-530-9700 or use the form on its private events page.
Charlie Gitto’s On the Hill: (314) 772-8898, or the private events inquiry on its site.
Helen Fitzgerald’s: (314) 984-0026.
Vicia: the private events inquiry link on its page.
The Hartford Reserve: book online on its event space page.
The Chase Club: (314) 454-9000.
Your guest list is the one number you control, so book the room around it. When a restaurant room is too small or the minimum is too steep, compare Banquet Halls on St Louis Near Me Directory and call two or three before you put down a deposit.
If you’re the restaurant with a back room and a door that closes, the planners are already searching. People hunting for a rehearsal dinner or a retirement party look here for a room, so list your business and give them yours to book.
### Bigger groups, buyouts and the parking question
In the Central West End, the Chase Club requires a minimum of 20 guests for semi-private or fully private events and can take up to 200 with its patio terrace. Its event coordinator sets minimums by party size, time of day and length of party, and private events get comped valet and garage parking with validation. Charlie Gitto’s Garden Room takes up to 100 guests, and full restaurant buyouts are available, with On the Hill’s full capacity at 180.
Parking sounds like a small thing until your aunt is circling the block in the rain. If guests are driving in from Scott Air Force Base or Winfield, a validated garage is worth more than a fancier appetizer.

### Frequently asked questions
### Q. What does minimum spend mean at a restaurant?
A.  It is the least your group must spend on food and drinks for the room. Helen Fitzgerald’s Board Room, for example, carries a required $250 food and beverage spend over two hours. If you spend less, expect to pay the difference.
### Q. What does food beverage minimum mean?
A.  It is the same idea: a floor on what the party orders in food and drinks, often in place of a room fee. Cleaver & Cocktail charges no rental fee for its 10-person room but requires a $1,000 food and beverage minimum.
### Q. Is a restaurant deposit refundable?
A.  Often it is credited, not refunded. Cleaver & Cocktail’s $250 deposit is non-refundable but goes toward the bill, while The Hartford Reserve refunds its deposit in full if you cancel 5 or more days ahead. Read the exact word on your form.
### Q. Is private dining worth it?
A.  For a toast, a speech or a group that needs to hear itself think, usually yes. You get a closed door, your own server team and often a set menu that keeps the night moving.
### Q. Is private dining more expensive?
A.  Not always per plate, but often in total, because minimums, room fees and service charges stack. Helen Fitzgerald’s adds sales tax and a 20 percent service charge to its banquet menus.
### Q. What is considered private dining?
A.  Any room or table a restaurant sets aside for one group, from a closed room with a door to a semi-private table. Vicia’s chef’s grill table for 8 to 14 guests is semi-private, while a full buyout gives you the entire restaurant.
### Q. Can you rent out a restaurant?
A.  Yes. Charlie Gitto’s says full restaurant buyouts are available, with On the Hill’s full capacity at 180, and the Chase Club’s full buyout seats 75. Expect a minimum set by date, time and length of the party.
### Q. How far ahead can you make dinner reservations?
A.  For private rooms, earlier is better; the Chase Club recommends booking as early as possible to secure your preferred date.
### Q. What do you call a private room in a restaurant?
A.  Most restaurants call it a private dining room, sometimes a banquet room or event room.

## File Before You Have a Sitter: Assistance for Single Mothers in Missouri
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/blog/assistance-for-single-mothers-in-missouri
The sitter doesn’t have a name yet. File anyway.
It’s late. The portal’s glow is the only light in the kitchen, a mug of coffee has gone cold on the corner of five forms, and down the hall a kid is breathing slow and even in sleep. One of those forms isn’t really a form.
### What kind of assistance can single mothers receive in Missouri?
The order matters more than the list. Child care goes first, because new families are waitlisted by the date they apply. One myDSS application for Temporary Assistance and MO HealthNet comes next: either one refers you to Child Support automatically, and Temporary Assistance makes you automatically eligible for WIC.
That one form is a place in a line you can’t see, and Missouri lines families up by the date they submit.
If you’ve read our guide to emergency cash and TANF help in Missouri, you already know the cash grant is small and slow. This page is about the stack, and the sequence, for a mom raising kids on her own in St. Louis. Some mornings a screen won’t do, and you want a face across a counter. The state’s Chouteau Resource Center sits at 3101 Chouteau St. Metro’s 31 Chouteau bus stops along that street at Grand, at Theresa and at Ewing. Ride it with the folder flat on your lap and the kids’ Social Security cards zipped in the front pocket.
Most moms work the list backwards. Rent is the loudest bill in the house, so the cash application goes in first, and the child care form waits until there’s a job offer and a sitter with a name. That instinct makes sense. It also costs you your place in line.
### The form that pays last goes in first
Missouri’s Child Care Subsidy Program now runs a waitlist for new applications. The state’s Office of Childhood says new families may be placed on it if funding is not available, and that they’re lined up by the date the application was submitted. The date you file is your ticket number, so when the confirmation screen loads, screenshot it. Every week you wait to file is a week further back in a line you can’t see.
That flips the usual order on its head. A mom who files on a Monday, before she’s picked a sitter, can sit ahead of a mom who files the week she lands the job. Once it comes, the approval letter does a second job in St. Louis: the Urban League Head Start, which serves 895 children from 6 weeks to 5 years old, lists a Child Subsidy Letter among the papers it takes as proof of income. And you don’t need the job yet. Missouri’s rules for families count needing care to work, to search for work, to train for a job or to attend school, for a child from birth to age 13.
The income limit for child care subsidy in Missouri is 150% of the federal poverty level. On the state’s own income chart, that tops out at $2,644 a month for a family of two and $3,331 a month for a family of three. Lay your last pay stub next to those numbers before you decide you earn too much. The waitlist doesn’t treat every family the same, either. Families are placed by application date and by a priority ranking, in the following order: children with special needs, children experiencing homelessness, families with income below 100% of the poverty level, then families above 100% that may be eligible. If your paycheck is thin, that ranking works for you, not against you.
It can feel strange, typing your kid’s birthday into a form for a sitter you haven’t met. It still counts. If the parent portal fights you, call 573-415-8605 and ask to speak to a Community Support Specialist. The state says help is available to families completing the application.
### Which one application quietly opens two more doors?
You’ll click Next on a lot of screens this week. One of them pays you back twice: the application for Temporary Assistance or MO HealthNet, the state’s Medicaid. File it through myDSS, and two more pieces of help start moving without you chasing them.
The first is child support. Missouri’s Department of Social Services says that if you get Temporary Assistance or MO HealthNet, you will automatically be referred to the Child Support program. That program can help locate the other parent, establish paternity, and set up and enforce a support order. You don’t dial a separate number or sit through a separate round of hold music; the referral rides along with the form you already sent. Moms on neither benefit have to apply for child support on their own, which means one more form, one more wait and one more envelope.
The second is WIC. Missouri’s WIC program says people on SNAP, Temporary Assistance and income-qualifying MO HealthNet are automatically eligible for WIC, and that families on those programs might get benefits without current proof of income. That’s one less pay stub to dig out from under the car seat. In the city, Affinia Healthcare offers WIC services at five of its locations, including 2220 Lemp Avenue and 3930 S. Broadway. Walk into the WIC clinic with your approval letter, and the letter does most of the talking.
MO HealthNet is worth filing even if you’re sure you earn too much for cash. Put the hold music on speaker, prop the phone against the sugar bowl and stir the oatmeal with your other hand. That one call opens more than any other.
### What does Temporary Assistance actually ask of a single mom?
More than the name suggests. At the counter on Chouteau, or on the couch with the laptop warm on your knees, the questions get personal fast. Who qualifies for cash assistance in Missouri is a narrow group: the parent or guardian of a child under 18 who lives in Missouri and doesn’t own resources worth more than $1,000 apart from a home and one vehicle. You’ll also answer questions about illegal drug use and agree to take a drug test if required.
The application comes with homework. You watch an orientation video first, earbuds in and the volume low enough to hear the kids stir. Then you complete a Personal Responsibility Plan and the Child Support Forms and send them in with the application, online at mydssupload.mo.gov or by fax to 573-526-9400. Once approved, you take part in the Missouri Work Assistance program. The Department of Social Services says processing can take up to 10 days, and the first payment lands on your EBT card or by direct deposit within 45 days.
One honest word about those child support pages. If the other parent is someone you need distance from, say so to the caseworker before you sign. Say it out loud, plainly, in the same voice you’d use to ask for a pen. Your safety is a fair question to raise, and asking it costs you nothing.

### How can a single mom get rental assistance in St. Louis?
Call the St. Louis Housing Help Line at (314) 802-5444. A housing specialist interviews you and, if you’re in crisis, refers you to rent or mortgage help or to emergency shelter. Our guide to emergency rent help in St. Louis lists every program, phone number and income limit in one place.
### What if you’re on no benefit and the support still never comes?
Apply for child support directly. You can do it online through myDSS, or print the paper application and send it to the Family Support Division by mail, email or fax at 573-635-7545. The state says it may take up to 20 business days to process. After that, a letter arrives with your case number, and you can check on your application at 573-556-3800.
Tape that letter inside the folder. Payments come by direct deposit or a prepaid card, and the case number is the first thing every person on every future phone call will ask you for.
### Your first week, in order
Clear one corner of the table before the kids are up. The folder, a pen that works, the phone on the charger so it doesn’t die halfway through the hold music. Here’s the whole sequence, so you can stop rereading the pile.
Day one, while the house is quiet: the Child Care Subsidy application, through the state’s parent portal, even before you have a sitter. Screenshot the confirmation screen. That date holds your place.
Same morning: one myDSS application for MO HealthNet and Temporary Assistance. Add SNAP if the fridge is down to milk and ketchup.
When the approval envelope shows up in the mailbox: WIC. Call Missouri WIC at 800-392-8209, and bring the letter.
If you weren’t referred: child support, applied for directly through myDSS or on paper.
Any day the bills land before the benefits do: 211, which points you to food and housing assistance.
Five steps, maybe two mornings at the table. Nobody hands you this list at a counter, so keep it with the folder.

### Frequently asked questions
### Q. What is the income limit for child care subsidy in Missouri?
A.  Families must be at or below 150% of the federal poverty level, have a child from birth to age 13 (or a child with special needs or in protective services), and need care to work, look for work, train or go to school. To see if you may be eligible, use the “Do I Qualify?” pre-screening tool on the DESE families page.
### Q. Is there free childcare available in Missouri?
A.  Yes, for some families. Head Start programs provide free learning and development services to children from birth to 5 in low-income families. In St. Louis, the Urban League Head Start provides center-based care from 7:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., takes a TANF letter, SNAP card or child subsidy letter as proof of income, and handles enrollment at (314) 867-9100.
### Q. Who qualifies for cash assistance in Missouri?
A.  Missouri’s Temporary Assistance is for a parent or guardian of a child under 18 who lives in Missouri, has resources of $1,000 or less (not counting a home and one vehicle), is under the income limit and has or applies for Social Security numbers for the household. Most adults on it also take part in the Missouri Work Assistance program.
### Q. What is a hardship grant for single mothers?
A.  Mostly a search term, not a program. USA.gov says the government does not offer “free money” for individuals, and that federal grants are typically only for states and organizations. For real help, start with 211, which connects local people to resources for food and housing. If anyone asks you for a fee to “release” a grant, hang up.
### Q. Where can I get immediate financial assistance?
A.  Call 211 first. Our emergency cash guide lists the St. Louis charities that give one-time help with rent and utilities.

## Most of Missouri Is Closed to Free Dentures. St. Louis Is Open: How to Qualify
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/blog/how-to-qualify-for-free-dentures-st-louis
Toasted ravioli was the first thing you stopped ordering. Then the steak, then the crust on anything. Now it’s soup at the kitchen table in Soulard, cooled so it won’t sting your gums, and you stopped pricing dentures a while ago.
### How do I qualify for free dentures?
Missouri Medicaid pays for dentures only if you are on MO HealthNet and pregnant, blind, under 21 or living in a nursing home.
That’s the whole list. Most working-age adults on Medicaid fall outside it, and in most cases Medicare doesn’t cover items like dentures either. But it isn’t a dead end.
A full upper denture averages $1,220 to $2,540 out of network. Most of Missouri is closed to the volunteer program that builds them for free, but St. Louis City and St. Louis County are open, so if you qualify, volunteer dentists and labs can build yours at no cost.
Our guide to free and low-cost dental care in St. Louis covers cleanings and same-day pain care. This page is only about one thing: getting your teeth back, and the first bite of an apple that comes with them.
### The free-denture door most St. Louisans never knock on
A 40-year-old crown breaking apart. Several molars gone, and no way left to chew. That was Richard, a Navy veteran and a veteran service manager at Missouri Veterans Endeavor (MOVE-STL), a nonprofit focused on housing for veterans. Through Dental Lifeline Network’s Donated Dental Services, a volunteer dentist restored five teeth, one lab donated a bridge and another donated a partial lower denture. His words: “It is a life changing experience.”
In Missouri the program works through volunteer dentists and volunteer dental labs. The labs matter. A denture isn’t drilled in a chair; it’s built at a bench from a mold of your mouth, and that bench work is a big part of the bill.
In Missouri, some of those benches work for free.
To apply in Missouri you must have no means to afford dental care and meet ONE of three criteria: 65 years of age or older, permanently disabled, or in need of medically necessary dental care. Counties open and close as slots fill, and the program’s list of counties now accepting applications includes both St. Louis and St. Louis City. They sit on it as two separate lines, just as the 1876 vote split the city from the county, so use the line that matches your address. If yours ever closes, you may still apply if you are a veteran who meets the qualifications, or if you have documentation from a physician stating that you cannot receive essential medical treatment due to your dental condition. The Missouri DDS coordinator’s number is 573-636-4440.
Now the honest part, so nothing surprises you. The application takes about 15 to 20 minutes. You’ll need a backup contact, your physician’s name and phone number, your medical conditions, and your income and expenses written out line by line. If you’re under 65, have your Social Security disability award letter ready; veterans should have a DD214. Then comes the hard part: the wait can run several months to a year or more, and the coordinators can’t return calls about your place in line. Final acceptance happens after your first visit with the volunteer dentist. You can only use the program once, emergencies and cosmetic work aren’t part of it, and implants, sedation and complex care may not be offered.
A year sounds long when you’re eating soup. It’s shorter than the years most people spend not applying at all.
### Does Missouri Medicaid cover dentures?
Slide your MO HealthNet card across the counter at St. Louis Community College’s dental hygiene clinic at 5600 Oakland Ave. and a cleaning costs you nothing: the clinic lists no charge for Veterans and Medicaid patients with valid ID. Dentures are a different story. For most adults on Medicaid, the answer is no, and your eligibility category, not the card, decides it. The state’s own dental page says coverage for adults is limited, built mostly around trauma to the mouth, jaw and teeth.
The denture rule is narrower still. The Missouri Department of Social Services names exactly four groups for whom dentures are a covered benefit: pregnant women, people in one of the assistance categories for the blind, people living in a nursing home with verified nursing-home eligibility, and anyone under 21. Dentures are not covered for anyone on a limited benefit package. When they are covered, full or partial, they don’t need prior authorization, so there’s one less form standing between you and the chair.
Here’s the line people miss. If your mother or your grandfather lives in a nursing home on Medicaid, dentures are on that list. The plate that clacks because the gums have shrunk, the one that went missing on a lunch tray, is worth a call to the facility to ask which dentist sees their residents.
Even when Medicaid won’t pay for the teeth themselves, keep it. The volunteer program above makes you use up every dental benefit you have first, Medicaid included. And the state health department notes that Medicaid can get you to a dental appointment through Non-Emergency Medical Transportation, so a missing ride doesn’t have to cancel a fitting. Not enrolled yet? Start with how to apply for MO HealthNet.
### Why won’t Medicare pay for my dentures?
Hand that same Oakland Avenue clinic a Medicare card at 65 and you get a 25% discount on a cleaning. Ask Original Medicare to pay for a denture and, in most cases, the answer is no. It was never built to. Medicare’s own coverage page says that in most cases, Medicare doesn’t cover dental services like routine cleanings, fillings, tooth extractions (removals), or items like dentures and implants.
There are narrow exceptions, and they’re tied to medical treatment, not to your smile: an oral exam and dental work before a heart valve replacement or an organ transplant, for example, or pulling an infected tooth before chemotherapy. If you chose a private Medicare plan, dig out its benefits booklet and look for the word dental. Original Medicare is the part that says no.
For seniors, though, age itself is the key that fits a different lock. Being 65 years of age or older is one of the three criteria for the volunteer program above, St. Louis City and St. Louis County are both on its open list, and nobody at the Medicare office is likely to mention it.
Unrelated, but someone should tell you which Missouri town out-Christmases the rest.
### What does a full set cost if every program says no?
Dentures are priced per arch, top and bottom, and the numbers are blunt. Delta Dental puts the average out-of-network cost of a complete upper denture at $1,220 to $2,540, and a complete lower at $1,115 to $2,425. The price generally covers the impressions of your mouth, the custom denture itself and the adjustments to make it fit.
That’s why the teaching clinic matters. The St. Louis Dental Center at 1500 Park Ave., where third- and fourth-year dental students work under faculty dentists, says its fees carry discounts of at least fifty percent from the St. Louis dental market, and that specific fees are explained before you receive treatment. The first visit includes x-rays, a look at your gums and bone, and impressions to make models: a cool, thick paste in a tray, held still while it sets. To schedule a first-time appointment, call 314-833-2758.
If you get Social Security disability, there’s one more piece people rarely hear about. The Missouri health department lists the Midwest Special Needs Trust’s charitable grant program, which gives small grants, up to $1500, to Missourians with a disability determined by the Social Security Administration, and dental care is one of the listed uses. It won’t buy a whole set at private-office prices. Paired with a teaching-clinic fee, it can close a gap.
### What should you do before the week is out?
Three moves, in this order. First, if you have MO HealthNet, find out your eligibility category, because that decides whether Medicaid pays for dentures at all. Second, if you’re 65 or older, disabled or medically fragile, fill out the Donated Dental Services application tonight; your place on that waitlist depends on when you submit, not when you feel ready. Third, book the comprehensive exam at the teaching clinic, so you have a written plan in hand whichever door opens first.
Don’t try to do all three tonight. Do the first one, and let the next bowl of soup be one of the last.

### Frequently asked questions
### Q. Does Medicare pay for dentures for senior citizens?
A.  In most cases, no. In most cases, Medicare doesn’t cover items like dentures and implants, with narrow exceptions tied to certain medical treatments. Seniors 65 and older who can’t afford care can apply to Dental Lifeline Network’s Donated Dental Services instead.
### Q. What type of dentures will Medicaid pay for?
A.  In Missouri, full and partial dentures are both covered, without prior authorization, but only for MO HealthNet members in four groups: pregnant women, people in an assistance category for the blind, nursing-home residents with verified eligibility, and anyone under 21. People on a limited benefit package are not covered for dentures.
### Q. Where can I get free dentures in Missouri?
A.  One free route is Donated Dental Services from Dental Lifeline Network, where volunteer dentists and labs treat people who are 65 or older, permanently disabled or in need of medically necessary care and can’t afford it. Its list of counties now accepting applications includes both St. Louis and St. Louis City. Call the Missouri DDS coordinator at 573-636-4440.
### Q. How to get dentures if you have no money?
A.  Apply to Donated Dental Services if you qualify, and expect a wait of several months to a year or more. If you receive Social Security disability, ask about the Midwest Special Needs Trust grant program, whose maximum grant award is $1500; grants may be requested for medical and dental care. Meanwhile, the St. Louis Dental Center explains its discounted fees before any treatment starts.
### Q. How much should I expect to pay for a full set of dentures?
A.  By Delta Dental’s average out-of-network figures, a complete upper denture runs $1,220 to $2,540 and a complete lower $1,115 to $2,425, and each arch is priced separately. The St. Louis Dental Center says its fees are at least fifty percent below the St. Louis dental market.
### Q. Is a full set of dentures top and bottom?
A.  It can be: a complete upper denture replaces all of the upper teeth and a complete lower replaces all of the lower teeth, and each is priced separately. If you still have some healthy teeth on one arch, a partial denture fills the gaps instead.
### Q. How do seniors afford dentures?
A.  If you are 65 years of age or older and have no means to afford dental care, you can apply to Donated Dental Services. Nursing-home residents on Medicaid have dentures covered by MO HealthNet. Others use the St. Louis Dental Center, where fees are discounted and explained up front.

## Take the House, Lose the Alimony: The Missouri Catch
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/blog/what-is-a-wife-entitled-to-in-a-divorce-in-missouri
Want the house? In Missouri, it can cost you the alimony.
You find that out at the kitchen table once the house goes quiet. The dishwasher ticks through its last cycle. The coffee you poured at supper has gone cold under your palm. The mortgage statement sits on one side of the table, the retirement summary with his name across the top sits on the other, and the number that tightens your chest is the one at the bottom of your own checking account.
Here is the catch, said plainly. The bigger your share of that house, the weaker your claim to maintenance, because Missouri counts the property you walk away with before it asks whether you need support. And in the City of St. Louis, the quiet divorce entered upon the affidavit of one party needs both of you represented by counsel the moment there is marital property to be divided.
### What is the wife entitled to in a divorce in Missouri?
As a wife in Missouri you are entitled to keep your own nonmarital property and to a just share of everything either of you acquired during the marriage, including the equity in the house and the marital part of a 401(k) or pension. Just does not mean half.
Maintenance, the thing most people call alimony, comes second, and it has two plain tests. Your share of the property can’t cover your reasonable needs. And you can’t support yourself through appropriate employment. Which makes the house and the alimony one negotiation, not two. Does taking the house cost you the alimony? It can. What you walk away with on paper decides the first test. The pay stub decides the second.
Before you call anyone, write down four numbers: what the house would sell for, what you still owe on it, the balance in every retirement account, and what you really spend in a month, groceries included. They are what the first test is built from, and the start of the folder you will bring to every lawyer.
And it runs both directions, which matters if you are the one with the bigger paycheck: RSMo 452.335 lets the court grant a maintenance order to either spouse.
If you were just served, start with our guide for anyone holding divorce papers in St. Louis and its parenting plan clock. This page covers the money: the house, the retirement account and the bank account with one name on it.
### What does filing look like at the courthouse door?
Your grocery bill is about to go under oath. But the security line comes first. Everyone walks through a metal detector and every bag, briefcase and folder goes through the screener. Scissors, pocket knives and needles are on the prohibited list, so the nail scissors stay in the kitchen drawer.
Then the third floor. The clerk’s office is in the Clyde S. Cahill Courts Building, 10 North Tucker Boulevard, and the circuit court’s divorce page says city residents may file there in person. A petition goes in the county where the petitioner resides.
Then the form. Under Local Rule 68.4 of the Twenty-Second Judicial Circuit, the clerk won’t accept a divorce petition until the income and expense statements are filed, completed under oath, and a number on the sworn form can’t say “varies” or “TBD” without approval of a family court judge. So the pen hovers over the grocery line, a number you have guessed at for years. Know it before you go.
If you hoped to skip the hearing, the same rulebook has a door for that. Local Rule 68.13 lets the court enter the final decree upon the affidavit of any party, but with a house or retirement account to divide, only if both of you are represented by counsel and have a written agreement on the split.
Fees and deposits vary by form, and the court says to contact the Circuit Clerk’s Office at 314-622-4044.
This is general information about Missouri law, not legal advice about your case.
### Property first, maintenance second, and the order is the whole game
Dig the car title out from under the takeout menus in the junk drawer and set it beside the mortgage statement, the retirement account summary and the credit card bill with the late fee circled in your own pen. That pile is the marriage on paper. Missouri looks at it twice, in a set order, and the first look decides the second.
Step one is the property. Under RSMo 452.330 the court sets apart each spouse’s nonmarital property, then divides the marital property and the marital debts in such proportions as it deems just. Step two is maintenance. And the first test for maintenance asks whether you lack sufficient property, including marital property apportioned to you, to provide for your reasonable needs.
Read that twice. The bigger the share of the house and the accounts you walk away with, the harder it is to show you need maintenance on top. A settlement that hands you the paid-down house can be the same settlement that ends the maintenance conversation.
The second reason the order matters is colder. The order dividing marital property is a final order not subject to modification. A modifiable maintenance order can later be decreased, increased or terminated after a substantial and continuing change of circumstances. The property split is the one decision you can’t come back and fix.
### Does it matter whose name is on the account?
Open the banking app and look at the top of the screen. One name. His, or yours. It feels like an answer, and it mostly isn’t.
Missouri presumes that all property acquired by either spouse after the marriage and before a decree of dissolution is marital property, regardless of whether title is held individually or jointly. The checking account in his name, the car titled to you alone: presumed marital if the money came in during the marriage.
The presumption can be beaten, but only by showing the property came in one of the listed ways: a gift, an inheritance, an exchange for something owned before the marriage, property excluded by a valid written agreement such as a prenup, or property acquired after a decree of legal separation. That means paper. The bank statement from before the wedding. The letter from the estate. The closing sheet from land a grandmother left to one of you.
One line protects people who mixed money without meaning to: nonmarital property does not become marital solely because it may have become commingled with marital property. If you can still trace an inheritance deposit by date, you sit in a far better seat than the spouse who can’t.
People are asking
### Can I get a divorce in Missouri without going to court?
Sometimes, if nothing is left to fight about. In the City of St. Louis, Local Rule 68.13 lets the court enter the final decree upon the affidavit of any party when there is no genuine issue as to any material fact and either there is no marital property to divide or both of you are represented by counsel and have signed a written agreement dividing it (children need the same: none, or lawyers and a written custody and support agreement). The affidavit does not shorten Missouri’s wait of thirty days after the petition is filed, and the judge can still order an evidentiary hearing.
### Who gets the house when there are children?
Listen to the house at bedtime: the creak on the third stair, the bathroom fan, a small voice asking for water. Nobody gets that house by default. But Missouri hands the judge one tool most couples don’t know exists. Among the factors in 452.330, the court weighs the desirability of awarding the family home, or the right to live therein for reasonable periods, to the spouse having custody of any children.
Or the right to live there. If you have the kids, the court can let you stay with them in the same bedrooms, the same creaking stair, the same walk to school, for a stretch it finds reasonable, with the equity dealt with later. For a family that can’t afford two mortgages, that clause can be the difference between the kids moving twice in a year and not moving at all.
Whether it fits also turns on each spouse’s contribution, homemaker included. Before anyone argues about the house, get its value on paper. An appraisal turns the fight from a feeling into a number.
### What happens to the 401(k) and the pension?
Open the retirement statement you have been stepping around, the one with his name in bold across the top. The account in his name is not only his account, at least not all of it. Contributions made between the wedding and the decree were acquired during the marriage, so the presumption of marital property reaches them no matter whose employer sponsors the plan. The balance that was already there on the wedding day starts on the other side of the line, and so does its growth, unless marital assets, including labor, contributed to that increase.
So can you, as a wife, take half of your husband’s retirement? Not automatically, and not the whole thing. The marital portion goes into the pot with the house and the savings, and the court divides the pot justly. Will you get half of his pension? Same answer.
The IRS says most plans require an ex-spouse to file a qualified domestic relations order with the plan administrator before the plan can pay any portion of the participant’s retirement plan benefits to that ex-spouse. Ask any lawyer you interview who drafts it, and when.
### What disqualifies you from alimony in Missouri?
Lay your last pay stub flat on the table and press the fold out with your thumb. That paper is half of this answer. Missouri doesn’t keep a list of disqualifications. It sets a door with two locks, and you have to open both. The court may grant you maintenance only if you lack sufficient property, including the marital property apportioned to you, to provide for your reasonable needs, and you are unable to support yourself through appropriate employment or are the custodian of a child whose condition or circumstances make it appropriate that the custodian not be required to work outside the home.
Fail either one and there is no maintenance. Enough property after the split, and the first lock holds. A steady paycheck that covers your reasonable needs, and the second does. So when people ask how hard it is to get alimony in Missouri, they are really asking about the property split.
Clear both, and the judge sets the amount and length after weighing the factors in the statute, among them the comparative earning capacity of each spouse, the standard of living during the marriage and the duration of the marriage. It’s the quiet arithmetic of a kitchen budget, the grocery receipts and the daycare bill and the car note, laid in front of a stranger in a robe.
And it ends. Under RSMo 452.370, unless the parties agreed otherwise in writing or the judgment says otherwise, the obligation to pay future maintenance ends on the death of either party or the remarriage of the spouse receiving it.
### What if you are going it alone, and what is due when?
The papers land heavy in your hand, and the clock starts that day. If you were the one served, your financial statements are due within 30 days of service or entry of appearance, whichever is earlier.
Going without a lawyer? The city court says anyone who plans to represent themselves in a divorce is required to complete Missouri’s Litigant Awareness Program. Start it tonight. The St. Louis Family Court is up on the ninth floor of the same building as the clerk, past the scanner.

### Frequently asked questions
### Q. How long does spousal maintenance last in Missouri?
A.  As long as the judgment says. A Missouri court can order maintenance with a termination date, and the order must state whether it is modifiable or nonmodifiable. Unless the parties agreed otherwise in writing or the judgment says otherwise, future maintenance ends on the death of either party or the remarriage of the spouse receiving it.
### Q. How hard is it to get alimony in Missouri?
A.  It takes opening two locks, and the first is the property split. The court may grant maintenance to either spouse only if the spouse seeking it lacks sufficient property, including marital property apportioned to them, to provide for their reasonable needs, and cannot support themselves through appropriate employment. Fail either one and there is no maintenance.
### Q. Can I stay in the house with my kids during a Missouri divorce?
A.  Not by default, but the court can allow it. One factor in RSMo 452.330 is the desirability of awarding the family home, or the right to live there for reasonable periods, to the spouse having custody of any children.
### Q. Who pays alimony in Missouri?
A.  Whichever spouse the court orders to. Missouri calls it maintenance, and the statute lets the court grant it to either spouse, but only to a spouse who lacks enough property to meet reasonable needs and cannot support themselves through appropriate employment.
### Q. What assets cannot be touched in divorce?
A.  In Missouri, you keep your nonmarital property. That covers property acquired by gift, bequest, devise or descent, property acquired in exchange for something owned before the marriage, and property excluded by a valid written agreement of the parties. Bring the paper that proves it, because property acquired during the marriage is presumed marital.

## Small Business Grants in Missouri: $416 Million Asked, $34 Million to Give
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/blog/small-business-grants-missouri-st-louis
$416 million. That is what eligible applicants asked for when the St. Louis Development Corporation ran its North St. Louis Small Business & Non-Profit Grant Program. The money on the table was $34,057,500. More than 700 applications came in, roughly twelve dollars requested for every dollar there was to give.
Behind plenty of them was a laptop open on a kitchen table after the second shift, the fan whirring, receipts fanned out next to a cold coffee ring, the same story typed into box after box until the words blur. More than $380 million of that asking could not be funded. That is not a verdict on anybody’s business. That is arithmetic.
Then the phone buzzes face-down at midnight: “You are eligible!” It promises federal startup money with your name on it. The SBA’s own grants page says it “does not provide grants for starting and expanding a business.”
### What grants are available for small businesses in Missouri?
Real Missouri grants exist, but each one pays for a single job behind its own fence: MO STEP funds qualifying international activities, the state’s Credential Training Program reimburses up to $2,000 per employee credential, federal SBIR and STTR awards fund research, and Arch Grants gives St. Louis startups $75,000 equity-free.
What fills your phone instead is the grant-scam trade and the myth it feeds on, that the SBA hands out startup money. That myth is somebody else’s business model. The “you qualify” text, the grant-finder subscription, the webinar with a countdown clock all live off it, and the fee is the small part of what they take. The big part is your time: the late nights, the dishwasher humming in a quiet house, spent chasing money that was never built for a cleaning business, a food truck or a barber chair.
Here is the St. Louis move almost nobody makes before they write a word. Visit the Transparency Portal linked from SLDC’s North St. Louis grant page. It includes portions of conditionally approved grant recipients’ applications and the scores those recipients earned. You can read what a winning answer looked like, line by line, from the people who actually won, instead of paying someone for a template.

### Where did all the St. Louis grant money go?
Most of the grant chatter you heard from neighbors in the last few years was real. It was also pandemic relief. The St. Louis Development Corporation’s Small Business Grant Fund was designed to assist small businesses hurt by the pandemic, and it gave 900 businesses across all 14 wards a $5,000 grant each, about $4.5 million in total. The city’s own page now says: “This program is complete.”
The North St. Louis program, the one with $416 Million+ requested, was funded with Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds. Same story, bigger check. When the relief dollars dried up, the headlines did not, and the scam texts learned to quote them.
So what are the odds of getting a small business grant? Odds like those make a grant a long shot worth one honest try, not a plan to run a business on. Missing out says nothing about your business.
### Who actually qualifies for the grants still open?
Arch Grants works out of 2315 Locust St. downtown, and its competition ends at a Finalist Pitch Day, founders on their feet pitching for a $75,000 grant. Every program still running has a fence around it. Learn the fence before you write a word.
The Startup Competition from Arch Grants awards $75,000 non-dilutive grants, plus $25,000 for companies relocating, in exchange for headquartering in the City of St. Louis for at least one year. Over 400 industry experts judge the applications, and 51% of the founding team, or one founder and 51% of the team, must live in St. Louis for the program year. One line of the fine print matters: at least one founder has to be working on the company as their primary or full-time professional role. For anyone building a business in the hours after a warehouse shift, that requirement rules this competition out for now.
MO STEP, run by the state’s Department of Economic Development, funds international trade activity for small businesses with 500 employees or fewer that have been in business in Missouri for at least a year and are operating profitably. For the current program cycle, the total program cost for the entire state is $313,333. The whole state. That is not a fund. That is a handful of trade-show booths.
SBIR and STTR are federal research money, built for companies with safety glasses pushed up on the forehead at a lab bench. A research team in Cortex fits that description. A bakery on Cherokee Street has other doors.
### Reimbursement means you pay first
One word changes the cash math: reimbursement. You spend the money, you keep the receipts, and the state pays you back if every form lines up.
MO STEP requires your full application no less than 15 business days before the trade activity, and approval has to come before the event. Afterward, all receipts go to DED within 90 days, along with a tax clearance letter from the Missouri Department of Revenue. Miss a document and the reimbursement can be delayed or cancelled. That means the plane ticket and the booth fee ride on your own card first, while the balance glows on your phone every time you open the banking app.
The Credential Training Program from Missouri One Start is a competitive grant for any employer registered to do business in Missouri, capped at $2,000 per employee and $30,000 per company each state fiscal year. Applications open for one month each quarter: January, April, July and October. The catch that stings a solo operator: a self-employed employer is prohibited from seeking funds for his or her own training. It pays for the people you hire, not the person in the mirror. If you are about to make that first hire, read what you owe when you hire your first employee in Missouri before you count on the credential money.

### How do you spot a grant scam before it costs you?
The scams sound warm. That is the trick. A text lands while you are wiping down the counter at close, the fryer still ticking as it cools, and it says “Great news! The tells settle it fast. The government does not charge a fee to apply for a federal grant. You cannot apply for federal grants over the phone or by email. And any federal grant you can spend any way you like is not a federal grant. The SBA adds another: SBA only communicates from email addresses ending in @sba.gov. If you already paid, report it to the FTC at 1-877-FTC-HELP.

### Frequently asked questions
### Q. Can an LLC get grant money?
A.  Yes, an LLC can get grant money when it meets a program’s fence. ### Q. How to get free grants for small business?
A.  Start from the purpose, not the money. Every federal grant involves an application through a government website such as Grants.gov, and the government does not charge a fee to apply for a federal grant.
### Q. What are the odds of getting a small business grant?
A.  Long. SLDC’s North St. Louis program had $34,057,500 to award against $416 Million+ requested by eligible applicants, roughly twelve dollars asked for every dollar available. Competitive programs score and rank applications, so even a strong one can lose on math alone.
### Q. Is it hard to get a grant?

### Q. Do you ever pay back a grant?

### Q. What not to say when applying for a grant?

### Q. What is the $10 000 SBA grant?
A.  It was the Targeted EIDL Advance, a pandemic payment of up to $10,000 for businesses in low-income communities that lost more than 30% of revenue and had 300 or fewer employees. It is closed. The SBA is no longer accepting new Advance applications, so anyone offering it today is not the SBA.

## Your 10 Days Started Before You Opened It: Missouri Unemployment Protest Period
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/blog/missouri-unemployment-protest-period
Ten calendar days. That is how long Missouri gives you to protest a former worker’s unemployment claim, and the count starts the day the state mails the notice, not the day you tear it open.
The envelope sits in the pile under the supplier invoices while the shift runs long. You find it at the kitchen table, boots still on, shoulders aching, thumb under the flap, and the mailing date printed inside is already a few squares back on the calendar. Nobody skipped anything. The paperwork clock simply started without you.
### How long is the Missouri unemployment protest period?
Ten calendar days, counted from the day the Division of Employment Security mailed the notice of claim to your last known address. Weekends count. Days you were closed count. Section 288.070 of the Missouri statutes puts it in plain words: a written protest within ten calendar days after the mailing of the notice.
That is the knot in your stomach. Now loosen it, in this order.
### Tonight, in four moves
First, take the paper calendar off the nail by the time clock, the one with the beer distributor’s logo, and grab a pen. Find the day the notice was mailed. Put the pen on the next square and count ten, every square on the page, the ones you were closed included. Circle where you land. Now look at where today is. The pen usually stops a lot closer than your stomach expected.
Second, stop letting the next clock start in a mailbox. UInteract, the Division of Employment Security’s employer system at labor.mo.gov/des/uinteract/employers, lists receiving Division correspondence electronically and protesting claim notices among its features, and its employer contact line is 573-751-1995. The same statute says the date the division transmits a notice electronically is treated as the mailing date, and it allows that delivery for any employer who requests it. The notice and the clock start on the same day, and you are looking at both.
Third, save two numbers in your phone, right where you are standing: the Division of Employment Security’s employer line, 573-751-1995, listed on its protest page, and the Department of Labor’s St. Louis line for claims information, 314-340-4950, on its contact page.
Fourth, deal with the empty shift, because that is what actually keeps you up. St. Louis has a stop for it. SLATE, the St. Louis Agency on Training and Employment, is the City of St. Louis government agency that offers businesses a variety of human resource assistance at no cost, including pre-screening candidates and on-site office space for interviews, at 1520 Market St., 3rd Floor. You can be across a table from your next hire while the protest is still pending.
### What a protest on time buys you
Inside those ten days you file a written protest, following the instructions printed on the notice, if you believe your former worker quit without good cause or was fired for misconduct. A protest on time is what makes you an interested party. The state’s own employer protest page puts the payoff plainly: if you submitted a timely protest, you get a copy of the deputy’s determination when a decision is made, and from there you can appeal it.
The stakes are Missouri’s own. A misconduct disqualification can be lifted only after the worker earns six times their weekly benefit amount in insured work, and a quit without good cause attributable to you or the work can run until other employment is secured and at least ten times that amount is earned.
### The clock starts before you open the envelope
The days you lost between the mailing and the kitchen table are not your mistake. The enemy here is a clock that starts before the paper does. That is how the rule is built. The law does not say ten days after you receive the notice; it says ten calendar days after the mailing. It is a deadline that assumes somebody opens the mail every morning, and on a two-truck crew working out of a garage, nobody does.
One Missouri wrinkle runs the other way. If you are a contributing employer and paid that worker gross wages of $400 or less during the base period, the state does not mail you a notice of the claim at all.
If you forward one line of this to another owner, make it this one: in Missouri, the ten days count from the day the state mails the notice, not the day you open it.
Already holding the paper one? Missouri also answers through SIDES E-Response. Have your federal and state employer identification numbers ready, plus the Access Code from the mailed notice of claim form. Once you log in to SIDES, the pending request shows the date and time your response is due to the state, and the site gives you a date-stamped confirmation of receipt. Screenshot it.
### What does a Missouri claims deputy need to see in your protest?
A protest is not a feeling. It is a stack of paper on a desk, and the person reading it, a claims deputy, never met your worker and never saw the schedule taped up by the back door. The deputy gets only what you send. A thin protest gets a thin result.
If you fired the person, the deputy wants the date and who did the firing, every incident of unsatisfactory conduct that played a part, the details of all warnings and reprimands, written or verbal, the details of the final incident, and the specific policy that was broken along with how the worker would have known about it. Attach a copy of that policy. Then read the sentence the state tucks into the middle of that list: policies prohibiting mistakes, accidents, poor workmanship or bad judgment may not provide a sufficient basis for protest. Being bad at a job is not the same thing as misconduct.
So what disqualifies a worker for unemployment in Missouri when you were the one who let them go? The legal word is misconduct, and the state’s definition is more specific than the word sounds. It includes a violation of your no-call, no-show policy, chronic absenteeism or tardiness in violation of a known policy, and two or more unapproved absences following a written reprimand or warning about an unapproved absence, unless the absences are protected by law. Known, written, policy. The warning form in the file drawer with their signature at the bottom is worth more than any story you tell on the phone.
If the worker quit, send what they said or did to show they were leaving. If they simply stopped showing up, say so and give the date they last worked. A timecard that ends on a Tuesday is evidence.
### Should you protest at all, or is that the expensive mistake?
Sometimes the honest answer is no. Under the heading Claimant Laid Off Due to Lack of Work, the state’s instruction is blunt: you should not protest a claim based on a separation for this reason. You can still tell the state about vacation, holiday or WARN pay going out, because those payments can affect the claim, and you should say so if the worker is not able or available for full-time work.
Why do owners fight at all? Because of how claiming unemployment affects an employer. According to the state’s page on laying off employees, benefits paid are charged to your account in ratio to the wages used to establish the claim, possibly resulting in an increased experience rate, and employers with reimbursable accounts get a direct charge.
But the same page carries the warning that should keep everybody honest. An employer who misrepresents or hides facts to deny benefits can face a penalty of 25 percent of the benefits denied on a first occurrence, rising to 100 percent for later ones, and can be found guilty of a misdemeanor. Protest what is true. Leave out what isn’t.
People are asking
### How much do you get on unemployment in Missouri?
Under Section 288.038 of the Missouri statutes, the weekly benefit is four percent of the worker’s wages in the average of their two highest base-period quarters, and it cannot go over $320 a week. The state’s page on laying off employees says twenty weeks of benefits is the maximum in a benefit year. For you as the employer, those are the weeks that get charged against your account when a quit or misconduct claim goes through unprotested.
### What happens if you miss the ten days?
The tight feeling in your chest when you find the envelope on day twelve is real, but it is not the end. The statute says the ten-day period may, for good cause, be extended. File it anyway, in writing, with the date it was mailed, the date it reached you and the date you opened it. I could not find the state’s list of what counts as good cause, so document everything.
### The phone hearing is the whole case
Say the deputy rules against you. You have 30 days from the date of the determination to appeal, and an appeal cannot be filed by email or phone. According to the Appeals Tribunal, most hearings take place over the phone, the hearing is de novo, meaning the referee hears the matter from the beginning, and you must present your evidence again even if you already gave it to the deputy. It may be your only chance to present evidence.
Forget the courtroom you are imagining. It is you, on speaker in the back office, the cooler humming behind you, your shift lead in the next chair because you have the right to present witnesses. The hearing is recorded. Have the warning forms, the policy, the timecards and a written timeline in front of you, in order, before the phone rings.

Write the mailing date on the envelope in marker and circle the tenth day on the wall calendar, the paper one you actually walk past. Then file the written protest the way the notice tells you to, keep a copy, and watch for the determination.
